| On CKS                                     | On Runpod                                                | Notes                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`                  | None                                                     | No Kubernetes API in the container.                                                 |
| Pod name from the Downward API             | `RUNPOD_POD_ID`                                          | Set on Pods.                                                                        |
| Zone or node labels from the Downward API  | `RUNPOD_DC_ID`                                           | Data center ID.                                                                     |
| `nvidia.com/gpu` count you passed yourself | `RUNPOD_GPU_COUNT`                                       | Set by Runpod.                                                                      |
| Service port from the manifest             | `PORT`, `PORT_HEALTH`                                    | Load-balancing workers. You set both.                                               |
| `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3=http://cwlota.com`    | Remove, or the Runpod S3-compatible endpoint             | Prefer reading the mounted path.                                                    |
| Secret mounted as a variable               | Variable set to `{{ RUNPOD_SECRET_name }}`               | Resolved when the Pod or worker starts.                                             |
| SUNK and Slurm variables                   | Unchanged, plus `PRIMARY_ADDR`, `NODE_RANK`, `NUM_NODES` | See [cluster configuration](https://docs.runpod.io/instant-clusters/configuration). |

### Status map

| Kubernetes                                   | Runpod Pod                                   | Runpod Serverless                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pod `Pending` (unschedulable, pulling image) | `PROVISIONING`, `STARTING`                   | Worker `INITIALIZING`, or `THROTTLED` while the host's GPUs are busy |
| Pod `Running` and ready                      | `RUNNING` with `runtimeStatus: running`      | Worker `RUNNING` or `IDLE`                                           |
| Pod `Running` but not ready                  | `RUNNING` with `runtimeStatus: initializing` | Worker `UNHEALTHY`, or health check returning `204`                  |
| Pod `Succeeded`                              | `EXITED`                                     | Job `COMPLETED`                                                      |
| Pod `Failed`, `CrashLoopBackOff`             | `ERROR`                                      | Job `FAILED` or `TIMED_OUT`                                          |
| Deleted                                      | `TERMINATED`                                 | Endpoint deleted                                                     |
| Job active                                   | Not applicable                               | Job `IN_QUEUE`, `IN_PROGRESS`                                        |

## Migrate with a coding agent

A coding agent with the Runpod skills and MCP server can run this migration with you: it reads your manifests, proposes a mapping, and creates the Runpod resources after you approve.

Install the tools for your agent:

```bash
# Claude Code (the plugin also connects the hosted MCP server)
claude plugin marketplace add runpod/runpod-plugins-official
claude plugin install runpod@runpod
```

```bash
# Any other agent (Codex, Cursor, and others): skills, then the hosted MCP server
npx skills add runpod/runpod-plugins-official --skill '*' --agent AGENT_ID --global
npx @runpod/mcp-server@latest add --client CLIENT_ID
```

The MCP server signs in with OAuth ("Sign in with Runpod"), so you don't need an API key to start. See [Agent skills](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/agent-skills) and [MCP servers](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/mcp-servers) for supported agents and options.

Then give the agent this prompt from the root of the repository that holds your manifests:

```text
Use the runpod-cloud-migrate skill to migrate this project from CoreWeave to Runpod.

1. Inventory first, and change nothing. Read every Kubernetes manifest, Helm values file,
   Terraform file, and CI script in this repo. If kubectl is configured for my CKS cluster,
   also run read-only commands (kubectl get nodepool, deploy, statefulset, job, cronjob, hpa,
   svc, ingress, pvc -A) to see what is running. List each workload with its image,
   command, env, ports, GPU count, instance type, volumes, and replica range.
2. For each workload, propose a Runpod target (Serverless load-balancing endpoint, Serverless
   queue endpoint, Pod, Instant Cluster, or SDK task) and say why. Flag anything with no
   direct equivalent: DaemonSets, operators, CRDs, sidecars, VPC rules, bucket policies.
3. Show me the plan as a table, with a GPU type per workload, the data to copy and where it
   lands, and a cost estimate from live Runpod pricing. Check GPU stock before proposing a
   type. Wait for my approval before creating anything billable.
4. Migrate one workload end to end: create the secret references, volume, and endpoint or
   Pod, copy only the data that workload needs, and verify with a real request from outside
   Runpod. Show me the response and the latency.
5. Update the client code and CI config for that workload, on a branch.
6. Never delete, scale down, or modify CoreWeave resources, and never print secret values.
   When I ask for the shutdown, list the exact commands and wait for my approval.
```

## Troubleshooting

**A load-balancing worker shows as running but requests time out.** The health check never returned `200`. Expose the server's port in `ports`, set both `PORT` and `PORT_HEALTH` to that port, and set `HEALTH_CHECK_PATH` if your server's health route isn't `/ping`. A readiness probe that pointed at a different port than the Service is the usual cause after a manifest translation.

**The model downloads again on every cold start.** The server is still writing to the PVC's old `mountPath`. On Serverless the volume is at `/runpod-volume`, so update the cache or download directory, or use [cached models](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/model-caching) for Hugging Face models.

**The image fails to pull.** Check two things: the image must be `linux/amd64`, and a private image needs a registry credential (`registry` or `--registry-auth-id`). `imagePullSecrets` and registries that were only reachable inside the CKS cluster don't carry over.

**Requests return `{"error":"not allowed for QB API"}`.** The URL style doesn't match the endpoint type. Load-balancing endpoints are called at `https://ENDPOINT_ID.api.runpod.ai/PATH`, and queue-based endpoints at `https://api.runpod.ai/v2/ENDPOINT_ID/run`. The type is fixed at creation, so recreate the endpoint if it's the wrong one.

**Requests through a Pod's proxy URL fail after about 100 seconds.** That's the proxy timeout. Stream the response, move the workload to a Serverless endpoint, or expose a TCP port and connect to the Pod's public IP and mapped port.

**The app can't reach another service by its Kubernetes name.** Names like `redis.default.svc.cluster.local` don't exist on Runpod. Use the other service's endpoint URL, or enable global networking on both Pods and use `POD_ID.runpod.internal`. Code that loads in-cluster Kubernetes credentials needs to be rewritten against the Runpod API.

**The Pod or endpoint can't find capacity.** A network volume pins everything that mounts it to one data center, and a CUDA floor narrows the machines further. List more than one pool in `gpu.pools`, attach a network volume per data center, or pick another GPU type that fits the workload.

**`aws s3` commands fail against the Runpod S3-compatible API.** Pass `--region` with the data center ID and `--endpoint-url` with that data center's URL, and use the Runpod S3 API key, not your Runpod API key. Keep the Runpod settings in a separate AWS CLI profile from the `cw` profile, because the `cw` profile sets CoreWeave's endpoint and addressing style.

**`/status` returns 404 for a job that finished.** Results of `/run` jobs are kept for 30 minutes, and jobs are removed when their TTL expires. Have the handler write outputs to a volume or object store, or pass a `webhook`.

**Slurm doesn't start on a new cluster.** Managed Slurm Clusters support only official Runpod PyTorch images. Recreate the cluster with one, or follow the [unmanaged Slurm guide](https://docs.runpod.io/instant-clusters/slurm) for a custom image.

If something in this guide is wrong or missing, open an issue on the [Runpod docs repository](https://github.com/runpod/docs/issues).

# Document: Migrate from Paperspace and DigitalOcean GPU to Runpod

Source path: migrate/paperspace.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/migrate/paperspace.mdx
Canonical documentation: https://docs.runpod.io/migrate/paperspace
Description: Move Paperspace Machines, Notebooks, Deployments, and Workflows, and DigitalOcean GPU Droplets and Inference, to Runpod.

# Migrate from Paperspace and DigitalOcean GPU to Runpod

Move Paperspace Machines, Notebooks, Deployments, and Workflows, and DigitalOcean GPU Droplets and Inference, to Runpod.

This guide is for teams that run GPU workloads on [Paperspace](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/paperspace/) or on DigitalOcean's own GPU products and want to run them on Runpod. Paperspace [Machines](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/paperspace/machines/) and DigitalOcean [GPU Droplets](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/gpu-droplets/) map to [Pods](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/overview), [Notebooks](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/paperspace/notebooks/) map to Pods with JupyterLab, [Deployments](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/paperspace/deployments/) map to [Serverless](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/overview) endpoints, [Workflows](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/paperspace/workflows/) map to the Runpod SDK or Serverless queue endpoints, and DigitalOcean [Inference](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/inference/) maps to [Public Endpoints](https://docs.runpod.io/public-endpoints/overview) or a Serverless vLLM endpoint. By the end you'll have each workload running on Runpod, your data on Runpod storage, your clients and automation pointed at Runpod, and the old resources shut down.

> **Tip**
>
> You can hand most of this migration to a coding agent. See [Migrate with a coding agent](#migrate-with-a-coding-agent).

> **Note**
>
> **Product names, checked against DigitalOcean's docs on 2026-11-14.** Paperspace is part of DigitalOcean and still offers Notebooks, Deployments, Workflows, and Machines through the Paperspace console. "Gradient" still names those Paperspace products and their subscription plans. DigitalOcean's own AI products are GPU Droplets, Bare Metal GPUs, and Inference (serverless inference, dedicated inference, and Agent Platform). DigitalOcean's docs list no retirement date for the four Paperspace products. They do state that the legacy Gradient and Core API endpoints are no longer available (so the `gradient` CLI no longer works), that Windows templates are unavailable to users who joined after July 1, 2024, and that NVIDIA GRID machines are retired.

## How Paperspace and DigitalOcean map to Runpod

| Paperspace or DigitalOcean concept                                                     | Runpod equivalent                                                                                                                                              | Notes                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Paperspace Machine (Linux VM)                                                          | [Pod](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/overview)                                                                                                                    | A Pod is a container, not a VM. You bring a Docker image instead of an OS template.                                         |
| DigitalOcean GPU Droplet (VM)                                                          | [Pod](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/overview)                                                                                                                    | Same shift from VM to container. 8-GPU plans map to a Pod with a GPU count of 8, subject to stock.                          |
| Paperspace Machine (Windows), desktop streaming                                        | None                                                                                                                                                           | Pods run Linux containers. See [What has no direct equivalent](#what-has-no-direct-equivalent).                             |
| Paperspace Notebook                                                                    | Pod from the official PyTorch template                                                                                                                         | JupyterLab on port 8888. Persistent files live in `/workspace`.                                                             |
| Paperspace Deployment (container, replicas, endpoint URL)                              | [Load-balancing endpoint](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/load-balancing/overview) or [queue-based endpoint](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/overview)     | Load balancing keeps your HTTP server as is. Queue-based needs a handler function.                                          |
| Paperspace Workflow (YAML jobs on Argo)                                                | Runpod SDK [`@app.task`](https://docs.runpod.io/sdk/overview) or a queue-based endpoint                                                                        | Runpod has no YAML pipeline engine. You express job order in Python or in your CI system.                                   |
| DigitalOcean serverless inference                                                      | [Public Endpoints](https://docs.runpod.io/public-endpoints/overview) or [Serverless vLLM](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/vllm/overview)                     | Both expose an OpenAI-compatible route. The model catalog differs.                                                          |
| DigitalOcean dedicated inference, 1-Click Models                                       | [Serverless vLLM](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/vllm/overview) or a Pod                                                                                    | You pick the Hugging Face model and the GPU.                                                                                |
| DigitalOcean Bare Metal GPUs, multi-node contract GPU Droplets                         | [Instant Clusters](https://docs.runpod.io/instant-clusters)                                                                                                    | Multi-node clusters for Slurm, PyTorch, and Ray.                                                                            |
| DOKS GPU node pools                                                                    | Serverless, Pods, or Instant Clusters                                                                                                                          | Runpod exposes no Kubernetes API. See [What has no direct equivalent](#what-has-no-direct-equivalent).                      |
| OS templates, custom templates, snapshots, Droplet images                              | Docker image plus a [template](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/templates/overview)                                                                                 | A template stores the image, ports, env, and disk sizes.                                                                    |
| Notebook container, Deployment `image`                                                 | Docker image                                                                                                                                                   | Images must be `linux/amd64`.                                                                                               |
| Machine block storage, Droplet boot disk                                               | Volume disk at `/workspace` or a [network volume](https://docs.runpod.io/storage/network-volumes)                                                              | Only the mounted path persists. The rest of the container filesystem resets when the Pod stops.                             |
| Droplet scratch disk                                                                   | Container disk                                                                                                                                                 | Both are temporary.                                                                                                         |
| Paperspace shared drive, Notebook `/storage`, DigitalOcean Network File Storage        | [Network volume](https://docs.runpod.io/storage/network-volumes)                                                                                               | Shared by Pods and Serverless workers in one data center.                                                                   |
| DigitalOcean Volumes (block storage)                                                   | [Network volume](https://docs.runpod.io/storage/network-volumes)                                                                                               | A file system mount, not a raw block device.                                                                                |
| Paperspace datasets (versioned), DigitalOcean Spaces                                   | Network volume with the [S3-compatible API](https://docs.runpod.io/storage/s3-api), or a [global volume](https://docs.runpod.io/storage/globalvolume/overview) | Runpod has no dataset versioning or bucket service. You can also keep reading from Spaces.                                  |
| Public IP (static or dynamic), Droplet public IPv4                                     | HTTP proxy URL or a mapped TCP port                                                                                                                            | Runpod assigns the public IP and external port. See [Expose ports](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/configuration/expose-ports). |
| Paperspace private network, DigitalOcean VPC                                           | [Global networking](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/networking)                                                                                                    | Private Pod-to-Pod DNS at `POD_ID.runpod.internal`. NVIDIA GPU Pods in supported data centers only.                         |
| Paperspace secrets (`secret:NAME`)                                                     | [Secrets](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/templates/secrets)                                                                                                       | Referenced as `{{ RUNPOD_SECRET_name }}` in environment variables.                                                          |
| Paperspace regions (NY2, CA1, AMS1), DigitalOcean regions                              | Data centers                                                                                                                                                   | List them with `runpodctl datacenter list`.                                                                                 |
| Paperspace hourly billing                                                              | Per-second billing                                                                                                                                             | Pods bill per second for compute and storage. Serverless bills per second while workers run.                                |
| DigitalOcean GPU Droplet per-second billing                                            | Per-second billing                                                                                                                                             | A stopped Pod stops compute billing and keeps billing its volume disk.                                                      |
| Spot GPU Droplets, contract GPU Droplets                                               | On-demand Pods                                                                                                                                                 | `runpodctl`, REST API v2, and the Terraform provider create on-demand Pods.                                                 |
| `digitalocean` Terraform provider                                                      | [Runpod Terraform provider](https://docs.runpod.io/integrations/terraform/overview)                                                                            | See [Migrate your Terraform](#migrate-your-terraform).                                                                      |
| `pspace` CLI, `doctl`                                                                  | [`runpodctl`](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/overview)                                                                                                       | See the [CLI command map](#cli-command-map).                                                                                |
| Paperspace API (`api.paperspace.com/v1`), DigitalOcean API (`api.digitalocean.com/v2`) | [REST API v2](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/overview) (`api.runpod.io/v2`)                                                                           | See the [API map](#api-map).                                                                                                |
| PyDo, Godo, DoTs                                                                       | Runpod SDK (`pip install runpod`)                                                                                                                              | Includes the `rp` CLI and `runpod.Endpoint`.                                                                                |
| Paperspace API key, DigitalOcean personal access token, model access key               | One [Runpod API key](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/credentials)                                                                                           | Sent as `Authorization: Bearer`.                                                                                            |
| Paperspace teams and projects, DigitalOcean teams and projects                         | [Organizations](https://docs.runpod.io/organizations/orgs-overview), [cost centers](https://docs.runpod.io/accounts-billing/cost-centers)                      | Roles and groups live on the organization.                                                                                  |
| Deployment logs and metrics, DigitalOcean Monitoring                                   | [Serverless logs](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/development/logs), `runpodctl pod logs`, REST v2 metrics routes                                            | Endpoint metrics are at `/v2/serverless/ENDPOINT_ID/metrics/requests`.                                                      |

## What's different

### What works differently

**VMs become containers.** A Paperspace Machine or a GPU Droplet is a virtual machine: you pick an OS image, get a boot disk that persists everything, and can install drivers, run `systemd` services, or run Docker yourself. A Pod is a single container that Runpod starts from your Docker image, with the GPU drivers provided by the host. Anything you installed by hand on the VM has to move into a Dockerfile. Runpod runs Docker for you, so you can't start your own Docker daemon or use Docker Compose inside a Pod.

**Only `/workspace` persists.** On a VM the whole boot disk survives a shutdown. On a Pod, the container disk resets when the Pod stops, the volume disk at `/workspace` survives a stop and is deleted with the Pod, and a network volume outlives the Pod. Keep code, data, and checkpoints under the mounted path, and install system packages in the image.

**Stopping and billing.** Paperspace bills machine compute only while the machine is powered on, and keeps billing storage and public IPs. DigitalOcean keeps billing a powered-off GPU Droplet until you destroy it. A stopped Pod stops billing compute and keeps billing its volume disk. A Serverless endpoint with zero active workers bills only while workers run. See [Pod pricing](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/pricing) and [Serverless pricing](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/pricing).

**Public access.** A Machine or Droplet gets a public IP address where every port you open is reachable. A Pod exposes only the ports you list. HTTP ports get a URL of the form `https://POD_ID-PORT.proxy.runpod.net`, which is public, has no built-in authentication, and closes connections after 100 seconds. TCP ports (such as SSH) get a public IP and a mapped external port that Runpod assigns. Pods support TCP and HTTP, not UDP.

**Deployment endpoints.** A Paperspace Deployment serves your container at a `paperspacegradient.com` URL, optionally protected with basic authentication (username `paperspace`). A Runpod load-balancing endpoint serves your container at `https://ENDPOINT_ID.api.runpod.ai` and always requires `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`. A queue-based endpoint uses a different contract: you write a handler function and clients call `/run` or `/runsync` with an `{"input": {...}}` body.

**Autoscaling signals.** Paperspace Deployments scale between `replicas` and `maxReplicas` on CPU, memory, or request duration, using the Kubernetes horizontal pod autoscaler. Runpod endpoints scale between a minimum and maximum worker count on request count (load balancing and queue-based) or queue delay (queue-based only). The minimum is 0 by default, so an endpoint scales to zero and the first request after idle pays a cold start.

**Health checks.** Paperspace supports `liveness`, `readiness`, and `startup` probes with any 2xx or 3xx code as success. A load-balancing worker has one health path (`/ping` by default, configurable with `HEALTH_CHECK_PATH`) where `200` means healthy, `204` means initializing, and anything else means unhealthy.

**Model APIs.** DigitalOcean serverless inference authenticates with a model access key against `https://inference.do-ai.run/v1` and includes commercial third-party models. Runpod Public Endpoints and vLLM endpoints authenticate with your Runpod API key and include the endpoint or model slug in the base URL.

**One credential.** Paperspace and DigitalOcean use separate credentials (a Paperspace API key, a DigitalOcean personal access token, model access keys, and Spaces keys). Runpod uses one API key for the CLI, REST API, SDK, and endpoint requests, plus a separate S3 API key for the S3-compatible API.

### What has no direct equivalent

**On Runpod:**

- **Windows machines and desktop streaming.** Pods run Linux containers. Keep Windows workloads where they are, or port them to Linux. For interactive work, use JupyterLab, SSH, or [an IDE connection](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/configuration/connect-to-ide).
- **A Kubernetes API.** DOKS GPU node pools have no Runpod counterpart you can point `kubectl` at. Move each workload to the product that fits its shape: a Deployment with a Service to a Serverless endpoint, a Job to `@app.task` or a queue-based endpoint, a StatefulSet or long-lived process to a Pod, and tightly coupled multi-node training to an [Instant Cluster](https://docs.runpod.io/instant-clusters). To keep a cluster-style scheduler, use the [SkyPilot](https://docs.runpod.io/integrations/skypilot) or [dstack](https://docs.runpod.io/integrations/dstack) integration.
- **VM snapshots and custom OS templates.** Rebuild the environment as a Docker image and store its settings in a template.
- **A workflow engine.** Gradient Workflows runs YAML job graphs with typed inputs and outputs. On Runpod, job order lives in Python (the SDK) or in your CI system.
- **Versioned datasets.** Paperspace datasets have immutable versions and tags. On a network volume, use versioned directory names, or keep datasets in an object store that supports versioning.
- **Object storage buckets with a CDN.** The S3-compatible API reads and writes files on a network volume. It isn't a bucket service with public URLs or a CDN. Keep Spaces for public assets.
- **Managed agents, knowledge bases, and commercial model routing.** Agent Platform, Knowledge Bases, the Inference Router, and third-party commercial models stay on DigitalOcean or move to another provider.
- **Raw block devices.** Network volumes mount as a file system. You can't partition or format them.
- **Multiple probe types.** Fold readiness and startup logic into the single health path.

**On the Paperspace and DigitalOcean GPU products this guide covers:**

- **Scale to zero for your own containers.** Paperspace `replicas` is the floor for a running Deployment, and you stop it by setting `enabled: false`.
- **A managed request queue.** Queue-based endpoints give you async jobs, status polling, streaming, retries, and webhooks without running a queue yourself.
- **Storage that isn't tied to a region.** A [global volume](https://docs.runpod.io/storage/globalvolume/overview) (beta) mounts in any data center.
- **Ephemeral compute per function call.** `@app.task` provisions a Pod per call and terminates it when the function returns.

## Requirements

- A [Runpod account](https://docs.runpod.io/accounts-billing/manage-accounts) with credits, and a [Runpod API key](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/credentials).
- Access to your Paperspace team (a Paperspace API key for `pspace`) or your DigitalOcean team (a personal access token for `doctl`), or both.
- Docker on your machine, and a container registry you can push to (Docker Hub, GHCR, or DigitalOcean Container Registry).
- An SSH key pair for Pod access and file transfer.
- For Terraform users: Terraform 1.6 or later.

## Step 1: Take inventory of what you run on Paperspace and DigitalOcean

List every resource, record its configuration, and find the code that calls either platform. Use the names from each product's API, because you'll map them field by field in later steps.

### Paperspace

Install `pspace` and log in with a Paperspace API key, then list the resources it manages. The `--json` flag is available on every command.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://paperspace.com/install.sh | sh
pspace login

pspace machine list --json > paperspace-machines.json
pspace deployment list --json > paperspace-deployments.json
pspace project list --json > paperspace-projects.json
pspace shared-drive list --json > paperspace-shared-drives.json
pspace snapshot list --json > paperspace-snapshots.json
pspace template list --json > paperspace-templates.json
pspace startup-script list --json > paperspace-startup-scripts.json
pspace public-ip list --json > paperspace-public-ips.json
pspace secret list --global --json > paperspace-team-secrets.json
```

For each machine, record `machineType`, `region`, `diskSize`, `templateId`, `publicIpType`, `networkId`, `startupScriptId`, and the auto-shutdown settings. Secret values aren't needed yet, only the names.

Export the full configuration of each Deployment. The response includes the spec (image, port, env, command, instance type, replicas, autoscaling, health checks, and integrations) and the endpoint URL.

```bash
pspace deployment get DEPLOYMENT_ID --json > deployment-DEPLOYMENT_ID.json
```

The same data is available from the Paperspace API at `https://api.paperspace.com/v1`, for example `GET /deployments`, `GET /machines`, `GET /shared-drives`, and `GET /datasets`, with an `Authorization: Bearer` header.

`pspace` has no commands for Notebooks, Workflows, or datasets. For those, use the Paperspace console:

- **Notebooks:** For each Notebook, record the container image, the workspace repository URL, the machine type, and what you keep in `/notebooks`, `/storage`, and `/datasets`.
- **Workflows:** Workflow specs live in your repository under `.gradient/workflows`. Record each job's `instance-type`, image, `inputs`, `outputs`, `env`, and `needs`.
- **Datasets and models:** Record each dataset ID and its storage provider (Gradient-managed or your own S3-compatible bucket).

### DigitalOcean

Install `doctl`, authenticate with a personal access token, and list GPU resources. `doctl compute droplet list` returns only non-GPU Droplets unless you pass `--gpus`.

```bash
doctl auth init

doctl compute droplet list --gpus --output json > do-gpu-droplets.json
doctl compute volume list --output json > do-volumes.json
doctl compute snapshot list --output json > do-snapshots.json
doctl kubernetes cluster list --output json > do-doks-clusters.json
doctl kubernetes cluster node-pool list CLUSTER_ID --output json > do-node-pools.json
```

For each GPU Droplet, record the size slug (for example `gpu-h100x1-80gb`), the image slug (`gpu-h100x1-base`, `gpu-h100x8-base`, `gpu-amd-base`, a 1-Click Model, or your own snapshot), region, attached volume IDs, VPC, tags, and the user data script. For DOKS, record which node pools use `gpu-` size slugs and which workloads schedule onto them.

List dedicated inference deployments with the DigitalOcean API:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/dedicated-inferences"
```

For serverless inference, list your model access keys in the DigitalOcean Control Panel and note which model IDs your applications request. For Spaces, list buckets with any S3 client pointed at your region's endpoint, for example `aws s3 ls --endpoint-url https://nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com`.

### Find code that calls either platform

Search your repositories for CLI invocations, hostnames, credentials, and Terraform resources:

```bash
grep -rnE \
  "pspace |gradient (deployments|workflows|notebooks|datasets)|api\.paperspace\.com|paperspacegradient\.com|PAPERSPACE_API_KEY|\.gradient/workflows|doctl |api\.digitalocean\.com|digitaloceanspaces\.com|inference\.do-ai\.run|dedicated-inference\.do-infra\.ai|DIGITALOCEAN_(ACCESS_)?TOKEN|MODEL_ACCESS_KEY|from pydo|digitalocean/godo|digitalocean_(droplet|volume|volume_attachment|spaces_bucket|kubernetes_cluster|kubernetes_node_pool)|paperspace_(machine|script|network|autoscaling_group)" \
  --include="*.py" --include="*.ts" --include="*.js" --include="*.go" --include="*.sh" \
  --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" --include="*.json" --include="*.toml" --include="*.tf" \
  --include="Dockerfile*" --include="Makefile" .
```

Also check for hardcoded paths that only exist on the old platform: `/notebooks`, `/storage`, `/datasets`, `/inputs`, `/outputs`, `/home/paperspace`, and Droplet volume mount points under `/mnt`.

## Step 2: Set up Runpod

Create a [Runpod account](https://www.console.runpod.io), add credits, and create an [API key](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/credentials). Then install the tools you'll use.

Install `runpodctl` and configure it. `runpodctl doctor` sets your API key and an SSH key in one pass.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://cli.runpod.net | sudo bash
runpodctl doctor
```

On macOS you can use `brew install runpod/runpodctl/runpodctl` instead.

Install the Runpod SDK if you'll migrate Workflows, write Serverless handlers, or call endpoints from Python. It requires Python 3.10 to 3.14 and includes the `rp` CLI.

```bash
pip install runpod
rp login
export RUNPOD_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
```

`rp login` stores your key in `~/.runpod/config.toml`. The `RUNPOD_API_KEY` variable is what the REST examples and the Terraform provider in this guide read.

To let a coding agent manage Runpod for you, connect the [Runpod MCP server](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/mcp-servers). For infrastructure as code, install the [Terraform provider](https://docs.runpod.io/integrations/terraform/overview).

## Step 3: Choose where each workload lands

Pick a target for each item in your inventory by its shape, not by the product it runs on today.

| Workload on Paperspace or DigitalOcean                                   | Runpod target                                                                                                       | Why                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Machine or GPU Droplet you SSH into for development or training          | [Pod](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/overview)                                                                         | Long-lived, interactive, SSH and ports.                               |
| Notebook                                                                 | Pod from the official PyTorch template                                                                              | JupyterLab with `/workspace` persistence.                             |
| Machine or Droplet that hosts a web UI or API all day                    | Pod, or a [load-balancing endpoint](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/load-balancing/overview) if traffic is bursty | A Pod is always on. An endpoint scales with traffic.                  |
| Deployment serving HTTP (FastAPI, Flask, TGI, vLLM)                      | [Load-balancing endpoint](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/load-balancing/overview)                                | Keeps your HTTP paths. Requests are limited to 5.5 minutes and 30 MB. |
| Deployment with long or bursty requests, or batch inference              | [Queue-based endpoint](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/overview)                                                  | Queues requests, retries, and supports async jobs and webhooks.       |
| Workflow job (train, evaluate, export)                                   | [`@app.task`](https://docs.runpod.io/sdk/overview)                                                                  | One Pod per call, terminated on return.                               |
| Workflow that fans out many short jobs                                   | Queue-based endpoint (`@app.queue`)                                                                                 | Autoscaling workers pull from a queue.                                |
| Serverless inference with an open model that Runpod hosts                | [Public Endpoint](https://docs.runpod.io/public-endpoints/overview)                                                 | Nothing to deploy.                                                    |
| Serverless or dedicated inference with another open model, 1-Click Model | [Serverless vLLM](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/vllm/get-started)                                               | OpenAI-compatible, your choice of Hugging Face model.                 |
| DOKS GPU workload                                                        | Serverless endpoint, Pod, or `@app.task` by shape                                                                   | See [What has no direct equivalent](#what-has-no-direct-equivalent).  |
| Bare Metal GPUs, multi-node training                                     | [Instant Cluster](https://docs.runpod.io/instant-clusters)                                                          | Multi-node with Slurm, PyTorch, or Ray.                               |
| Windows machine                                                          | Stays where it is                                                                                                   | Pods are Linux containers.                                            |

### Map your GPUs

Choose a GPU by what the workload needs (VRAM first, then generation), then confirm stock. The Runpod IDs below come from the [GPU types reference](https://docs.runpod.io/references/gpu-types). Pods take a GPU type ID. Serverless endpoints take a GPU pool ID.

| H100                         | 80 GB | `NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3` or `NVIDIA H100 PCIe`              | `ADA_80_PRO`    |

| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------- | ----------------- |
