| Change scaling       | `baseten model deployment update-autoscaling` | `runpodctl serverless update ENDPOINT_ID --workers-min N --workers-max N --idle-timeout N`                                  |
| Read logs            | `baseten model deployment logs --tail`        | Console **Logs** tab, or `GET /v2/serverless/ENDPOINT_ID/workers/WORKER_ID/logs`                                            |
| Set a secret         | `baseten org secret set`                      | `rp secret add NAME`, or `POST /v2/account/secrets`                                                                         |

Updating the image creates a release, and workers move to it as a [rolling release](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/rolling-releases). To roll a new image, patch the endpoint itself:

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://api.runpod.io/v2/serverless/ENDPOINT_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RUNPOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"image": "docker.io/DOCKER_USERNAME/text-generator:v1.1.0"}'
```

The full maps are in the [Reference](#reference) section.

## Step 8: Verify, cut over, and shut down

1. Call the new endpoint from a machine outside Runpod and check the job status and output.

   ```bash
   curl -X POST https://api.runpod.ai/v2/ENDPOINT_ID/runsync \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $RUNPOD_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"input": {"prompt": "Hello, world!"}}'

   curl https://api.runpod.ai/v2/ENDPOINT_ID/health \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $RUNPOD_API_KEY"
   ```

   The first request after a deploy includes a cold start. Send a second one to see warm latency.
2. Replay a fixed set of production inputs against both platforms with the same seed and sampling settings, and diff the outputs. In the Runpod job object, `delayTime` is queue plus cold start time and `executionTime` is handler time, both in milliseconds. Compare `executionTime` with your Baseten inference latency, and tune active workers and idle timeout against `delayTime`.
3. Keep the Baseten deployment active and send a small share of traffic to Runpod from your client or gateway. Raise max workers before each increase. Watch the endpoint's **Metrics** tab for delay time, cold starts, and failed requests.
4. Max workers caps how far an endpoint scales, and the execution timeout stops runaway jobs. Keep active workers at 0 unless you need warm capacity. Check spend with `runpodctl billing --help` or the REST v2 `/v2/billing/serverless` route.
5. When traffic has been at zero for long enough to trust it, deactivate first (reversible), then delete.

   ```bash
   # Stop compute spend but keep the deployment
   baseten model deployment deactivate --model-id MODEL_ID --deployment-id DEPLOYMENT_ID --yes

   # Stop any running training jobs
   baseten train job list --status running
   baseten train job stop --job-id JOB_ID --yes

   # Later: delete models, Chains, and BDN volumes
   baseten model delete --model-id MODEL_ID --yes
   curl -X DELETE https://api.baseten.co/v1/chains/CHAIN_ID \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $BASETEN_API_KEY"
   baseten volume rm --recursive --yes bdn:NAMESPACE/VOLUME

   # Confirm nothing is still accruing
   baseten org billing usage
   ```

   Deleting a model or volume can't be undone. Deactivate instead of only scaling to zero, because a scaled-to-zero deployment stays live and any stray request starts a replica. Finally, delete the Baseten API keys your services used (`baseten org api-key list`) and remove `BASETEN_API_KEY` from your secret stores.

## Migrate your Terraform

Baseten publishes the `basetenlabs/baseten` provider with a `baseten_model` resource (which can push a Truss directory and manage environment autoscaling) and a `baseten_secret` resource. The Runpod provider, `runpod/runpod` at `~> 2.0`, is built on REST API v2.

| Baseten                                                    | Runpod                                                                        | Notes                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `baseten_model` with `push`                                | `runpod_serverless_endpoint` with `image`                                     | The Runpod provider deploys an image you already built. Build and push in CI before `terraform apply`.                        |
| `baseten_model.environments.NAME.autoscaling`              | `workers_min`, `workers_max`, `idle_timeout`, `scaling_type`, `scaling_value` | One `runpod_serverless_endpoint` per environment.                                                                             |
| `baseten_model.environments.NAME.promotion.rolling_deploy` | No arguments                                                                  | Rolling releases run on every image change.                                                                                   |
| `baseten_secret`                                           | No secret resource                                                            | Create the secret in the console or with `POST /v2/account/secrets`, and reference it in `env` as `{{ RUNPOD_SECRET_name }}`. |
| Registry auth in `config.yaml`                             | `runpod_registry`, referenced by `registry`                                   |                                                                                                                               |
| BDN volume                                                 | `runpod_network_volume`                                                       |                                                                                                                               |

```hcl Baseten
terraform {
  required_providers {
    baseten = {
      source  = "basetenlabs/baseten"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "baseten" {}

resource "baseten_model" "text_generator" {
  name = "text-generator"

  push = {
    config_dir  = "${path.module}/text-generator"
    environment = "production"
    wait        = true
  }

  environments = {
    production = {
      autoscaling = {
        min_replica      = 0
        max_replica      = 3
        scale_down_delay = 300
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```hcl Runpod
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.6"
  required_providers {
    runpod = {
      source  = "runpod/runpod"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "runpod" {}

resource "runpod_serverless_endpoint" "text_generator" {
  name          = "text-generator"
  image         = "docker.io/DOCKER_USERNAME/text-generator:v1.0.0"
  endpoint_type = "QUEUE"

  gpu_pools        = ["AMPERE_24"]
  gpu_count        = 1
  min_cuda_version = "12.8"
  disk             = 20

  workers_min   = 0
  workers_max   = 3
  idle_timeout  = 300
  scaling_type  = "QUEUE_DELAY"
  scaling_value = 4
  flashboot     = "FLASHBOOT"
  timeout       = 600000

  env = {
    MODEL_ID = "HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct"
    HF_TOKEN = "{{ RUNPOD_SECRET_hf_access_token }}"
  }
}

output "run_url" {
  value = runpod_serverless_endpoint.text_generator.request_urls.run
}
```

Both providers read the API key from the environment (`BASETEN_API_KEY` and `RUNPOD_API_KEY`). A new image tag in `image` rolls the endpoint. `timeout` is in milliseconds and `idle_timeout` in seconds. For every argument, see the [provider reference](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/runpod/runpod/latest/docs).

| Baseten                                                                      | Runpod                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `POST https://model-MODEL_ID.api.baseten.co/environments/production/predict` | `POST https://api.runpod.ai/v2/ENDPOINT_ID/runsync`            |

| `.../environments/production/sync/PATH` (custom server routes)               | `https://ENDPOINT_ID.api.runpod.ai/PATH` (load balancing)      |
| `.../environments/production/sync/v1` (OpenAI base URL)                      | `https://api.runpod.ai/v2/ENDPOINT_ID/openai/v1` (vLLM worker) |
| `https://inference.baseten.co/v1` (Model APIs)                               | `https://api.runpod.ai/v2/PUBLIC_ENDPOINT_ID/openai/v1`        |
| `https://chain-CHAIN_ID.api.baseten.co/production/run_remote`                | `/runsync` on your orchestrator endpoint                       |
| Wake endpoint                                                                | No equivalent call. A request starts a worker.                 |
| `GET https://api.baseten.co/v1/models`                                       | `GET https://api.runpod.io/v2/serverless`                      |
| `PATCH /v1/models/MODEL_ID/deployments/DEPLOYMENT_ID/autoscaling_settings`   | `PATCH /v2/serverless/ENDPOINT_ID` (`workers`, `scaling`)      |
| `POST /v1/models/MODEL_ID/deployments/DEPLOYMENT_ID/promote`                 | `PATCH /v2/serverless/ENDPOINT_ID` (`image`)                   |
| `POST /v1/models/MODEL_ID/deployments/DEPLOYMENT_ID/deactivate`              | `PATCH /v2/serverless/ENDPOINT_ID` (`workers.max` set to 0)    |
| `DELETE /v1/models/MODEL_ID`                                                 | `DELETE /v2/serverless/ENDPOINT_ID`                            |
| `POST /v1/secrets`                                                           | `POST /v2/account/secrets`                                     |
| `GET /v1/instance_types`                                                     | `GET /v2/catalog/gpus`, `GET /v2/catalog/cpus`                 |

### Request and response field map

| Baseten                           | Runpod                                 |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Request body is the model input   | `{"input": MODEL_INPUT}`               |
| `model_input` (async)             | `input`                                |
| `webhook_endpoint`                | `webhook`                              |
| `max_time_in_queue_seconds`       | `policy.ttl` (ms, queue plus run time) |
| `priority`                        | `policy.lowPriority`                   |
| Response body is the model output | `output` inside the job object         |
| `request_id`                      | `id`                                   |
| Webhook `data`                    | Webhook `output`                       |
| `X-Baseten-Request-Id` header     | `job["id"]` in the handler             |

### Environment variable map

| Inside a Baseten container                                   | Inside a Runpod worker                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `BT_MODEL_ID`                                                | `RUNPOD_ENDPOINT_ID`                                                                         |
| `BT_MODEL_DEPLOYMENT_ID`                                     | No equivalent. Put the version in your image tag or an env var.                              |
| Replica identity                                             | `RUNPOD_POD_ID` (the worker ID)                                                              |
| `kwargs["secrets"]["NAME"]`, `/secrets/NAME`                 | An env var set to `{{ RUNPOD_SECRET_NAME }}`                                                 |
| `kwargs["environment"]["name"]`                              | An env var you set per endpoint                                                              |
| `kwargs["data_dir"]` (`/app/data`)                           | A path you `COPY` to in the image                                                            |
| `/app/model_cache/VOLUME_FOLDER`, `weights` `mount_location` | `/runpod-volume/huggingface-cache/hub/` (cached models) or `/runpod-volume` (network volume) |
| `PORT` (always `8080`)                                       | `PORT`, `PORT_HEALTH` on load balancing endpoints (default `80`)                             |

### Status map

| Baseten async request | Runpod job                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `QUEUED`              | `IN_QUEUE`                                                                                    |
| `IN_PROGRESS`         | `IN_PROGRESS`                                                                                 |
| `SUCCEEDED`           | `COMPLETED`                                                                                   |
| `FAILED`              | `FAILED`                                                                                      |
| `EXPIRED`             | `TIMED_OUT`. Once a job's `ttl` passes, its data is deleted and `/status` stops returning it. |
| `CANCELED`            | `CANCELLED`                                                                                   |
| `WEBHOOK_FAILED`      | `COMPLETED`. The result is still available from `/status`.                                    |

Baseten deployment statuses map more loosely: **Active** is an endpoint with a running worker, **Scaled to zero** is an endpoint with no running workers, **Waking up** and **Loading model** are a worker that is initializing, and **Inactive** is an endpoint with max workers set to 0.

## Migrate with a coding agent

Install the Runpod plugin or skills and connect the MCP server.

```bash
# The plugin also connects the hosted MCP server
claude plugin marketplace add runpod/runpod-plugins-official
claude plugin install runpod@runpod
```

```bash
# Codex, Cursor, and others: skills, then the hosted MCP server
npx skills add runpod/runpod-plugins-official --skill '*' --agent AGENT_ID --global
npx @runpod/mcp-server@latest add --client CLIENT_ID
```

The MCP server signs in with OAuth ("Sign in with Runpod"), so you don't need an API key to start. See [Agent skills](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/agent-skills) and [MCP servers](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/mcp-servers) for the supported agents and client IDs.

Then give the agent this prompt from the root of your repository:

```text
Migrate this project from Baseten to Runpod using the runpod-cloud-migrate skill.

1. Inventory first. Find every Truss (config.yaml + model/model.py), every docker_server
   config, every Chain (truss_chains), every training config, every call to
   *.api.baseten.co or inference.baseten.co, every use of BASETEN_API_KEY, and any
   basetenlabs/baseten Terraform. If the baseten CLI is authenticated, also list models,
   deployments, environments, autoscaling settings, and secret names. Don't change
   anything yet.
2. Show me a plan: for each workload, the Runpod target (queue endpoint with a handler,
   load balancing endpoint, vLLM worker, Public Endpoint, Pod, or @app.task), the GPU
   pool, the worker and idle timeout settings mapped from my Baseten autoscaling, how
   weights and secrets move, and an estimated cost from current Runpod pricing. List
   anything with no direct equivalent (engine builder, Chains, Loops, environments,
   webhook signatures) and what you propose instead.
3. Wait for my approval before you create anything billable on Runpod.
4. Migrate one workload end to end: translate the Truss to handler.py, a Dockerfile, and
   requirements.txt (or a runpod.App if I ask for no Dockerfile), deploy it with max
   workers of 1, and send a real request. Show me the job output next to the Baseten
   output for the same input.
5. Update the client code for that workload: URL, {"input": ...} wrapper, response
   parsing, async polling or webhook payload, and auth header.
6. Stop and report. Don't deactivate or delete any Baseten model, deployment, Chain,
   volume, secret, or API key unless I approve that exact action.
```

## Troubleshooting

**The handler raises `KeyError` on the input.** The client is still sending the bare model input. Wrap it as `{"input": {...}}`. If the handler receives a nested `input` inside `job["input"]`, the client wrapped it twice.

**The client gets a 200 but no result.** `/runsync` returned before the job finished, or the code reads the top level of the response. Check `status`, read `output`, and switch long requests to `/run` plus `/status`.

**The model reloads on every request.** The load is inside `handler` (a direct port of `predict` that calls `self.load()`-style code). Move it to module scope.

**The secret is empty.** Code still reads `kwargs["secrets"]` or `/secrets/NAME`. Read the environment variable, and check that its value on the endpoint is `{{ RUNPOD_SECRET_name }}` with the exact secret name. Workers pick up a changed secret the next time they start.

**The worker never becomes ready on a load balancing endpoint, and requests return 502.** The server listens on a port the load balancer doesn't check. Set `PORT` and `PORT_HEALTH` to the server's port, expose that port, and make sure `HEALTH_CHECK_PATH` returns `200`. A server ported from Baseten that reads `PORT` and expects `8080` needs the variable set explicitly.

**The worker is stopped during startup with a large model.** Initialization exceeded the [Initialization timeout](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/endpoint-configurations#initialization-timeout). Raise it in the endpoint settings. Startup includes pulling the image and downloading the model. Baseten's default startup threshold is 30 minutes, so a model that loaded there can time out here.

**Jobs sit in the queue with no workers.** The GPU pool has no stock in the endpoint's data centers, the endpoint is pinned to one data center by a network volume, or max workers is 0 because the endpoint went unused for 7 days. Add a second pool, widen the data centers, or raise max workers.

**`exec format error` in the worker logs.** The image was built for ARM. Rebuild with `--platform linux/amd64`.

**The new image isn't running after a push.** The endpoint still references the old tag, or you pushed over a mutable tag such as `:latest`. Push a new version tag and patch the endpoint's `image`.

**The webhook receiver rejects Runpod's callbacks.** It still verifies `X-BASETEN-SIGNATURE` and parses `data`. Update it for the Runpod job payload.

# Migrate from fal to Runpod

Move fal Model API calls, fal Serverless apps, and fal Compute instances to Runpod Public Endpoints, Serverless, Pods, and Instant Clusters.

This guide is for teams that run production workloads on [fal](https://fal.ai/docs) and want to move some or all of them to Runpod. Calls to fal's hosted [Model APIs](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/model-apis/overview) map to Runpod [Public Endpoints](https://docs.runpod.io/public-endpoints/overview), `fal.App` deployments on [fal Serverless](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/serverless) map to Runpod [Serverless](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/overview) endpoints, and [fal Compute](https://fal.ai/docs/documentation/compute) instances map to [Pods](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/overview) and [Instant Clusters](https://docs.runpod.io/instant-clusters). By the end, each workload runs on Runpod, your client code calls Runpod, and the fal resources that were billing are shut down.

> **Tip**
>
> A coding agent can do most of this migration for you. See [Migrate with a coding agent](#migrate-with-a-coding-agent).

## How fal maps to Runpod

| fal concept                                                                                      | Runpod equivalent                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Notes                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Model APIs (hosted model gallery, model IDs such as `fal-ai/flux/dev`)                           | [Public Endpoints](https://docs.runpod.io/public-endpoints/overview)                                                                                                                                                   | Hosted models you call with an API key. The catalogs overlap but aren't identical. See the [model map](#model-map).         |
| Queue API (`https://queue.fal.run/MODEL_ID`)                                                     | `/run` and `/status/JOB_ID` on `https://api.runpod.ai/v2/ENDPOINT_ID`                                                                                                                                                  | Same submit, poll, and fetch pattern. On Runpod the result comes back in the status response.                               |
| Sync endpoint (`https://fal.run/MODEL_ID`), `subscribe`                                          | `/runsync`                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Waits 90 seconds by default. Raise it with `?wait=` (up to 300000 ms).                                                      |
| Streaming (`/stream`, SSE)                                                                       | `/stream/JOB_ID` on queue-based endpoints, or your own SSE route on a load-balancing endpoint                                                                                                                          | Text Public Endpoints also expose an OpenAI-compatible route.                                                               |
| Realtime (`@fal.realtime`, WebSocket)                                                            | [Load-balancing endpoint](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/load-balancing/overview) with your own WebSocket route                                                                                                     | See [Realtime and WebSocket inference](#realtime-and-websocket-inference).                                                  |
| Workflow endpoints (`workflows/OWNER/NAME`)                                                      | Your own orchestration code                                                                                                                                                                                            | Chain Public Endpoint calls in your application.                                                                            |
| fal Serverless (`fal.App`, `@fal.endpoint`)                                                      | [Serverless](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/overview): the [Runpod SDK](https://docs.runpod.io/sdk/overview) (`runpod.App`) or a custom image with a handler                                                        | Queue-based endpoints for jobs, load-balancing endpoints for your own HTTP routes.                                          |
| Runner                                                                                           | Worker                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | One container instance that serves requests.                                                                                |
| `machine_type`, `num_gpus`                                                                       | GPU pools and GPU types, `gpu_count`                                                                                                                                                                                   | See the [GPU map](#gpu-map).                                                                                                |
| `min_concurrency`, `max_concurrency`, `keep_alive`                                               | Active (minimum) workers, max workers, idle timeout                                                                                                                                                                    | See the [configuration field map](#configuration-field-map).                                                                |
| `requirements`, `ContainerImage`                                                                 | SDK `dependencies` and `system_dependencies`, or your own Docker image and [template](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/templates/overview)                                                                                  | Images must be `linux/amd64`.                                                                                               |
| `/data` persistent storage                                                                       | [Network volume](https://docs.runpod.io/storage/network-volumes), [global volume](https://docs.runpod.io/storage/globalvolume/overview), or [cached models](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/model-caching) | Network volumes mount at `/runpod-volume` on Serverless and `/workspace` on Pods, and live in one data center.              |
| fal CDN (`fal.toolkit.Image`, `fal_client.upload_file`)                                          | Your own S3-compatible bucket with the `rp_upload` helper, or base64 in the response                                                                                                                                   | Public Endpoints return hosted output URLs that expire after 7 days.                                                        |
| `fal secrets set`                                                                                | [Runpod secrets](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/templates/secrets)                                                                                                                                                        | You reference each secret explicitly in the environment.                                                                    |
| `regions`                                                                                        | `datacenter` (SDK), `dataCenterIds` (REST), `--data-center-ids` (runpodctl)                                                                                                                                            | GPU stock varies by data center.                                                                                            |
| fal Compute (`1xH100-SXM`, `8xH100-SXM`)                                                         | [Pods](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/overview), [Instant Clusters](https://docs.runpod.io/instant-clusters)                                                                                                              | Pods are containers, not VMs.                                                                                               |
| Billing: per output (Model APIs), per second of runner lifetime (Serverless), per hour (Compute) | Per output (Public Endpoints), per second while workers run (Serverless), per second (Pods)                                                                                                                            | See [Serverless pricing](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/pricing) and [Pod pricing](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/pricing). |
| `fal` CLI                                                                                        | [`runpodctl`](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/overview) and the [`rp` CLI](https://docs.runpod.io/sdk/cli)                                                                                                            | `rp flash` commands develop and deploy SDK apps.                                                                            |
| `fal-client`, `@fal-ai/client`                                                                   | `runpod` Python package, plain HTTP, [`@runpod/ai-sdk-provider`](https://docs.runpod.io/public-endpoints/ai-sdk)                                                                                                       | The Runpod SDKs are built on REST API v2.                                                                                   |
| Platform APIs (`https://api.fal.ai/v1`)                                                          | [REST API v2](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/overview) (`https://api.runpod.io/v2`)                                                                                                                           | Manage endpoints, templates, volumes, secrets, and billing.                                                                 |
| `Authorization: Key FAL_KEY`                                                                     | `Authorization: Bearer RUNPOD_API_KEY`                                                                                                                                                                                 | One API key for inference and management.                                                                                   |
| Teams and organizations                                                                          | [Organizations](https://docs.runpod.io/organizations/orgs-overview)                                                                                                                                                    | Roles, groups, and billing per organization.                                                                                |
| Dashboard logs and analytics, `fal runners logs`                                                 | Endpoint **Logs** and **Metrics** tabs, [worker logs](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/development/logs)                                                                                                              | [Job states and metrics](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/job-states) lists what's tracked.                      |
| fal MCP server                                                                                   | [Runpod MCP server](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/mcp-servers)                                                                                                                                                    | OAuth sign-in.                                                                                                              |

## What's different

### What works differently

**The request body is wrapped.** fal takes model parameters at the top level of the JSON body. Runpod takes them inside an `input` object, and options such as `webhook` and `policy` sit beside `input`.

**The result arrives with the status.** fal has separate status and result URLs. Runpod's `/status/JOB_ID` returns the status and, once the job completes, the `output`.

**Failures have their own statuses.** fal reports `IN_QUEUE`, `IN_PROGRESS`, and `COMPLETED`, and a failed request is `COMPLETED` with an `error` field. Runpod adds `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, and `TIMED_OUT`. Update any code that treats `COMPLETED` as the only terminal state.

**Results don't stay around as long.** fal stores request payloads for 90 days by default. Runpod keeps the result of a `/run` job for 30 minutes after completion and a `/runsync` result for 1 minute. Fetch results promptly or use a webhook, and store what you need.

**Output URLs expire.** Public Endpoint output URLs (`image_url`, `video_url`, `audio_url`, `result`) expire after 7 days. If you relied on fal CDN URLs as long-lived links, copy outputs to your own storage.

**Secrets are opt-in per endpoint.** By default fal injects every secret in the environment into a runner. On Runpod you map each secret into an environment variable yourself, with `runpod.Secret("NAME")` in the SDK or `{{ RUNPOD_SECRET_NAME }}` in a template or endpoint.

**Model weights aren't cached for you.** fal sets `HF_HOME` to `/data/.cache/huggingface` on every runner. On Runpod, weights download to the worker's container disk on each cold start unless you use [cached models](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/model-caching), a volume, or bake them into the image.

**Storage is attached, not ambient.** `/data` is mounted on every fal runner in your account. A Runpod network volume is created with a size, lives in one data center, and is attached to specific endpoints or Pods. Attaching one limits those workers to that data center.

**Auth is always a Runpod API key.** fal apps can be `private`, `public`, or `shared`. Runpod Serverless endpoints check a Runpod API key on every request. For unauthenticated access, put your own backend in front of the endpoint.

**Idle timeout defaults are shorter.** fal's `keep_alive` defaults to 60 seconds. The Runpod SDK's `idle_timeout` also defaults to 60, but the console default is 5 seconds and the REST v2 default is 10. Set it explicitly.

**Execution timeouts are shorter by default.** fal's `request_timeout` defaults to 3600 seconds. Runpod's execution timeout defaults to 600 seconds in the console and 300000 ms in REST v2. The SDK's `execution_timeout_ms` defaults to no limit.

**You build images yourself for the custom-image path.** `fal deploy` builds containers remotely. With the Runpod SDK, `rp flash deploy` also packages your code without Docker. With a custom worker, you build and push a `linux/amd64` image, or let the [GitHub integration](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/workers/github-integration) build it.

### What has no direct equivalent

| On fal                                                               | On Runpod                                                                                                                    | Workaround                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Workflow endpoints that chain models in one call                     | Not a hosted feature                                                                                                         | Chain calls in your own code. See the [text-to-video pipeline tutorial](https://docs.runpod.io/tutorials/public-endpoints/text-to-video-pipeline). |
| `fal_client.upload_file` and `fal.storage.upload` for input files    | Public Endpoint model pages take input media as URLs                                                                         | Host inputs in your own bucket and pass a URL the endpoint can fetch.                                                                              |
| Automatic CDN upload of `Image` and `File` outputs from your own app | Your handler uploads to your bucket with `rp_upload`, or returns base64                                                      | See [Step 4](#step-4-move-your-images-and-code).                                                                                                   |
| Signed webhooks (`X-Fal-Webhook-Signature`)                          | The Runpod webhook docs describe retries, not a signature                                                                    | Put an unguessable token in the webhook URL and confirm the job with `/status/JOB_ID`.                                                             |
| `fal.realtime` client and msgpack protocol                           | Raw WebSockets on a load-balancing endpoint                                                                                  | Define your own message format.                                                                                                                    |
| `shared` auth (callers pay with their own key)                       | Each account calls its own endpoints                                                                                         | Publish the worker to the [Hub](https://docs.runpod.io/hub/overview) so others deploy it in their account.                                         |
| `concurrency_buffer`, `concurrency_buffer_perc`                      | Autoscaling by queue delay or request count                                                                                  | Keep active workers for headroom and tune the scaler threshold.                                                                                    |
| 90-day request history and per-request payload APIs                  | Results expire in minutes                                                                                                    | Persist inputs and outputs from your webhook receiver.                                                                                             |
| Automatic retries of failed runner attempts (up to 10)               | Queue-based endpoints retry on failure, but the docs don't state a count. `/retry/JOB_ID` requeues a failed or timed-out job | Call `/retry` from your client or webhook receiver for jobs that still end as `FAILED` or `TIMED_OUT`.                                             |

Going the other way, some things exist on Runpod that you may not have used on fal: text models with an OpenAI-compatible route on Public Endpoints, `@app.task` for run-to-completion jobs on a dedicated Pod, per-second Pod billing, and Community Cloud or Secure Cloud placement for Pods.

## Requirements

- A [Runpod account](https://docs.runpod.io/accounts-billing/manage-accounts) with credits.
- A [Runpod API key](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/credentials).
- Access to your fal account or team, with the `fal` CLI installed and logged in (`fal auth login`).
- Python 3.10 to 3.14 for the Runpod SDK.
- Docker, if you'll deploy a custom image.
- An S3-compatible bucket, if your app returns files and you don't want to return base64.

## Step 1: Take inventory of what you run on fal

List everything in each fal account and team before you move anything. If you use teams, switch with `fal account set TEAM_NAME` and repeat.

```bash
# Who you're logged in as, and which accounts you can switch to
fal auth whoami
fal account list

# Environments (main, staging, and so on)
fal environments list

# Deployed apps, per environment
fal apps list --json
fal apps list --env staging --json

# Runners for one app, to see real concurrency
fal apps runners APP_NAME

# Secret names (values are never shown)
fal secrets list
fal secrets list --env staging

# Files on /data
fal files list
fal files list models/

# API keys
fal keys list
```

fal Compute instances don't appear in the app list. List them in the [Compute dashboard](https://fal.ai/dashboard/compute) or through the Platform API.

```bash
curl -s "https://api.fal.ai/v1/compute/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Key $FAL_KEY"
```

For each `fal.App`, record these values from the source file or `pyproject.toml`: `machine_type`, `num_gpus`, `min_concurrency`, `max_concurrency`, `keep_alive`, `max_multiplexing`, `request_timeout`, `startup_timeout`, `regions`, `requirements` or the `ContainerImage` Dockerfile, the secrets it reads, every `/data` path it touches, and every `@fal.endpoint` and `@fal.realtime` path. Scaling values changed with `fal apps scale` override the code, so trust `fal apps list --json` over the source for those.

Then find the code that calls fal. This command finds SDK imports, CLI usage, hostnames, and environment variables.

```bash
grep -rnE "fal_client|@fal-ai/|@ai-sdk/fal|import fal\b|from fal[. ]|fal\.run|queue\.fal\.run|fal\.media|api\.fal\.ai|FAL_KEY|FAL_API_KEY|fal (deploy|run|apps|secrets|files) |\[tool\.fal" \
  --include="*.py" --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" --include="*.js" --include="*.mjs" \
  --include="*.toml" --include="*.yml" --include="*.yaml" --include="*.sh" --include="*.env*" \
  --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.venv .
```

Write down every model ID you call (strings such as `fal-ai/flux/dev` and `workflows/OWNER/NAME`), whether each call uses `subscribe`, `submit`, `run`, `stream`, or `realtime`, and whether it uses webhooks, `fal_client.upload_file`, or stored fal CDN URLs.

## Step 2: Set up Runpod

Create an [API key](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/credentials) in the console, then install the tools you need.

```bash
# runpodctl: manage endpoints, templates, Pods, and volumes
curl -fsSL https://cli.runpod.net | sudo bash

# Runpod SDK and the rp CLI (Python 3.10 to 3.14)
pip install runpod

# Log in once. Credentials are saved to ~/.runpod/config.toml
rp login

# For scripts and CI
export RUNPOD_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
```

On macOS you can also install `runpodctl` with `brew install runpod/runpodctl/runpodctl`. For agent-driven work, connect the [Runpod MCP server](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/mcp-servers).

## Step 3: Choose where each workload lands

| What you run on fal                                                                            | Where it lands on Runpod                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Calls to a hosted model that Runpod also hosts                                                 | [Public Endpoint](https://docs.runpod.io/public-endpoints/overview)                                                                                                                |
| Calls to a hosted model that isn't a Public Endpoint                                           | Deploy the open model yourself on Serverless, or check the [Hub](https://docs.runpod.io/hub/overview) for a ready-made worker. Closed models stay with a provider that hosts them. |
| `fal.App` called through the queue (`subscribe`, `submit`, webhooks)                           | Serverless queue-based endpoint: `@app.queue` in the Runpod SDK, or a custom image with a handler                                                                                  |
| `fal.App` with several HTTP routes, SSE streaming, or an existing HTTP server (`exposed_port`) | Serverless load-balancing endpoint: `@app.api` in the Runpod SDK, or a custom image that serves HTTP                                                                               |
| `@fal.realtime` or `is_websocket=True` endpoints                                               | Serverless load-balancing endpoint with a WebSocket route                                                                                                                          |
| ComfyUI workflow deployed as a `fal.App`                                                       | The [ComfyUI worker](https://docs.runpod.io/tutorials/serverless/comfyui) from the Hub, or a customized `runpod/worker-comfyui` image                                              |
| `@fal.function` one-off jobs, training runs                                                    | `@app.task` in the Runpod SDK (one Pod per call), or a Pod                                                                                                                         |
| fal Compute `1xH100-SXM`                                                                       | Pod                                                                                                                                                                                |
| fal Compute `8xH100-SXM`, single node                                                          | Pod with multiple GPUs                                                                                                                                                             |
| fal Compute multi-node in one sector (InfiniBand)                                              | [Instant Cluster](https://docs.runpod.io/instant-clusters)                                                                                                                         |
