| `aws ec2 start-instances`                                 | `runpodctl pod start POD_ID`                                                                                                       |
| `aws ec2 reboot-instances`                                | `runpodctl pod restart POD_ID`                                                                                                     |
| `aws ec2 terminate-instances`                             | `runpodctl pod delete POD_ID`                                                                                                      |
| `aws ec2 describe-instance-types`                         | `runpodctl gpu list`                                                                                                               |
| `aws ec2 describe-regions`                                | `runpodctl datacenter list`                                                                                                        |
| `aws ec2 create-volume`                                   | `runpodctl network-volume create`                                                                                                  |
| `aws sagemaker create-model`                              | `runpodctl template create --serverless`                                                                                           |
| `aws sagemaker create-endpoint-config`, `create-endpoint` | `runpodctl serverless create`                                                                                                      |
| `aws sagemaker describe-endpoint`                         | `runpodctl serverless get ENDPOINT_ID`, `runpodctl serverless health ENDPOINT_ID`                                                  |
| `aws sagemaker list-endpoints`                            | `runpodctl serverless list`                                                                                                        |
| `aws sagemaker update-endpoint`                           | `runpodctl serverless update ENDPOINT_ID`, `runpodctl template update TEMPLATE_ID --image ...`                                     |
| AWS Cost Explorer                                         | `runpodctl billing pods`, `runpodctl billing serverless`, `runpodctl billing network-volume`                                       |
| `aws sagemaker delete-endpoint`                           | `runpodctl serverless delete ENDPOINT_ID`                                                                                          |
| `aws sagemaker-runtime invoke-endpoint`                   | `runpodctl serverless run ENDPOINT_ID --input '{...}'`                                                                             |
| `aws s3 sync`                                             | `aws s3 sync` inside a Pod, `aws s3 sync` against the volume's S3-compatible endpoint, or `runpodctl send` and `receive`           |
| `aws ecr get-login-password`                              | Not needed with an ECR delegation. For other registries, `runpodctl registry create`                                               |
| `aws logs tail --follow`                                  | `runpodctl pod logs POD_ID --follow`, `runpodctl serverless logs ENDPOINT_ID --follow`                                             |
| `aws ssm start-session`, `ssh`                            | `runpodctl ssh info POD_ID` prints the SSH command (see the [reference](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-ssh)) |

Run `runpodctl COMMAND --help` for current flags.

### API map

| AWS API                                                          | Runpod REST API v2                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| EC2 `RunInstances`                                               | `POST /v2/pods`                                                                                                |
| EC2 `DescribeInstances`                                          | `GET /v2/pods`, `GET /v2/pods/{id}`                                                                            |
| EC2 `StopInstances`, `StartInstances`, `RebootInstances`         | `POST /v2/pods/{id}/action` with `stop`, `start`, or `restart`                                                 |
| EC2 `TerminateInstances`                                         | `DELETE /v2/pods/{id}`                                                                                         |
| EC2 `CreateVolume`                                               | `POST /v2/network-volumes`                                                                                     |
| SageMaker `CreateModel`                                          | `POST /v2/templates`                                                                                           |
| SageMaker `CreateEndpointConfig`, `CreateEndpoint`               | `POST /v2/serverless`                                                                                          |
| SageMaker `UpdateEndpoint`, `UpdateEndpointWeightsAndCapacities` | `PATCH /v2/serverless/{id}`                                                                                    |
| SageMaker `DeleteEndpoint`                                       | `DELETE /v2/serverless/{id}`                                                                                   |
| SageMaker Runtime `InvokeEndpoint`                               | `POST https://api.runpod.ai/v2/ENDPOINT_ID/runsync`, or your own path on `https://ENDPOINT_ID.api.runpod.ai`   |
| SageMaker Runtime `InvokeEndpointAsync`                          | `POST https://api.runpod.ai/v2/ENDPOINT_ID/run`                                                                |
| SageMaker Runtime `InvokeEndpointWithResponseStream`             | `GET https://api.runpod.ai/v2/ENDPOINT_ID/stream/JOB_ID`, or a streaming response from a load balancing worker |
| Bedrock Runtime `Converse`, `InvokeModel`                        | `POST https://api.runpod.ai/v2/ENDPOINT_ID/openai/v1/chat/completions`                                         |
| ECR `GetAuthorizationToken`                                      | `POST /v2/registries/delegations` (once)                                                                       |
| Secrets Manager `CreateSecret`                                   | `POST /v2/account/secrets`                                                                                     |
| CloudWatch Logs `GetLogEvents`                                   | `GET /v2/pods/{id}/logs`, `GET /v2/serverless/{id}/workers/{workerId}/logs`                                    |

Management routes use `https://api.runpod.io/v2`. Inference routes use `https://api.runpod.ai`.

### Configuration field map

| AWS field                                 | REST API v2 field                                         | runpodctl flag                             |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `InstanceType`                            | `gpu.id` and `gpu.count` (Pods), `gpu.pools` (Serverless) | `--gpu-id`, `--gpu-count`                  |
| `ImageId` (AMI), `PrimaryContainer.Image` | `image`                                                   | `--image`                                  |
| `UserData`                                | `cmd`, `entrypoint`, or the image's own command           | `--docker-args`                            |
| `PrimaryContainer.Environment`            | `env`                                                     | `--env`                                    |
| `SecurityGroupIds` (ingress ports)        | `ports`                                                   | `--ports`                                  |
| `BlockDeviceMappings` root volume size    | `disk`                                                    | `--container-disk-in-gb`                   |
| EBS data volume                           | `mounts.persistent`, `mounts.network`                     | `--volume-in-gb`, `--network-volume-id`    |
| `Placement.AvailabilityZone`, Region      | `dataCenterIds`                                           | `--data-center-ids`                        |
| `InitialInstanceCount`, `MinCapacity`     | `workers.min`                                             | `--workers-min`                            |
| `MaxCapacity`                             | `workers.max`                                             | `--workers-max`                            |
| Target tracking `TargetValue`             | `scaling.requestCount` or `scaling.queueDelay`            | `--scale-by`, `--scale-threshold`          |
| Scale-in cooldown                         | `workers.idleTimeout`                                     | `--idle-timeout`                           |
| `ModelDataUrl`                            | No field. Image, network volume, or cached model          | `--network-volume-id`, `--model-reference` |
| `ExecutionRoleArn`, `IamInstanceProfile`  | No field. Secrets in `env`                                | `--env`                                    |
| `KeyName`                                 | `startSsh` with account SSH keys                          | `--ssh`                                    |

### Environment variable map

| On AWS                                                              | On Runpod                                                 | Notes                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Instance ID from the metadata service                               | `RUNPOD_POD_ID`                                           | Runpod has no metadata service at `169.254.169.254`.       |
| Region or Availability Zone from the metadata service, `AWS_REGION` | `RUNPOD_DC_ID`                                            | Keep `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` set for boto3 calls back to AWS. |
| Public IPv4 from the metadata service                               | `RUNPOD_PUBLIC_IP`, `RUNPOD_TCP_PORT_22`                  | Present when the Pod has a public IP.                      |
| Credentials from the instance profile or execution role             | `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` from secrets | Set them yourself.                                         |
| Port 8080 (SageMaker contract)                                      | `PORT`, `PORT_HEALTH`, `HEALTH_CHECK_PATH`                | Load balancing endpoints only.                             |
| `/opt/ml/model`                                                     | Your own path, such as `/runpod-volume/my-model`          | Or bake the same path into the image.                      |
| `SAGEMAKER_BATCH`, `SAGEMAKER_MAX_CONCURRENT_TRANSFORMS`            | None                                                      | Batch behavior is handled by your handler.                 |
| GPU count from the instance type                                    | `RUNPOD_GPU_COUNT`                                        | Pods also set `RUNPOD_CPU_COUNT`.                          |

### Status map

| AWS status                                 | Runpod status                                                |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| EC2 `pending`                              | Pod `PROVISIONING`, `STARTING`                               |
| EC2 `running`                              | Pod `RUNNING`                                                |
| EC2 `stopping`, `stopped`                  | Pod `EXITED`                                                 |
| EC2 `shutting-down`, `terminated`          | Pod `TERMINATED`                                             |
| SageMaker endpoint `Creating`, `Updating`  | Workers `INITIALIZING`                                       |
| SageMaker endpoint `InService`             | Workers `IDLE` or `RUNNING`                                  |
| SageMaker endpoint `Failed`                | Workers `UNHEALTHY`, or `THROTTLED` when waiting on capacity |
| Asynchronous request queued or processing  | Job `IN_QUEUE`, `IN_PROGRESS`                                |
| Asynchronous success or error notification | Job `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `TIMED_OUT`, `CANCELLED`          |

A Runpod endpoint has no single endpoint-level status like `InService`. Read worker states from `runpodctl serverless health ENDPOINT_ID`.

## Migrate with a coding agent

A coding agent with the Runpod skills and MCP server can run this migration with you: it reads your AWS inventory, proposes a plan, and creates Runpod resources after you approve them.

```bash
# The plugin also connects the hosted MCP server
claude plugin marketplace add runpod/runpod-plugins-official
claude plugin install runpod@runpod
```

```bash
# Skills, then the hosted MCP server (Codex, Cursor, and others)
npx skills add runpod/runpod-plugins-official --skill '*' --agent AGENT_ID --global
npx @runpod/mcp-server@latest add --client CLIENT_ID
```

The MCP server signs in with OAuth ("Sign in with Runpod"), so you don't need an API key to start. See [Agent skills](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/agent-skills) and [MCP servers](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/mcp-servers) for details. Then give the agent this prompt from the root of your repository:

```text
Use the runpod-cloud-migrate skill to migrate our AWS GPU workloads to Runpod.

1. Inventory first, read-only. Use the AWS CLI with my current profile to list GPU EC2
   instances (and their user data), SageMaker endpoints, endpoint configs, models,
   autoscaling targets, notebook instances, Bedrock provisioned throughput, ECR
   repositories, and the S3 buckets they read. Search this repo for boto3
   sagemaker-runtime and bedrock-runtime calls, SageMaker inference scripts
   (model_fn, /invocations, /opt/ml), and aws_instance or aws_sagemaker_* Terraform.
2. Show me a plan: each workload, its Runpod target (Pod, queue endpoint, load
   balancing endpoint, Public Endpoint, vLLM endpoint, or Instant Cluster), the GPU
   type or pool, where its data will live, what stays on AWS, and a cost estimate
   from current Runpod pricing. List every gap that needs my decision (VPC-only
   resources, IAM roles, KMS, multi-model endpoints).
3. Wait for my approval before creating anything billable on Runpod.
4. Migrate one workload end to end. Keep S3 as the data store unless I say otherwise,
   and use scoped IAM credentials stored as Runpod secrets, never my admin keys.
   If we use Terraform, add the Runpod provider next to the AWS provider.
5. Verify with a real request and compare the output with the AWS endpoint.
6. Never stop, delete, or modify AWS resources without my explicit approval. When
   I approve shutdown, list the leftovers first: EBS volumes and snapshots, Elastic
   IPs, NAT gateways, endpoint configs, models, log groups.
```

## Troubleshooting

**Workers start, then requests return `502` and workers recycle after about 8 minutes.** The load balancer can't reach your health check. SageMaker containers listen on 8080, and Runpod checks port 80 unless told otherwise. Set both `PORT` and `PORT_HEALTH` to `8080` and expose `8080/http`.

**The container exits immediately on Runpod but ran on SageMaker.** SageMaker starts inference containers with the `serve` argument. Without it, an entrypoint that dispatches on `serve` or `train` exits. Set the container command to `serve`, or change the image's `CMD`.

**`FileNotFoundError` under `/opt/ml/model`.** Nothing unpacks `model.tar.gz` on Runpod. Bake the files into the image, or mount a network volume and point your code at it.

**`Unable to locate credentials` or `NoCredentialsError` from boto3.** There's no instance profile or execution role. Create a scoped IAM user, store its keys as Runpod secrets, and map them to `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` in the template's environment variables. Set `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` too.

**Requests to `169.254.169.254` hang.** Code is calling the EC2 instance metadata service. Replace those lookups with the `RUNPOD_` environment variables and explicit configuration.

**`exec format error` when the container starts.** The image was built for arm64 (Graviton or Apple silicon). Rebuild with `--platform linux/amd64`.

**Image pull fails for an ECR image.** Confirm the repository policy lists both Runpod role ARNs exactly, that a delegation exists for that repository (`GET /v2/registries/delegations`), and that the tag exists. If you stored a `get-login-password` token as a registry credential, it expired after 12 hours. Use a delegation instead.

**`{"error":"no workers available"}` from a load balancing endpoint.** The endpoint scaled to zero and the first worker hasn't passed its health check. Retry with a delay of 5 to 10 seconds, or set min workers to 1.

**CUDA or driver errors on some workers only.** Hosts differ in driver version. Set `--min-cuda-version` (REST `gpu.minCudaVersion`) to the version your framework build needs.

**A Pod can't see a network volume, or deploy fails for lack of capacity.** The volume pins the Pod to its data center, and the GPU you asked for isn't in stock there. Pick a GPU type that data center has, or create the volume in a data center with stock for your GPU.

  Review the health check, port, and timeout contract.

# Migrate from Google Cloud to Runpod

Move GPU training, inference, and batch workloads from Compute Engine, Vertex AI, Cloud Run, and GKE to Runpod, and keep the rest on Google Cloud.

This guide is for teams that run GPU workloads on Google Cloud and want to move the GPU-heavy part (training, inference, batch) to Runpod. Most teams keep their data, identity, and the rest of the application on Google Cloud, so the guide covers that hybrid setup first and a full exit second. [Compute Engine](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus) GPU VMs map to [Pods](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/overview), [Vertex AI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/get-online-predictions) endpoints and [Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/gpu) GPU services map to [Serverless](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/overview) endpoints, managed model APIs map to [Public Endpoints](https://docs.runpod.io/public-endpoints/overview), and Slurm clusters map to [Instant Clusters](https://docs.runpod.io/instant-clusters/slurm-clusters). When you finish, your workload runs on Runpod, your callers use a Runpod API key, and the Google Cloud resources you replaced are shut down.

> **Tip**
>
> You can hand this migration to a coding agent. See [Migrate with a coding agent](#migrate-with-a-coding-agent).

> **Note**
>
> Google's documentation now calls Vertex AI "Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform". The `gcloud ai` commands, the Vertex AI SDK for Python, the `aiplatform.googleapis.com` API, and the Terraform `google_vertex_ai_*` resources keep their names, so this guide says Vertex AI throughout.
