# hub

Browse and search Runpod Hub repos with runpodctl, inspect repository details, and use Hub IDs to deploy Serverless endpoints.

Browse and search the Runpod Hub marketplace to discover deployable repos. You can list popular repos, search by name, and get details for specific repos. Use Hub repo IDs with [`runpodctl serverless create --hub-id`](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-serverless) to deploy endpoints directly from the Hub.

```bash
runpodctl hub <subcommand> [flags]
```

## Subcommands

### List repos

List repos from the Hub marketplace. By default, shows the top 10 repos ordered by stars.

```bash
# List top repos by stars
runpodctl hub list

# List only Serverless repos
runpodctl hub list --type SERVERLESS

# List only Pod repos
runpodctl hub list --type POD

# Filter by category
runpodctl hub list --category ai --limit 20

# Order by deployment count
runpodctl hub list --order-by deploys

# Filter by repo owner
runpodctl hub list --owner runpod
```

#### List flags

**--type (type: string)**

Filter by deployment type (`POD` or `SERVERLESS`). This filter is applied client-side, so `--limit` may return fewer results than specified.

**--category (type: string)**

Filter by category.

**--owner (type: string)**

Filter by repo owner.

**--order-by (type: string)**

Sort results by field: `createdAt`, `deploys`, `releasedAt`, `stars`, `updatedAt`, or `views`.

**--order-dir (type: string)**

Sort direction: `asc` or `desc`.

**--limit (type: int)**

Maximum number of results to return.

**--offset (type: int)**

Number of results to skip for pagination.

### Search repos

Search for repos in the Hub by name:

```bash
# Search for vLLM repos
runpodctl hub search vllm

# Search Serverless repos only
runpodctl hub search whisper --type SERVERLESS

# Limit search results
runpodctl hub search stable-diffusion --limit 5
```

#### Search flags

**--type (type: string)**

Filter by deployment type (`POD` or `SERVERLESS`). This filter is applied client-side, so `--limit` may return fewer results than specified.

**--category (type: string)**

Filter by category.

**--owner (type: string)**

Filter by repo owner.

**--order-by (type: string)**

Sort results by field: `createdAt`, `deploys`, `releasedAt`, `stars`, `updatedAt`, or `views`.

**--order-dir (type: string)**

Sort direction: `asc` or `desc`.

**--limit (type: int)**

Maximum number of results to return.

**--offset (type: int)**

Number of results to skip for pagination.

### Get repo details

Get detailed information about a specific Hub repo by its ID or owner/name:

```bash
# Get by listing ID
runpodctl hub get cm8h09d9n000008jvh2rqdsmb

# Get by owner/name
runpodctl hub get runpod-workers/worker-vllm
```

## Deploy from the Hub

After finding a repo you want to deploy, use its listing ID with `serverless create`:

```bash
# Find a repo
runpodctl hub search vllm

# Deploy it
runpodctl serverless create --hub-id cm8h09d9n000008jvh2rqdsmb --name "my-vllm"
```

GPU IDs and container disk size are automatically pulled from the Hub release config. You can override the GPU type with `--gpu-id`.

# Document: model

Source path: runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-model.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-model.mdx
Canonical documentation: https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-model
Description: Use runpodctl to add, list, and remove models in the Runpod model repository, including uploads from a local directory or Hugging Face.

# model

Use runpodctl to add, list, and remove models in the Runpod model repository, including uploads from a local directory or Hugging Face.

Manage models in the Runpod model repository. You can add a model from a local directory or mirror one from Hugging Face, list your models, and remove ones you no longer need.

```bash Command
runpodctl model <subcommand> [flags]
```

## Subcommands

### List models

List the models in your model repository:

```bash
runpodctl model list
```

You can use `ls` as a shorthand for `list`.

#### List flags

**--name (type: string)**

Filter by model name.

**--provider (type: string)**

Filter by provider.

### Add a model

Add a model by mirroring a Hugging Face repository. `--name` is the name the model gets in your repository, and `--huggingface-model` is the source:

```bash
runpodctl model add --name tiny-llm --huggingface-model arnir0/Tiny-LLM
```

Add a model by uploading a local directory of model files:

```bash
runpodctl model add --name my-model --model-path ./my-model-dir
```

To wait until the uploaded model is ready to deploy, add `--wait-for-hash`. To also delete the local files once the upload is confirmed, add `--delete-my-model-files-after-upload`:

```bash
runpodctl model add --name my-model --model-path ./my-model-dir \
  --wait-for-hash --delete-my-model-files-after-upload
```

`--huggingface-model` can't be combined with the local upload flags, such as `--model-path`.

> **Warning**
>
> `--delete-my-model-files-after-upload` deletes the files in `--model-path` from your machine. It requires `--wait-for-hash`, so files are deleted only after the model version is confirmed deployable.

#### Add flags

**--name (type: string; required)**

Name for the model in your repository.

**--huggingface-model (type: string)**

Hugging Face model to mirror, in `owner/repo` format.

**--model-path (type: string)**

Local directory containing the model files to upload.

**--owner (type: string)**

Owner namespace for the model: a user or team owner ID.

**--wait-for-hash (type: bool)**

Wait for a completed `--model-path` upload to become deployable.

**--hash-timeout (type: duration)**

Maximum time to wait with `--wait-for-hash` (default `30m`). `0` disables the timeout.

**--delete-my-model-files-after-upload (type: bool)**

Delete the uploaded `--model-path` files once the model version is confirmed deployable. Requires `--wait-for-hash`.

**--verbose, -v (type: bool)**

Include upload details in the `--wait-for-hash` output.

**--metadata (type: string)**

Metadata as `key=value` pairs.

**--model-status (type: string)**

Initial model status.

**--credential-type (type: string)**

Credential type, if the source requires one.

**--credential-reference (type: string)**

Credential reference, if the source requires one.

**--create-upload (type: bool)**

Create an upload session.

**--file-name (type: string)**

File name for the upload.

**--file-size (type: string)**

File size in bytes.

**--content-type (type: string)**

Content type of the upload.

**--part-size (type: string)**

Part size for multipart uploads, in bytes.

### Remove a model

Remove a model from your repository. Both `--name` and `--owner` are required:

```bash
runpodctl model remove --owner <owner> --name my-model
```

You can use `rm` or `delete` as a shorthand for `remove`.

A model that a Serverless endpoint still references can't be removed. The command fails and lists the endpoints that use it. Detach the model from each endpoint first, then remove it:

```bash
runpodctl serverless update <endpoint-id> --clear-models
runpodctl model remove --owner <owner> --name my-model
```

#### Remove flags

**--name (type: string; required)**

Name of the model to remove.

**--owner (type: string; required)**

Owner of the model.

**--version (type: string)**

UUID of a specific model version to remove.

**--hash (type: string)**

Hash of a specific model version to remove.

- [`runpodctl network-volume`](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-network-volume)


# Document: network-volume

Source path: runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-network-volume.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-network-volume.mdx
Canonical documentation: https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-network-volume
Description: Use runpodctl to create, inspect, list, update, and remove persistent network volumes shared by Pods and Serverless endpoints.

# network-volume

Use runpodctl to create, inspect, list, update, and remove persistent network volumes shared by Pods and Serverless endpoints.

Manage network volumes for persistent shared storage across Pods and Serverless endpoints.

```bash Command
runpodctl network-volume <subcommand> [flags]
```

## Alias

You can use `nv` as a shorthand for `network-volume`:

```bash
runpodctl nv list
```

## Subcommands

### List network volumes

List all your network volumes:

```bash
runpodctl network-volume list
```

### Get network volume details

Get detailed information about a specific network volume:

```bash
runpodctl network-volume get <volume-id>
```

### Create a network volume

Create a new network volume:

```bash
runpodctl network-volume create --name "my-volume" --size 100 --data-center-id "US-GA-1"
```

#### Create flags

**--name (type: string; required)**

Volume name.

**--size (type: int; required)**

Volume size in GB (10-4096).

**--data-center-id (type: string; required)**

Datacenter ID where the volume will be created. Use [`runpodctl datacenter list`](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-datacenter) to see available datacenters.

### Update a network volume

Update network volume configuration:

```bash
runpodctl network-volume update <volume-id> --name "new-name"
```

#### Update flags

**--name (type: string)**

New volume name.

**--size (type: int)**

New volume size in GB. Must be larger than the current size.

### Upload files

Upload a file or folder to a network volume:

```bash
runpodctl network-volume upload <volume-id> ./model.safetensors models/
runpodctl network-volume upload <volume-id> ./dataset datasets/dataset
```

The remote path is optional and defaults to the local name. A file uploaded to a remote path that ends in `/` keeps its name inside that folder, and a folder's contents land under the remote path.

### Download files

Download a file or folder from a network volume:

```bash
runpodctl network-volume download <volume-id> models/model.safetensors
runpodctl network-volume download <volume-id> outputs/ ./outputs
```

The local path is optional and defaults to the remote name. Use `/` as the remote path to download the whole volume.

#### Requirements for upload and download

Both commands need `runpodctl` v3.1.0 or later. They use the network volume's [S3-compatible API](https://docs.runpod.io/storage/s3-api), so they also need the following:

- **S3 API keys**, which are separate from your Runpod API key. Create them in your [account settings](https://console.runpod.io/user/settings), then set the `RUNPOD_S3_ACCESS_KEY` and `RUNPOD_S3_SECRET_KEY` environment variables, pass the flags below, or set `s3AccessKey` and `s3SecretKey` in `~/.runpod/config.toml`.
- **A data center that supports the S3-compatible API.** The CLI looks up the volume's data center with your Runpod API key. Pass `--data-center-id` to skip the lookup.

Transfers resume. If one stops because of a network drop or an interruption, run the same command again: finished files are skipped, and a large file continues from the parts already transferred. Files are also skipped when the destination copy has the same size and isn't older.

#### Upload and download flags

**--concurrency (type: int)**

Number of parallel requests, from 1 to 64 (default `4`).

**--data-center-id (type: string)**

The volume's data center ID, such as `EU-RO-1`. By default, the CLI looks it up from the volume.

**--force (type: bool)**

Transfer every file, including files that the size and time check treats as unchanged. Use it after an edit that kept a file the same size.

**--s3-access-key (type: string)**

S3 API access key. Defaults to the `RUNPOD_S3_ACCESS_KEY` environment variable.

**--s3-secret-key (type: string)**

S3 API secret key. Defaults to the `RUNPOD_S3_SECRET_KEY` environment variable.

### Delete a network volume

Delete a network volume:

```bash
runpodctl network-volume delete <volume-id>
```

> **Warning**
>
> Deleting a network volume permanently removes all data stored on it. Make sure to back up any important data before deleting.

- [`runpodctl datacenter list`](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-datacenter)


# Document: registry

Source path: runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-registry.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-registry.mdx
Canonical documentation: https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-registry
Description: Use runpodctl to list, inspect, create, update, and remove credentials for private container registries used by Runpod workloads.

# registry

Use runpodctl to list, inspect, create, update, and remove credentials for private container registries used by Runpod workloads.

Manage container registry authentications for private Docker images.

```bash Command
runpodctl registry <subcommand> [flags]
```

## Alias

You can use `reg` as a shorthand for `registry`:

```bash
runpodctl reg list
```

## Subcommands

### List registry authentications

List all your container registry authentications:

```bash
runpodctl registry list
```

### Get registry authentication details

Get details about a specific registry authentication:

```bash
runpodctl registry get <registry-id>
```

### Create a registry authentication

Create credentials for a private container registry. Supply the password in one of three ways:

- Pass it directly with the `--password` flag.
- Pipe or redirect it into `--password-stdin`.
- Omit both flags to enter it at an interactive prompt.

Pass the password directly with `--password`:

```bash
runpodctl registry create --name "docker-hub" --username "myuser" --password "mypassword"
```

Omit the password flag to have the command prompt for the password without echoing it:

```bash
runpodctl registry create --name "docker-hub" --username "myuser"
```

Pipe a token held in an environment variable into `--password-stdin`:

```bash
printenv REGISTRY_TOKEN | runpodctl registry create --name "docker-hub" --username "myuser" --password-stdin
```

Redirect a token from a file into `--password-stdin`:

```bash
runpodctl registry create --name "docker-hub" --username "myuser" --password-stdin < token.txt
```

For Google Artifact Registry or gcr.io, set `--username` to the literal `_json_key` and feed the multi-line service-account JSON key file through `--password-stdin`. The command supports multi-line passwords and strips only a single trailing newline added by the pipe or redirection.

```bash
runpodctl registry create --name "gcr" --username "_json_key" --password-stdin < service-account.json
```

> **Tip**
>
> Prefer `--password-stdin` or the interactive prompt over `--password`. A value passed to `--password` is visible in the process table and your shell history.

#### Create flags

**--name (type: string; required)**

Name for this registry authentication.

**--username (type: string; required)**

Registry username.

**--password (type: string)**

Registry password or access token. Cannot be used with `--password-stdin`. If neither `--password` nor `--password-stdin` is given, the command prompts for the password when run in an interactive terminal, or exits with an error otherwise.

**--password-stdin (type: bool)**

Read the registry password from standard input (pipe, heredoc, or file redirection). Supports multi-line values. Cannot be used with `--password`.

### Delete a registry authentication

Delete a registry authentication:

```bash
runpodctl registry delete <registry-id>
```

- [`runpodctl template create`](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-template)
- [`runpodctl pod create`](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-pod)


# Document: gpu

Source path: runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-gpu.mdx

Description: Use runpodctl to list available GPU types, include unavailable options, and review hardware specifications from the command line.

# gpu

Use runpodctl to list available GPU types, include unavailable options, and review hardware specifications from the command line.

List available GPU types and their specifications.

```bash Command
runpodctl gpu <subcommand> [flags]
```

## Subcommands

### List available GPUs

List GPUs that are currently available. A GPU counts as available when it has stock in Secure Cloud or Community Cloud:

```bash
runpodctl gpu list
```

Include unavailable GPUs in the list:

```bash
runpodctl gpu list --include-unavailable
```

#### List flags

**--include-unavailable (type: bool)**

Include GPUs that are currently unavailable.

## Example output

GPU entries report on-demand pricing and, where the catalog provides them, per-data-center stock statuses and an overall `stockStatus`:

```json
[
  {
    "available": true,
    "communityCloud": true,
    "communityPricePerHr": 0.34,
    "dataCenterAvailability": [
      { "dataCenterId": "US-CA-2", "stockStatus": "High" },
      { "dataCenterId": "EU-RO-1", "stockStatus": "Low" },
      { "dataCenterId": "US-KS-2", "stockStatus": "none" }
    ],
    "displayName": "RTX 4090",
    "gpuId": "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090",
    "memoryInGb": 24,
    "secureCloud": true,
    "securePricePerHr": 0.44,
    "stockStatus": "High"
  },
  {
    "available": true,
    "communityCloud": false,
    "communityPricePerHr": null,
    "dataCenterAvailability": [
      { "dataCenterId": "US-CA-2", "stockStatus": "High" },
      { "dataCenterId": "EU-RO-1", "stockStatus": "Medium" }
    ],
    "displayName": "A100 PCIe",
    "gpuId": "NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe",
    "memoryInGb": 80,
    "secureCloud": true,
    "securePricePerHr": 1.39,
    "stockStatus": "High"
  }
]
```

### Output fields

**securePricePerHr (type: number | null)**

On-demand price per hour in USD on Secure Cloud. Explicitly `null` when the GPU is not offered on Secure Cloud (distinguishable from a real `0`).

**communityPricePerHr (type: number | null)**

On-demand price per hour in USD on Community Cloud. Explicitly `null` when the GPU is not offered on Community Cloud.

**stockStatus (type: string)**

Best availability from the catalog's overall status and its per-data-center entries. Typical values are `High`, `Medium`, and `Low`; the field is omitted when no stock is reported. The overall catalog status can reflect Community Cloud stock that has no data-center entry.

**dataCenterAvailability (type: array)**

Per-data-center availability breakdown. Every data center that offers the GPU is listed; a data center with no reported stock is included with `stockStatus: "none"` so you can tell "offered here, out of stock" apart from "not offered here." The field is omitted when the catalog returns no data-center entries.

**available (type: bool)**

`true` when `stockStatus` reports stock. Derived from the best overall status, including Community Cloud stock that has no data-center entry.

## Using GPU IDs

When creating Pods or Serverless endpoints, use the GPU ID from the list with the `--gpu-id` flag:

```bash
runpodctl pod create --template-id runpod-torch-v21 --gpu-id "NVIDIA RTX 4090"
```

# billing

Use runpodctl to retrieve billing history for Pods, Serverless endpoints, and network volumes across configurable time ranges.

View billing history for Pods, Serverless endpoints, and network volumes. Each command returns one record per resource per time bucket, with the total cost split into its components.

```bash Command
runpodctl billing <subcommand> [flags]
```

## Subcommands

### View Pod billing

View billing history for Pods:

```bash
runpodctl billing pods
```

#### Pod billing flags

**--bucket-size (type: string)**

Time bucket size (`hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`).

**--start-time (type: string)**

Start time in RFC3339 format (e.g., `2024-01-01T00:00:00Z`).

**--end-time (type: string)**

End time in RFC3339 format.

**--pod-id (type: string)**

Filter by specific Pod ID.

Each record includes `startTime`, `endTime`, `podId`, `totalAmount`, and the cost split into `gpuAmount`, `cpuAmount`, and `diskAmount`. CPU Pods are included.

```json
[
  {
    "startTime": "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z",
    "endTime": "2026-09-02T00:00:00Z",
    "podId": "abc123xyz",
    "totalAmount": 4.32,
    "gpuAmount": 4.08,
    "cpuAmount": 0,
    "diskAmount": 0.24
  }
]
```

### View Serverless billing

View billing history for Serverless endpoints:

```bash
runpodctl billing serverless
```

#### Serverless billing flags

**--bucket-size (type: string)**

Time bucket size (`hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`).

**--start-time (type: string)**

Start time in RFC3339 format.

**--end-time (type: string)**

End time in RFC3339 format.

**--endpoint-id (type: string)**

Filter by specific endpoint ID.

Each record includes `startTime`, `endTime`, `serverlessId` (the endpoint ID), `totalAmount`, and the cost split into `gpuAmount`, `cpuAmount`, and `diskAmount`. CPU endpoints are included.

### View network volume billing

View billing history for network volumes:

```bash
runpodctl billing network-volume
```

#### Network volume billing flags

**--bucket-size (type: string)**

Time bucket size (`hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`).

**--start-time (type: string)**

Start time in RFC3339 format.

**--end-time (type: string)**

End time in RFC3339 format.

Each record includes `startTime`, `endTime`, `networkVolumeId`, `totalAmount`, and the cost split into `standardAmount` and `highPerformanceAmount` for standard and high-performance storage.

# Document: ssh

Source path: runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-ssh.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-ssh.mdx
Canonical documentation: https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-ssh
Description: Use runpodctl to manage SSH keys and retrieve the connection command and key details required to access a Runpod Pod.

# ssh

Use runpodctl to manage SSH keys and retrieve the connection command and key details required to access a Runpod Pod.

Manage SSH keys and get SSH connection information for Pods.

```bash Command
runpodctl ssh <subcommand> [flags]
```

## Subcommands

### Get SSH connection info

Get SSH connection details for a Pod. This returns the SSH command and key information, but does not initiate an interactive session:

```bash
runpodctl ssh info <pod-id>
```

#### Info flags

**--verbose (type: bool)**

Include Pod ID and name in output. Shorthand: `-v`.

> **Note**
>
> The `ssh info` command returns connection details that you can use to connect via SSH manually. It does not start an interactive SSH session. When a Pod is not reachable, `runpodctl ssh info` reports the specific reason instead of a generic message.
>
> To connect to your Pod, use the SSH command provided in the output:
>
> ```bash
> ssh user@host -p <port> -i <key-path>
> ```

`runpodctl ssh info` explains which of the following cases applies. It also reports the Pod's `runtimeStatus`, so you can match a not-ready result to the runtime status vocabulary:

| Reason                   | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                          | What to do                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Pod is initializing      | No container is reported yet (image pull, container creation, or boot).                                                                                                                          | Wait and try again.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Pod is stopped           | The Pod's container is gone but its disk is kept.                                                                                                                                                | Start it with `runpodctl pod start <pod-id>`.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Pod is terminated        | The Pod has been destroyed.                                                                                                                                                                      | None; deploy a new Pod.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Pod is in an error state | The Pod is in a state it won't recover from on its own.                                                                                                                                          | Check `runpodctl pod logs <pod-id>`, then delete or recreate the Pod.                                                                                                                                                    |
| No SSH port published    | The Pod is running but does not publish `22/tcp`.                                                                                                                                                | Add it with the `runpodctl pod update` command the CLI provides (see the Warning below).                                                                                                                                 |
| No public IP             | Port 22 is mapped, but the machine has no publicly routable IP. This affects direct SSH over a public IP specifically; basic SSH (proxied through Runpod, no public IP required) may still work. | Use [Basic SSH](https://docs.runpod.io/pods/configuration/use-ssh#basic-ssh-with-key-authentication), which does not need a public IP. If you need direct SSH over a public IP, redeploy on a machine that provides one. |
| Mapping not ready yet    | Port 22 is declared, but the host has not published the mapping yet.                                                                                                                             | Wait and try again.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

For the "No SSH port published" case, `runpodctl ssh info` gives you a ready-to-run command of the form `runpodctl pod update <pod-id> --ports <existing-ports>,22/tcp` that preserves your existing ports.

> **Warning**
>
> `runpodctl pod update --ports` replaces the Pod's entire port list (unlike `--env`, which merges), so always include your current ports when you add `22/tcp`. Changing the port list also bumps the Pod's version, which can restart the container. Processes and container-local state outside the volume disk may not survive. If the Pod is running an active job, checkpoint your work to the volume disk before changing ports, since the container may restart.

For the full list of runtime status values, see [Pod runtime status](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-pod#pod-runtime-status).

### List SSH keys

List all SSH keys associated with your account:

```bash
runpodctl ssh list-keys
```

### Add an SSH key

Add a new SSH key to your account:

```bash
# Add a key from a file
runpodctl ssh add-key --key-file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

# Add a key directly
runpodctl ssh add-key --key "ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."
```

If the key or file contains several public keys, one per line, each is saved as a separate key. Blank lines and comment lines that start with `#` are skipped. If any other line isn't a valid public key, the command fails before saving anything. Keys already on your account are matched by fingerprint and aren't added again.

#### Add-key flags

**--key (type: string)**

The public key string to add.

**--key-file (type: string)**

Path to a file containing the public key.

**--remove-invalid (type: bool)**

Delete saved entries that aren't valid public keys without asking. See [Fix invalid saved entries](#fix-invalid-saved-entries).

### Remove an SSH key

Remove an SSH key from your account by name or fingerprint:

```bash
# Remove a key by name
runpodctl ssh remove-key --name my-laptop

# Remove a key by fingerprint
runpodctl ssh remove-key --fingerprint SHA256:abcd1234...
```

You must provide `--name`, `--fingerprint`, or `--invalid`. If multiple keys share the same name, use `--fingerprint` instead.

#### Remove-key flags

**--name (type: string)**

Name of the key to remove.

**--fingerprint (type: string)**

Fingerprint of the key to remove. Use this when multiple keys have the same name.

**--invalid (type: bool)**

Remove every saved entry that isn't a valid public key, and keep all valid keys. Can't be combined with `--name` or `--fingerprint`.

**--remove-invalid (type: bool)**

Delete saved entries that aren't valid public keys without asking, then remove the key you specified.

### Fix invalid saved entries

Older accounts can have saved SSH key entries that aren't valid public keys, such as a stray line of text. While any such entry exists, Runpod rejects every change to your key list, so you can't add or remove keys.

When you run `ssh add-key` or `ssh remove-key` in an interactive terminal, runpodctl lists the invalid entries and asks whether to delete them before continuing. Nothing is deleted unless you confirm.

When runpodctl runs in a script or from an AI agent, it doesn't prompt. Instead, the command fails with a `conflict` error that names the invalid entry. To fix it, do one of the following:

- Re-run the command with `--remove-invalid` to delete the invalid entries as part of the same change.
- Run `runpodctl ssh remove-key --invalid` to delete only the invalid entries.

### Forget a Pod's host key

Remove the host key that runpodctl recorded for a Pod in `~/.runpod/ssh/known_hosts`, so the next connection trusts the key the Pod offers:

```bash
runpodctl ssh forget <pod-id>
```

Use this after stopping and starting a Pod, or updating it, changed its host key. If the Pod didn't restart, a host key mismatch can mean the connection is being intercepted, so check before you run it. The SSH command that `ssh info` prints uses your own `~/.ssh/known_hosts` and isn't affected.

- [`runpodctl pod get`](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-pod)
- [`runpodctl doctor`](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-doctor)

# Document: update

Source path: runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-update.mdx

Description: Update runpodctl to the latest release, verify the downloaded binary with its SHA-256 checksum, and confirm the installed version.

# update

Update runpodctl to the latest release, verify the downloaded binary with its SHA-256 checksum, and confirm the installed version.

Update `runpodctl` to the latest version to access new features and bug fixes.

```bash Command
runpodctl update
```

## Description

The `update` command downloads the latest version of `runpodctl` and verifies it against its SHA-256 checksum before replacing the installed binary. Verification always runs. If it fails, the update aborts and leaves your existing binary in place. After updating, verify the installation with [`runpodctl version`](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-version).

The command never prompts, so you can run it from scripts. If you installed `runpodctl` with Homebrew, conda, or pixi, the update goes through that package manager.

To check whether a newer release exists without installing it:

```bash
runpodctl update --check
```

## Flags

**--check (type: bool)**

Report whether a newer release exists, without installing it.

## Related commands

- [`runpodctl version`](https://docs.runpod.io/runpodctl/reference/runpodctl-version)

# Document: API v2

Source path: api-reference-v2/overview.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/api-reference-v2/overview.mdx
Canonical documentation: https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/overview
Description: Manage Runpod Pods, Serverless endpoints, Clusters, storage, templates, billing, and account resources programmatically with the REST API v2.

# API v2

Manage Runpod Pods, Serverless endpoints, Clusters, storage, templates, billing, and account resources programmatically with the REST API v2.

The Runpod REST API v2 provides programmatic access to your Runpod resources over standard HTTP. Use it to create and manage Pods, query Serverless endpoints, provision storage, and retrieve billing data — without using the console.

> **Note**
>
> REST API v1 is deprecated and no longer available.
>
> If you have an existing REST v1 or GraphQL integration, run `/runpod:migrate` with the [Runpod skills plugin](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/agent-skills#migrate-an-existing-integration) installed in your coding agent to migrate it to v2 automatically. See the [migration guide](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/migrate-from-v1) for details.

## Base URL

```
https://api.runpod.io/v2
```

The Runpod REST API v2 provides programmatic access to all Runpod compute resources. Integrate GPU infrastructure into your applications, workflows, and automation systems.

## Available resources

- **Pods**: Create and manage persistent GPU instances for development, training, and long-running workloads.
- **Serverless**: Deploy and scale containerized applications with autoscaling and job monitoring.
- **Templates**: Save and reuse Pod and endpoint configurations.
- **Network volumes**: Create persistent storage attachable to multiple resources.
- **Container registry auth**: Connect to private Docker registries.
- **Catalog**: Browse available GPU types, CPU types, and data centers.
- **Billing**: Access usage metrics and billing information.

## Authentication

All requests require a [Runpod API key](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/credentials) in the request headers. The API uses standard HTTP methods and returns JSON responses.

## Rate limits

The API limits how many requests each user can send per minute, hour, and day. Responses include `RateLimit` headers that report your remaining quota, and requests over the limit return `429 Too Many Requests`. To learn how to read these headers and build a client that handles them, see [Rate limits](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/rate-limits).

## OpenAPI schema

Retrieve the complete OpenAPI specification for client generation, request validation, or tooling integration.

```bash cURL
curl --request GET \
  --url https://api.runpod.io/v2/openapi.json \
```

```python Python
import requests

url = "https://api.runpod.io/v2/openapi.json"
response = requests.get(url)
print(response.json())
```

# Rate limits

Learn how the Runpod REST API v2 limits request rates, read your remaining quota from response headers, and build a client that handles 429 responses.

The Runpod REST API v2 limits how many requests each user can send so that one integration can't degrade the API for everyone else. Limits apply per user across several time windows at once, and every authenticated response tells your client how much quota it has left. A client that reads this information can slow down before it reaches a limit and recover cleanly when it does.

This page covers the management API at `https://api.runpod.io/v2`. Requests to Serverless endpoints (`https://api.runpod.ai/v2/ENDPOINT_ID/...`) have separate per-endpoint limits, described in [Send API requests](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/send-requests#rate-limits).

## How limits work

Each user has a quota for three windows: `minute`, `hour`, and `day`. A request counts against all three. When any window runs out, the API rejects further requests with `429 Too Many Requests` until that window resets, even if the other windows still have quota left.

## Rate limit headers

Responses to authenticated requests include two headers that follow the [IETF RateLimit header fields draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers/). They're present on successful responses as well as on 429 responses, so your client can track quota before it's rejected. If your responses don't include these headers, your requests aren't subject to these limits.

`RateLimit-Policy` describes the quota for each window. Each entry carries the quota `q` (requests allowed) and the window length `w` in seconds:

```text
RateLimit-Policy: "minute";q=60;w=60, "hour";q=3000;w=3600, "day";q=50000;w=86400
```

`RateLimit` describes the live state of each window. Each entry carries the remaining request count `r` and the seconds `t` until the window resets:

```text
RateLimit: "minute";r=0;t=12, "hour";r=2800;t=1812, "day";r=49500;t=45012
```

The quota values on this page are illustrative, not the limits that apply to your account. Read your actual quotas from the `RateLimit-Policy` header on your own responses, and don't hardcode them in your client.

## 429 responses

When your client exceeds a window, the API returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header that gives the number of seconds to wait, plus the `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` headers. The body uses the same `application/problem+json` format as other v2 errors, and `detail` names the window you exceeded:

```http
HTTP/2 429
Content-Type: application/problem+json
Retry-After: 12
RateLimit: "minute";r=0;t=12, "hour";r=2800;t=1812, "day";r=49500;t=45012

{
  "title": "Too Many Requests",
  "status": 429,
  "detail": "rate limit exceeded for the minute window"
}
```

## Build a client that respects limits

Design your integration to treat a 429 as an expected signal rather than a failure:

- Wait for the number of seconds in `Retry-After` before retrying. Retrying sooner returns another 429.
- Watch the `RateLimit` header and slow down when `r` for any window gets close to zero, instead of waiting for a 429.
- Cap the number of retries, and surface an error once the cap is reached.
- Add random jitter to retry delays so that multiple workers or processes that were rejected together don't retry at the same moment.
- Reduce request volume where you can. For example, list resources once and reuse the result instead of fetching each resource in a loop. Cache data that changes rarely, such as the [catalog](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-gpu-types).
- Share one rate-limit-aware client across your code. Quotas are per user, so separate processes using the same API key draw from the same quota.

For errors other than 429, retry only when a retry is safe. Server errors (`5xx`) and network timeouts are usually transient, so retrying `GET` requests with exponential backoff is safe. A `POST` that creates a resource, such as a Pod, may have succeeded even though your client didn't receive the response. Before retrying it, list your resources to check whether the first attempt went through, or you may create a duplicate. Don't retry other `4xx` errors without changing the request, because they won't succeed on their own.

### Example

The following Python client honors `Retry-After` on 429 responses and pauses when the minute window is almost empty. It also retries transient errors on `GET` requests with exponential backoff and jitter. It requires the `requests` package and a `RUNPOD_API_KEY` environment variable.

```python
import os
import random
import re
import time

import requests

BASE_URL = "https://api.runpod.io/v2"
MAX_RETRIES = 5
RETRYABLE_STATUSES = {500, 502, 503, 504}

session = requests.Session()
session.headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {os.environ['RUNPOD_API_KEY']}"


def seconds_until_reset(ratelimit_header, window="minute", threshold=1):
    """Return how long to pause if the given window is almost exhausted."""
    match = re.search(rf'"{window}";r=(\d+);t=(\d+)', ratelimit_header or "")
    if match and int(match.group(1)) < threshold:
        return int(match.group(2))
    return 0


def request(method, path, **kwargs):
    for attempt in range(MAX_RETRIES):
        try:
            response = session.request(method, f"{BASE_URL}{path}", timeout=30, **kwargs)
        except (requests.ConnectionError, requests.Timeout):
            # The request may have reached the server. Only retry methods that are safe to repeat.
            if method != "GET" or attempt == MAX_RETRIES - 1:
                raise
            time.sleep(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1))
            continue

        if response.status_code == 429:
            # Wait as long as the API asks, plus jitter so parallel clients spread out.
            time.sleep(int(response.headers.get("Retry-After", 2**attempt)) + random.uniform(0, 1))
            continue

        if response.status_code in RETRYABLE_STATUSES and method == "GET":
            time.sleep(2**attempt + random.uniform(0, 1))
            continue

        response.raise_for_status()

        # Slow down before the next request if this window is nearly used up.
        time.sleep(seconds_until_reset(response.headers.get("RateLimit")))
        return response.json() if response.content else None

    raise RuntimeError(f"{method} {path} failed after {MAX_RETRIES} attempts")


pods = request("GET", "/pods")
print(pods)
```

The `request` function sends every call through one shared session and handles each outcome differently:

- A 429 response waits for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`, plus up to one second of jitter, and then retries. If the header is missing, the client falls back to exponential backoff.
- A network error or a `5xx` response is retried with exponential backoff only for `GET` requests. Other methods raise the error immediately, because a `POST` that timed out may already have created a resource.
- A successful response is passed to `seconds_until_reset`, which reads the `minute` entry of the `RateLimit` header. When no requests remain in that window, the client sleeps until the window resets, so the next call doesn't receive a 429.

After `MAX_RETRIES` attempts, the client raises an error instead of retrying indefinitely.

# Document: Migrate from API v1

Source path: api-reference-v2/migrate-from-v1.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/api-reference-v2/migrate-from-v1.mdx

Description: Move your integrations from the Runpod REST API v1 to the v2 base URL, endpoints, and request and response shapes.

# Migrate from API v1

Move your integrations from the Runpod REST API v1 to the v2 base URL, endpoints, and request and response shapes.

The Runpod REST API v2 reorganizes resource paths, consolidates Pod lifecycle actions, and standardizes request and response shapes. This guide maps the v1 surface you know to its v2 equivalent so you can update your integrations with confidence.

Read this guide if you have an existing integration built against REST API v1 or the GraphQL API. REST API v1 is deprecated and will be retired on November 15, 2026. Migrate your integrations to v2 before that date. For a complete list of changes that can break a migrated integration, see [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes).

## What changed at a glance

- The base URL moves from `https://rest.runpod.io/v1` to `https://api.runpod.io/v2`. Update every request to the new host and version prefix.

- The OpenAPI schema also moves accordingly, from `https://rest.runpod.io/v1/openapi.json` to `https://api.runpod.io/v2/openapi.json`. Regenerate any client or tooling against the v2 schema.

- Authentication is unchanged. Continue to pass your [Runpod API key](https://docs.runpod.io/get-started/credentials) as an HTTP Bearer token in the `Authorization: Bearer RUNPOD_API_KEY` header. You don't need to change key management or scopes to call v2.

## Breaking changes

Breaking changes between v1 or GraphQL and v2 fall into three classes:

- **Renamed or moved:** the request fails with an error, so you find these right away.
- **Same name, different behavior:** the request succeeds, but the result is different. These can pass your tests, so check each one.
- **Removed:** the capability has no v2 equivalent.

Changes marked **(GraphQL only)** apply only if you're migrating from the GraphQL API.

### Renamed or moved

v2 rejects unknown fields in request bodies. A field that was renamed or moved returns a `422` error that names it, for example `additional properties 'dataCenterId' not allowed`. A renamed path returns a `404`. The [endpoint mapping](#endpoint-mapping) and [request and response shape changes](#request-and-response-shape-changes) sections cover most of these. The following changes aren't covered there:

| Change           | v1 or GraphQL                                        | v2                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CUDA constraints | Top-level `allowedCudaVersions` and `minCudaVersion` | `gpu.allowedCudaVersions` and `gpu.minCudaVersion`. Sending both returns a `400`. |
| GPU host filters | `minRAMPerGPU` and `minVCPUPerGPU`                   | `gpu.minRamPerGpu` and `gpu.minVcpuCountPerGpu`                                   |

> **Warning**
>
> Unknown query parameters don't return an error. For example, `GET /v2/pods?desiredStatus=RUNNING` ignores the filter and returns every Pod. Filter list results in your own code instead.

### Same name, different behavior

These changes pass validation, so they don't return an error:

| Field or path                                 | v1 or GraphQL                                  | v2                                                                     | What to do                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/billing/endpoints`                          | Serverless billing                             | Public Endpoint billing                                                | Use `/v2/billing/serverless` for Serverless billing.                                         |
| `flashboot`                                   | Boolean                                        | `OFF`, `FLASHBOOT`, or `PRIORITY_FLASHBOOT`. Defaults to `OFF`.        | Set it explicitly to keep FlashBoot on.                                                      |
| `ports`                                       | Defaults to `8888/http,22/tcp`                 | No default                                                             | List every port you need, including `22/tcp` for SSH.                                        |
| Pod storage                                   | Every Pod gets a 20 GB volume at `/workspace`  | Without `mounts`, the Pod has no persistent storage                    | Add `mounts` to keep data across restarts.                                                   |
| `idleTimeout`                                 | Accepted with any scaler                       | Rejected on queue-based endpoints that scale by request count          | Remove it from those endpoints.                                                              |
| `executionTimeoutMs` → `timeout`              | Set on the endpoint                            | Don't rely on the default value                                        | Set `timeout` explicitly.                                                                    |
| `desiredStatus` → `status`                    | The requested state                            | The actual state, including `PROVISIONING`, `STARTING`, and `ERROR`    | Handle `ERROR` in polling loops.                                                             |
| `dockerStartCmd` → `args`                     | An array of arguments                          | A single string                                                        | Quote arguments that contain spaces, or send the array as `cmd`.                             |
| `dockerEntrypoint` → `entrypoint`             | Separate override                              | Array, stored with `cmd` in `args`                                     | Don't send `args` together with `entrypoint` or `cmd` unless they describe the same command. |
| `templateId`                                  | The resource stays linked to the template      | The template is copied when you create the resource                    | Update each Pod or endpoint directly. Template edits don't reach existing resources.         |
| Pod storage updates                           | `PATCH` with `volumeInGb` or `volumeMountPath` | The mount type is fixed at creation. You can't change or clear mounts. | Create a new Pod to change its storage.                                                      |
| List responses                                | One response with every item                   | Paginated, up to 1,000 items per page                                  | Follow `pagination.nextCursor` until `pagination.hasNextPage` is `false`.                    |
| `env` (GraphQL only)                          | `[{key, value}]`                               | `{"KEY": "value"}`                                                     | Update code that reads environment variables back.                                           |
| `stockStatus` → `availability` (GraphQL only) | `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `None`                | `HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, `LOW`, `NONE`                                        | Update comparisons to uppercase values.                                                      |
| `cloudType` → `cloud` (GraphQL only)          | Accepts `ALL`                                  | `SECURE` or `COMMUNITY`                                                | Choose one, or try one and fall back to the other.                                           |

### Removed

These capabilities have no v2 equivalent:

| Capability                        | v1 or GraphQL                                                                 | v2 alternative                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pod GPU fallback list             | `gpuTypeIds` with several GPU types                                           | A Pod takes one GPU type. Check availability with [List GPU types](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-gpu-types), then retry with the next type in your own code. Serverless endpoints still accept several GPU pools. |
| Pod `reset` action                | `POST /pods/{podId}/reset`                                                    | None. The `action` field accepts `start`, `stop`, `restart`, and `terminate`.                                                                                                                                                            |
| Spot Pods                         | `interruptible`, `podRentInterruptable`, `podBidResume`                       | None.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Savings plans                     | `savingsPlans`, `adjustedCostPerHr`                                           | None.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Country placement                 | `countryCodes`                                                                | Find data centers in those countries with [List GPU types](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-gpu-types), then pass them in `dataCenterIds`.                                                                           |
| Bandwidth and public IP placement | `minDownloadMbps`, `minUploadMbps`, `minDiskBandwidthMBps`, `supportPublicIp` | None.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Server-side list filters          | `desiredStatus`, `includeMachine`, and other query parameters                 | Filter in your own code after reading every page.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Host machine details              | `machineId`, `podHostId`                                                      | `dataCenterId` only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Account balance (GraphQL only)    | `myself { clientBalance }`                                                    | None. Keep using the GraphQL API for this.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Volume encryption flag            | `volumeEncrypted`                                                             | None.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

## Endpoint mapping

Most resources keep the same concept but move to a new path. The following table maps each v1 resource to its v2 path.

| Resource               | v1 path                   | v2 path                       |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Pods                   | `/pods`                   | `/v2/pods`                    |
| Serverless             | `/endpoints`              | `/v2/serverless`              |
| Templates              | `/templates`              | `/v2/templates`               |
| Network volumes        | `/networkvolumes`         | `/v2/network-volumes`         |
| Registries             | `/containerregistryauth`  | `/v2/registries`              |
| Instant Clusters       | No equivalent             | `/v2/clusters`                |
| Pod billing            | `/billing/pods`           | `/v2/billing/pods`            |
| Serverless billing     | `/billing/endpoints`      | `/v2/billing/serverless`      |
| Network volume billing | `/billing/networkvolumes` | `/v2/billing/network-volumes` |

v2 generalizes path parameters: where v1 used resource-specific names such as `{podId}`, `{endpointId}`, `{networkVolumeId}`, `{templateId}`, and `{containerRegistryAuthId}`, v2 uses a single generic `{id}` parameter across resources.

## Consolidated Pod lifecycle

In v1, each Pod state change had its own endpoint: `POST /pods/{podId}/start`, `/stop`, `/reset`, and `/restart`. In v2, these collapse into a single [Pod state transition endpoint](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/pods/trigger-a-pod-state-transition), `POST /v2/pods/{id}/action`, whose request body carries the desired action as `{"action":"start|stop|restart|terminate"}`. Deletion still uses [`DELETE /v2/pods/{id}`](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/pods/terminate-a-pod).

For in-place changes to a Pod, v2 replaces v1's `POST /pods/{podId}/update` with a standard [PATCH request](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/pods/update-a-pod) to `PATCH /v2/pods/{id}`. Serverless follows the same pattern: v2 drops v1's `POST /endpoints/{id}/update` in-place variant in favor of `PATCH /v2/serverless/{id}`.

The following example shows how stopping a Pod changes between versions.

```bash v1
curl --request POST \
  --url https://rest.runpod.io/v1/pods/{podId}/stop \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer RUNPOD_API_KEY'
```

```bash v2
curl --request POST \
  --url https://api.runpod.io/v2/pods/{id}/action \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer RUNPOD_API_KEY' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"action":"stop"}'
```

Instead of targeting a dedicated `/stop` path, v2 sends the same `POST .../action` request for every lifecycle transition and selects the operation with the `action` field in the request body.

## Request and response shape changes

The v2 request and response formats differ from v1. The most impactful changes are nested create bodies, wrapped list responses, and standardized error objects. Full field-by-field mapping is out of scope for this guide; see the linked reference pages for complete schemas.

### Nested create bodies

- In v1, create bodies are flat, with top-level fields such as `gpuCount`, `gpuTypeIds`, `imageName`, `containerDiskInGb`, `volumeInGb`, `env`, and `ports`. The v2 `CreatePodRequest` is nested: `name` and `image` are required, GPU settings live under `gpu: {id, count}`, CPU settings under `cpu`, and storage under `mounts`. The `cloud` field defaults to `SECURE`, and you must set exactly one of `gpu` or `cpu`. See [Create a Pod](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/pods/create-a-pod) for the full request schema.

- Serverless endpoint creation changes more than its path. In v1, `EndpointCreateInput` requires a `templateId`. v2's `CreateEndpointRequest` still supports `templateId`: you can create an endpoint from a template ID, or provide the container details directly with `name`, `image`, and `gpu`. When you create from a template, `image` is optional because the template supplies it. Worker and scaling settings nest under `workers` and `scaling`, replacing v1's flat `workersMin`, `workersMax`, `scalerType`, and `idleTimeout`. See [Create a Serverless endpoint](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/serverless/create-a-serverless-endpoint) for the full schema.

- Templates share the same container-field renames as Pods: v1's `imageName`, `containerDiskInGb`, `isPublic`, and `containerRegistryAuthId` become `image`, `disk`, `public`, and a nested `registry` in v2. See [Create a template](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/templates/create-a-template).

- Network volume creation renames `dataCenterId` to `dataCenter` and adds an optional `type` field for selecting the storage tier (`STANDARD` or `HIGH_PERFORMANCE`). See [Create a network volume](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/network-volumes/create-a-network-volume).

### Wrapped list responses

In v1, list endpoints return a bare JSON array. In v2, list responses wrap the array in an object keyed by the resource name.

```json v1
[
  { "id": "pod-1" },
  { "id": "pod-2" }
]
```

```json v2
{
  "pods": [
    { "id": "pod-1" },
    { "id": "pod-2" }
  ]
}
```

The v2 wrapper key matches the resource: `GET /v2/pods` returns `{"pods":[...]}`, Serverless returns `{"endpoints":[...]}`, templates return `{"templates":[...]}`, network volumes return `{"networkVolumes":[...]}`, and registries return `{"registries":[...]}`. See [List Pods](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/pods/list-pods) for a complete example.

### RFC 9457 error objects

In v1, errors return a simple `{"message":"..."}` object. In v2, errors follow the RFC 9457 problem format with required `title`, `status`, and `detail` fields, plus an optional `errors` array of validation strings.

As in v1, Runpod returns a `403` when a valid API key lacks access to the requested resource—but in v2 that response now uses the problem format shown here.

```json v1
{
  "message": "Pod not found"
}
```

```json v2
{
  "title": "Not Found",
  "status": 404,
  "detail": "The requested Pod does not exist."
}
```

## New in v2

- The v2 API adds capabilities that have no v1 equivalent.

- Catalog endpoints let you browse available compute without provisioning it: `GET /v2/catalog/gpus` and `/gpus/{id}`, `/cpus` and `/cpus/{id}`, and `/datacenters` and `/datacenters/{id}`. See [List GPU types](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-gpu-types).

- Pod log streaming exposes `GET /v2/pods/{id}/logs` so you can follow a Pod's output over the API. See [Stream Pod logs](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/pods/stream-pod-logs).

- Serverless observability adds worker and release visibility through `GET /v2/serverless/{id}/workers`, `/workers/{workerId}/logs`, and `/releases`. See [List Serverless endpoint workers](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/serverless/list-serverless-endpoint-workers), [Stream Serverless worker logs](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/serverless/stream-serverless-worker-logs), and [List Serverless endpoint releases](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/serverless/list-serverless-endpoint-releases).

- Registry ECR delegations manage delegated registry access with `GET` and `POST /v2/registries/delegations` and `DELETE /v2/registries/delegations/{id}`. These endpoints aren't yet covered by a dedicated reference page during beta; consult the [v2 OpenAPI schema](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/overview) for their request and response formats.

- Expanded billing adds an aggregated history at `GET /v2/billing` alongside Serverless, Public Endpoint, and Instant Clusters histories, going beyond v1's Pods, endpoints, and network volume breakdowns. See [Get aggregated billing history](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/billing/get-aggregated-billing-history).

Description: Retrieve your current Runpod organization.

# Get Your Current Organization

Retrieve your current Runpod organization.

`GET /v2/organization`

**Get your current organization**

Returns the authenticated caller's current organization. Organization context comes from the caller's membership; no selector is required. Returns 404 when the caller does not belong to an organization, or 403 when organizations are unavailable to the caller.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object): The authenticated caller's current organization. Its role and groups are the caller's membership in this organization.
      - `id` (required; string): Organization ID.
      - `name` (required; string): Organization name.
      - `role` (required; object): An organization role, by ID and display name.
        - `id` (required; string): Role ID. A built-in role's ID is `builtin:` followed by its key; a custom role carries its own ID.
        - `type` (required; string; enum: `builtin`, `custom`): Who defines the role. `builtin` roles are Runpod's: `builtin:admin`, `builtin:dev`, `builtin:billing` and `builtin:basic`. A `custom` role is one the organization defined, under its own ID.
        - `name` (required; string): The role's display name: `Admin`, `Developer`, `Billing` or `Contributor` for a built-in role, or a custom role's own name. A custom role that has since been deleted reads as `Contributor` while `id` keeps its own ID.
      - `groups` (required; array): The caller's groups in this organization. Empty when the caller belongs to no groups.
        - `items` (object): An organization group, by ID and name.
          - `id` (required; string): Group ID.
          - `name` (required; string): Group name.
    - Example `organization`: `{"id":"org_id_abc_123","name":"my-org","role":{"id":"builtin:dev","type":"builtin","name":"Developer"},"groups":[{"id":"group_id_abc_123","name":"Engineering"}]}`
- `401`: Authentication failed because the bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or invalid.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `missingBearerToken`: `{"title":"Unauthorized","status":401,"detail":"missing bearer token"}`
- `403`: The bearer token is valid, but it does not grant access to the requested resource or action.
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.

**List groups in your current organization**

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `cursor` (query; string; minimum length: `1`): Opaque resume cursor — pass the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` through verbatim; omit for the first page. A cursor is only valid for the operation and parameters that issued it; a malformed or foreign cursor is rejected with 422.
  - Example: `Y3JlYXRlZEF0PTE3NDg3ODA0MDA`
- `limit` (query; integer; minimum: `1`; maximum: `100`): Page size, 1–100. Defaults to 100 when omitted.
  - Example: `50`

# List Members Of A Group

List members of a group with cursor pagination.

`GET /v2/organization/groups/{id}/members`

**List members of a group**

Members are ordered newest first by membership creation time, with a unique upstream tie-breaker. Returns 404 when the group does not exist in the current organization, or when the caller does not belong to an organization.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string; minimum length: `1`): Group ID.
- `cursor` (query; string; minimum length: `1`): Opaque resume cursor — pass the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` through verbatim; omit for the first page. A cursor is only valid for the operation and parameters that issued it; a malformed or foreign cursor is rejected with 422.
  - Example: `Y3JlYXRlZEF0PTE3NDg3ODA0MDA`
- `limit` (query; integer; minimum: `1`; maximum: `100`): Page size, 1–100. Defaults to 100 when omitted.
  - Example: `50`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object)

        - `items` (object): A member of the group. `id` is the member's user ID.
          - `id` (required; string): User ID.
          - `email` (required; nullable): The member's email address. Null for an account that has none.
      - `pagination` (required; object): Cursor-pagination metadata, uniform across list endpoints. Every response carries it: follow `nextCursor` while `hasNextPage` is true to walk the full result set.

# Remove An Organization Member

Remove a member from your organization by user ID.

`DELETE /v2/organization/users/{id}`

**Remove an organization member**

Removes one member from the authenticated caller's organization by user ID. Their group memberships end and the API keys attributed to them within the organization are revoked; the resources they created stay with the organization. Removing another member requires the organization's member-removal capability, which the built-in admin role holds; any member can remove themselves. The organization keeps at least one member with the built-in admin role, so removing the last one returns 409. A user who is not a member, including one from another organization, returns 404. A member without the capability removing someone else, a caller outside an organization, and a caller for whom organizations are unavailable receive 403.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string): User identifier
  - Example: `user_id_abc_123`

# Update An Organization Member

Change a member's role, replace their groups, or both, by user ID.

`PATCH /v2/organization/users/{id}`

**Update an organization member**

Changes one member of the authenticated caller's organization by user ID: assigns a role, replaces their set of groups, or both, applied together or not at all. Send at least one field; an omitted field is left as it is, and an empty `groups` list removes the member from every group. Updating members requires the organization's member-management capability, which the built-in admin role holds; other members, and callers outside an organization, receive 403, as does a caller for whom organizations are unavailable. Returns 403 when the caller changes their own role or assigns a role granting a capability the caller lacks; 409 when the change would leave the organization without a member in the built-in admin role; and 404 when the user is not a member or the role or a group is unknown to the organization, with the detail naming which.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string): User identifier
  - Example: `user_id_abc_123`

**Request body** (required)

- Media type: `application/json`
  - Schema (object): Changes to a member. Send `role`, `groups`, or both; an omitted field is left as it is.
    - `role` (object): An organization role to assign, by ID.
      - `id` (required; string; minimum length: `1`): Role ID, as reported on a member or an invite: `builtin:admin`, `builtin:dev`, `builtin:billing`, `builtin:basic`, or a custom role's own ID.
    - `groups` (array; unique items): The member's groups after the change: the whole set, by ID. An empty list removes the member from every group.
      - `items` (object): An organization group, by ID.
        - `id` (required; string; minimum length: `1`): Group ID.
  - Example `role`: `{"role":{"id":"builtin:dev"}}`
  - Example `groups`: `{"groups":[{"id":"group_id_abc_123"}]}`
  - Example `clearGroups`: `{"groups":[]}`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object): A member of the caller's organization. `id` is the member's user ID.
      - `id` (required; string): User ID.
      - `email` (required; nullable): The member's email address. Null for an account that has none.
      - `role` (required; object): An organization role, by ID and display name.
        - `id` (required; string): Role ID. A built-in role's ID is `builtin:` followed by its key; a custom role carries its own ID.
        - `type` (required; string; enum: `builtin`, `custom`): Who defines the role. `builtin` roles are Runpod's: `builtin:admin`, `builtin:dev`, `builtin:billing` and `builtin:basic`. A `custom` role is one the organization defined, under its own ID.
        - `name` (required; string): The role's display name: `Admin`, `Developer`, `Billing` or `Contributor` for a built-in role, or a custom role's own name. A custom role that has since been deleted reads as `Contributor` while `id` keeps its own ID.
      - `groups` (required; array): The groups the member belongs to, by name.
        - `items` (object): An organization group, by ID and name.
          - `id` (required; string): Group ID.
          - `name` (required; string): Group name.
    - Example `user`: `{"id":"user_id_abc_123","email":"member@example.com","role":{"id":"builtin:dev","type":"builtin","name":"Developer"},"groups":[{"id":"group_id_abc_123","name":"Engineering"}]}`
- `400`: The request could not be processed because it is malformed or conflicts with request rules.
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `badRequest`: `{"title":"Bad Request","status":400,"detail":"request could not be processed"}`
- `401`: Authentication failed because the bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or invalid.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation

# List Pending Organization Invites

List the pending invitations to your organization.

`GET /v2/organization/invites`

**List pending organization invites**

Returns the pending invitations to the authenticated caller's organization, newest first. Only unexpired invites are pending: an invite leaves the list once it is accepted, revoked or expired. The list is complete and takes no pagination parameters, because an organization's pending invites are capped. Reading invites requires the organization's invite-management capability, which the built-in admin role holds; other members receive 403. Returns 404 when the caller does not belong to an organization, or 403 when organizations are unavailable to the caller.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.

  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `invites` (required; array): Pending invites, newest first.
        - `items` (object): A pending invitation to join the caller's organization. An invite stops being listed once it is accepted, revoked or expired.

          - `email` (required; string): Email address the invitation was sent to. The invitee accepts by signing in with a verified account on this address.

            - `id` (required; string): Role ID. A built-in role's ID is `builtin:` followed by its key; a custom role carries its own ID.

            - `name` (required; string): The role's display name: `Admin`, `Developer`, `Billing` or `Contributor` for a built-in role, or a custom role's own name. A custom role that has since been deleted reads as `Contributor` while `id` keeps its own ID.
          - `createdAt` (required; string; format: date-time): When the invite was sent.
          - `expiresAt` (required; string; format: date-time): When the invite can no longer be accepted.
    - Example `invites`: `{"invites":[{"id":"invite_id_abc_123","email":"new-member@example.com","role":{"id":"builtin:dev","type":"builtin","name":"Developer"},"createdAt":"2026-10-01T09:00:00Z","expiresAt":"2026-10-15T09:00:00Z"}]}`

# Invite A User To Your Organization

Invite a user to your organization by email and choose the role they receive on joining.

`POST /v2/organization/invites`

**Invite a user to your organization**

Sends an invitation to join the authenticated caller's organization and returns the pending invite; `expiresAt` is when it lapses. The invitee receives an email carrying the acceptance link, which is never returned here. Returns 409 when the address already belongs to a member or to a pending invite, or when the organization has reached its pending-invite limit; 404 when the role is unknown to the organization; and 403 when the caller does not hold every capability the role grants. Inviting requires the organization's invite-management capability, which the built-in admin role holds; other members, and callers outside an organization, receive 403, as does a caller for whom organizations are unavailable.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Request body** (required)

- Media type: `application/json`
  - Schema (object)
    - `email` (required; string; format: email; minimum length: `1`; maximum length: `254`): Address to invite, stored lowercased. The invitee accepts by signing in with a verified account on this address.
    - `role` (required; object): An organization role to assign, by ID.
      - `id` (required; string; minimum length: `1`): Role ID, as reported on a member or an invite: `builtin:admin`, `builtin:dev`, `builtin:billing`, `builtin:basic`, or a custom role's own ID.
  - Example `invite`: `{"email":"new-member@example.com","role":{"id":"builtin:dev"}}`

**Responses**

      - `createdAt` (required; string; format: date-time): When the invite was sent.
      - `expiresAt` (required; string; format: date-time): When the invite can no longer be accepted.
    - Example `invite`: `{"id":"invite_id_abc_123","email":"new-member@example.com","role":{"id":"builtin:dev","type":"builtin","name":"Developer"},"createdAt":"2026-10-01T09:00:00Z","expiresAt":"2026-10-15T09:00:00Z"}`

# Create A Custom Organization Role

Create a custom role in your organization from a name and the capabilities it grants.

`POST /v2/organization/roles`

**Create a custom organization role**

Creates a custom role in the authenticated caller's organization and returns it. Returns 409 when the organization already has a role with this name or has reached its custom-role limit; 422 when a capability is unknown or the name is reserved; and 403 when the caller does not hold every capability the role grants. Creating roles requires the organization's role-management capability, which the built-in admin role holds; other members, and callers outside an organization, receive 403, as does a caller for whom organizations are unavailable.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Request body** (required)

- Media type: `application/json`
  - Schema (object)
    - `name` (required; string; minimum length: `1`; maximum length: `191`; pattern: `[^\t-\r  - ]`): Display name, 1–191 characters with at least one non-whitespace character. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed. It must be unique within the organization and cannot be a built-in role's name.
    - `capabilities` (required; array; minimum items: `1`; unique items): What the role grants, as `FAMILY:VERB` capabilities from `GET /v2/organization/roles/capabilities`. The caller must hold every capability it lists.
      - `items` (string; pattern: `^[A-Z0-9_]+:[A-Z0-9_]+$`)
  - Example `role`: `{"name":"Pod viewer","capabilities":["POD:VIEW"]}`

**Responses**
