          - `mounts` (required): Storage mounts attached to a pod. `persistent` (the volume disk) is mutually exclusive with both `network` and `global` (enforced at the handler with 400 if combined). A pod takes up to 4 network volumes and 1 global volume. Every network volume must be in the pod's data center, each volume may be listed once, and mount paths must not overlap; a request that breaks one of these is rejected. To change a pod's mounts after creation, see `UpdatePodMounts`.
            - allOf:
              - `variant 1` (object): Shared base type for all resources that mount storage volumes. `persistent` and `network` cannot both be set (rejected with 400). Each resource that uses this type sets its own limit on network volumes.
                - `persistent` (object): Host-local persistent storage. Pinned to the pod's host machine — data does not survive a host failure. Disallowed on CPU pods. Mutually exclusive with NetworkMount. Deprecated: prefer NetworkMount for any data you cannot recreate.
                  - `size` (required; integer; minimum: `10`): Host-local persistent storage in GB. Minimum 10 GB.

# Terminate A Pod

Permanently terminate a Runpod Pod, release its compute, and understand what happens to persistent mounts, network volumes, and Cluster members.

`DELETE /v2/pods/{id}`

**Terminate a pod**

Permanently terminates and deletes a pod. This is irreversible:
compute is released, any `mounts.persistent` host-local storage is
destroyed with it (a `mounts.network` volume is only detached — the
volume itself is not deleted), and the pod no longer appears in
`listPods`.

Pods that belong to a Cluster cannot be terminated here — delete the
cluster via `DELETE /v2/clusters/{id}`.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string): Pod identifier
  - Example: `pod_abc123`

**Responses**

- `204`: Deleted. Response has no body.
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.

  - Media type: `application/problem+json`

      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation

        - `items` (string)
    - Example `missingBearerToken`: `{"title":"Unauthorized","status":401,"detail":"missing bearer token"}`
- `403`: The bearer token is valid, but it does not grant access to the requested resource or action.

      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `insufficientAccess`: `{"title":"Forbidden","status":403,"detail":"access denied"}`

# Document: Update A Pod

Source path: api-reference-v2/pods/update-a-pod.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/api-reference-v2/pods/update-a-pod.mdx
Canonical documentation: https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/pods/update-a-pod
Description: Update selected settings on an existing Runpod Pod while preserving omitted fields, with guidance on mutable fields and restart behavior.

# Update A Pod

Update selected settings on an existing Runpod Pod while preserving omitted fields, with guidance on mutable fields and restart behavior.

`PATCH /v2/pods/{id}`

**Update a pod**

Partially updates a pod's configuration. This is a PATCH: only the
fields present in the body are changed, and omitted fields are left
untouched. Use empty values only when you explicitly mean to clear a
field (for example, set `registry` to `null` or set `ports` to `[]`).
See `UpdatePodRequest` for the full body.

Mutable fields: `name`, `image`, `args`, `disk`, `ports`, `env`,
`registry`, `mounts`, `locked`, and `globalNetworking`. Some changes
apply immediately while others (e.g. `globalNetworking`) take effect
on the pod's next start/restart, as noted on the individual fields.

Volumes can be mounted, moved, or unmounted after creation through
`mounts`, one entry per volume; see `UpdatePodMounts` for the rules.

Pods that belong to a Cluster cannot be updated here — manage them
through `/v2/clusters/{id}`.

Returns `200` with the full updated pod.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string): Pod identifier
  - Example: `pod_abc123`

**Request body** (required)

- Media type: `application/json`
  - Schema
    - allOf:
      - `variant 1`: Reusable container configuration shared across templates, pods, serverless endpoints, and clusters. Adding a field here automatically propagates to all of them.
        - allOf:
          - `variant 1` (object): Container configuration universal to every containerized resource. ContainerConfig composes it and adds `registry`; resources compose ContainerConfig.
            - `args` (string): The container's command, as a single raw string. This is the field `entrypoint` and `cmd` encode into, exposed in its stored form. Two shapes are accepted. A bare shell string is treated as CMD and split into arguments, which is what the console's "Container start command" field writes. A JSON object of the form `{"entrypoint":[...],"cmd":[...]}` sets either or both explicitly. Responses always return both representations: `args` exactly as stored, plus the deconstructed `entrypoint` and `cmd`. Supplying `args` together with `entrypoint` or `cmd` is allowed only when they describe the same command, so a read-modify-write client can send back everything it received. Send `""` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
            - `cmd` (array): Container CMD in exec form. When the image defines an ENTRYPOINT, this is the argument list passed to it. Encoded into the `args` field; supplying both is allowed only when they describe the same command. Send `[]` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
              - `items` (string)
            - `entrypoint` (array): Container ENTRYPOINT in exec form, overriding the image's own. Encoded into `args` field; supplying both is allowed only when they describe the same command. Send `[]` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
              - `items` (string)
            - `disk` (integer; minimum: `1`): Container disk in GB (ephemeral, wiped on restart)
            - `env` (object): Environment variables as key-value pairs
              - `additional properties` (string)
            - `image` (string): Docker image reference
            - `ports` (array): Exposed ports, formatted as port/protocol
              - `items` (string)
          - `variant 2` (object)
            - `registry` (nullable): Container registry credential ID for a private image: one of your credentials from `/v2/registries`. Leave it unset for a private Amazon ECR image. Runpod pulls those with an ECR delegation (`/v2/registries/delegations`) matched to the image's account, region and repository at pull time, so there is no delegation ID to pass here (a delegation ID is not a credential ID). A credential set here is used instead of any delegation.
      - `variant 2` (object)
        - `globalNetworking` (boolean): Enable (true) or disable (false) global networking. Takes effect on the next pod start/restart, not live. Requires an NVIDIA GPU and a global-networking-enabled data center. See `GET /v2/catalog/datacenters` (`globalNetwork`) for eligible data centers.
        - `locked` (boolean): Lock the pod (true) or unlock it (false). Locked pods cannot be stopped or reset.
        - `mounts` (object): Changes to a pod's mounts. Each entry names one volume by `volumeId` and changes only that volume; volumes that are not listed, and kinds that are omitted, are left as they are. Omitting `mounts` or sending `{}` changes nothing. - A listed volume the pod does not have is mounted at `path`. - A listed volume the pod already has moves to `path` (or stays put when `path` is omitted). - `remove: true` unmounts the volume. It cannot be combined with `path`, and the volume must be mounted on the pod. - To swap a volume, remove the old one and add the new one in the same request. Limits are checked against the pod as it would be after the request and rejected with 400: at most 4 network volumes and 1 global volume, and a volume disk cannot share a pod with network or global volumes. A volume disk can be added to a pod that has no volumes mounted (or unmounts them all in the same request), and it can only grow. Removing a volume disk is not supported yet.
          - `persistent` (object): Adds the pod's volume disk, grows it, or moves it. Adding a disk requires `size`; on a pod that already has one, omitted fields are left as they are. Not available on CPU pods.
            - `size` (integer; minimum: `10`): Volume disk size in GB. Can only grow; a smaller size than the current one is rejected with 400.
            - `path` (string; minimum length: `1`): Mount path inside the container.
            - `remove` (boolean): Removes the volume disk. Not supported yet: `remove: true` is rejected with 400.
          - `network` (array; maximum items: `8`): Network volumes to mount, move, or unmount. Up to 8 entries, so a request can unmount 4 volumes and mount 4 others; the pod can still hold at most 4 afterwards.
            - `items` (object): Mounts, moves, or unmounts one network volume. Mounting a volume the pod does not have requires `path`.
              - `volumeId` (required; string): ID of an existing NetworkVolume in the same data center as the pod.
              - `path` (string; minimum length: `1`): Mount path inside the container. Required when mounting; optional when moving a mounted volume.
              - `remove` (boolean): Unmount the volume. Cannot be combined with `path`.
          - `global` (array; maximum items: `2`): Global volumes to mount, move, or unmount. Up to 2 entries, so a request can swap the global volume; the pod can still hold at most 1 afterwards.
            - `items` (object): Mounts, moves, or unmounts the pod's global volume.
              - `volumeId` (required; string): ID of an existing GlobalVolume.
              - `path` (string; minimum length: `1`): Mount path inside the container. Optional; when mounting, a default is chosen for you if omitted.
              - `remove` (boolean): Unmount the volume. Cannot be combined with `path`.
        - `name` (string; minimum length: `1`)
        - `templateId` (string): ID of a pod template whose container settings are applied as if they were provided in this PATCH body (image, args, disk, ports, env, registry — mounts are not applied on update). Explicit body fields override the template's; `env` merges template and body per key (body wins) and, per PATCH semantics, replaces the pod's env. One-time application — no link to the template is retained. Must be one of your templates or a public template (unknown or inaccessible ID → 404); must not be a serverless template (→ 422).
  - Example `renamePod`: `{"name":"renamed-training-pod"}`
  - Example `mountNetworkVolume`: `{"mounts":{"network":[{"volumeId":"vol_abc","path":"/datasets"}]}}`
  - Example `swapNetworkVolume`: `{"mounts":{"network":[{"volumeId":"vol_xyz","remove":true},{"volumeId":"vol_abc","path":"/workspace"}]}}`
  - Example `unmountNetworkVolume`: `{"mounts":{"network":[{"volumeId":"vol_xyz","remove":true}]}}`

              - `args` (string): The container's command, as a single raw string. This is the field `entrypoint` and `cmd` encode into, exposed in its stored form. Two shapes are accepted. A bare shell string is treated as CMD and split into arguments, which is what the console's "Container start command" field writes. A JSON object of the form `{"entrypoint":[...],"cmd":[...]}` sets either or both explicitly. Responses always return both representations: `args` exactly as stored, plus the deconstructed `entrypoint` and `cmd`. Supplying `args` together with `entrypoint` or `cmd` is allowed only when they describe the same command, so a read-modify-write client can send back everything it received. Send `""` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.

Description: Stream a Runpod Pod's container and system logs in real time as Server-Sent Events, with resumable reconnects via Last-Event-ID.

# Stream Pod Logs

Stream a Runpod Pod's container and system logs in real time as Server-Sent Events, with resumable reconnects via Last-Event-ID.

`GET /v2/pods/{id}/logs`

**Stream pod logs**

Streams pod logs as Server-Sent Events. The `source` query parameter
selects which log source to include.

The SSE `data` payload shape is:
`{ "source": "container", "line": "...", "ts": "..." }`.
Log-event `id` values are the event `ts` timestamp so
browser/EventSource reconnects can resume with `Last-Event-ID`.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string): Pod identifier
  - Example: `pod_abc123`
- `source` (query; string; enum: `container`, `system`): Log source to stream. Omit to include both container and system logs.
- `tail` (query; integer; default: `100`; minimum: `0`; maximum: `5000`): Number of historical lines to backfill before streaming. Defaults to 100 when omitted; set `0` to stream live with no backfill. Maximum 5000. Ignored when `since` or `Last-Event-ID` is provided — the resume cursor drives the backfill instead.
- `since` (query; string; format: date-time): RFC3339 timestamp to resume from. Ignored when `Last-Event-ID` is provided. When set, the stream resumes from this point and `tail` is ignored.
- `Last-Event-ID` (header; string; format: date-time): SSE reconnect cursor — a timestamp emitted by this endpoint. Takes precedence over `since` and `tail`: when present, the stream resumes from this point. Sent automatically by EventSource on reconnect.

**Responses**

- `200`: Pod log event stream
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `Cache-Control` (string): Always `no-cache` for SSE responses.
  - Header `Connection` (string): Always `keep-alive` to hold the SSE stream open.
  - Header `X-Accel-Buffering` (string): Always `no` to disable proxy buffering of the SSE stream.
  - Media type: `text/event-stream`
    - Schema (string): Server-Sent Events stream. Each event includes an `id:` line and a JSON `data:` payload with `source`, `line`, and `ts` fields.
    - Example `logLine`: `id: 2026-06-01T12:02:03Z/000000000001 data: {"ts":"2026-06-01T12:02:03Z","source":"container","line":"Model loaded."}`
- `401`: Authentication failed because the bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or invalid.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `missingBearerToken`: `{"title":"Unauthorized","status":401,"detail":"missing bearer token"}`
- `403`: The bearer token is valid, but it does not grant access to the requested resource or action.
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `insufficientAccess`: `{"title":"Forbidden","status":403,"detail":"access denied"}`
- `404`: The requested resource was not found or is not accessible to the caller.
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `notFound`: `{"title":"Not Found","status":404,"detail":"resource not found"}`

# Document: Trigger A Pod State Transition

Source path: api-reference-v2/pods/trigger-a-pod-state-transition.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/api-reference-v2/pods/trigger-a-pod-state-transition.mdx

Description: Start, stop, or restart a Runpod Pod by sending a supported state transition action and retrieving the Pod's updated lifecycle state.

# Trigger A Pod State Transition

Start, stop, or restart a Runpod Pod by sending a supported state transition action and retrieving the Pod's updated lifecycle state.

`POST /v2/pods/{id}/action`

**Trigger a pod state transition**

Triggers a state transition on a pod. Send a JSON body with a single
`action` field, e.g. `{ "action": "stop" }`.

Valid actions:

- `start`     — boot a stopped pod (`EXITED` or `ERROR`) back toward
  `RUNNING`.
- `stop`      — stop a running or provisioning pod, releasing GPU/CPU
  compute while keeping its disk. The pod moves to `EXITED`.
- `restart`   — restart a `RUNNING` pod's container in place.
- `terminate` — permanently delete the pod and release its resources
  (equivalent to `deletePod`).

Which actions are valid depends on the pod's current status, and the
currently permitted set is published in the pod's `actions` field:
`RUNNING` allows `stop`/`restart`/`terminate`; `EXITED` and `ERROR`
allow `start`/`terminate`; `PROVISIONING` and `STARTING` allow
`stop`/`terminate`.

`start`, `stop`, and `restart` return `200` with the updated pod.
`terminate` returns `204` with no body. Requesting an action that is
not valid for the pod's current status returns `409`.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string)
  - Example: `pod_abc123`

**Request body** (required)

- Media type: `application/json`
  - Schema (object)
    - `action` (required; string; enum: `start`, `stop`, `restart`, `terminate`): State transition to trigger on a pod.
  - Example `startPod`: `{"action":"start"}`

Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/api-reference-v2/pods/run-a-command-in-a-pod.mdx

Description: Run one command inside a running Runpod Pod's container and get its stdout, stderr, and exit code back, with no SSH setup.

# Run A Command In A Pod

Run one command inside a running Runpod Pod's container and get its stdout, stderr, and exit code back, with no SSH setup.

`POST /v2/pods/{id}/exec`

**Run a command in a pod**

Runs one command inside the pod's container and returns its stdout,
stderr and exit code once it finishes. No SSH key, public IP or exposed
port is needed, and it works with any image.

`command` is an argv array, run directly and never through a shell. For
pipes, redirects or globbing pass `["sh", "-c", "..."]`.

A command that exits non-zero is a result, not an error: the call
answers `200` with `exitCode` set. A command still running after
`timeoutSeconds` (1-25, default 20) answers `200` with
`timedOut: true` and a null `exitCode`. `timedOut` means the call
stopped waiting, not that the command was stopped: it may keep
running in the container.

`stdout` and `stderr` are each capped at 1 MiB. Output past the cap is
cut and `truncated` is `true`.

The pod must be running with its container up, otherwise this answers
`409`; while the container is still starting, the `409` carries
`Retry-After`. A pod whose machine has not been updated for exec yet
answers `503` with `Retry-After`.

A caller whose team or organization role lacks the Terminal permission
gets `403`.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string): Pod identifier
  - Example: `pod_abc123`

**Request body** (required)

- Media type: `application/json`
  - Schema (object)
    - `command` (required; array; minimum items: `1`; maximum items: `256`): Command to run, as an argv array of 1-256 arguments of at most 4096 characters each. It is run directly, never through a shell; for pipes, redirects or globbing pass `["sh", "-c", "..."]`. The first element, the program, must contain a non-whitespace character; later arguments may be empty. No argument may contain a NUL character.
      - `items` (string; maximum length: `4096`; pattern: `^[^\x00]*$`)
    - `timeoutSeconds` (integer; default: `20`; minimum: `1`; maximum: `25`): How long the call waits for the command to finish, in seconds. A command still running at this point returns with `timedOut: true`.
    - `cwd` (string; maximum length: `1024`; pattern: `^/[^\x00-\x1f\x7f]*$`): Absolute working directory for the command, at most 1024 characters and without control characters. Defaults to the image's `WORKDIR`.
    - `env` (object): Up to 64 environment variables added to the container's environment for this command only. A name is 1-256 characters and must not contain `=` or a NUL character; a value is at most 16384 characters and must not contain a NUL character.
      - `additional properties` (string; maximum length: `16384`; pattern: `^[^\x00]*$`)
  - Example `gpuQuery`: `{"command":["nvidia-smi","--query-gpu=name,memory.used","--format=csv"],"timeoutSeconds":10}`
  - Example `failingInstall`: `{"command":["sh","-c","pip install -q nosuchpackage"],"cwd":"/workspace"}`
  - Example `timeout`: `{"command":["sleep","120"],"timeoutSeconds":5}`

**Responses**

- `200`: The command finished or the call stopped waiting for it. A non-zero `exitCode` is a result, not an error.
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `stdout` (required; string): The command's standard output, as UTF-8 with invalid bytes replaced. Capped at 1 MiB; see `truncated`.
      - `stderr` (required; string): The command's standard error, as UTF-8 with invalid bytes replaced. Capped at 1 MiB; see `truncated`.
      - `exitCode` (required; nullable): The command's exit code. A non-zero code is a result, not an error. Null only when `timedOut` is `true`.
      - `timedOut` (required; boolean): The call stopped waiting at `timeoutSeconds`. It does not mean the command was stopped: it may still be running inside the container.
      - `truncated` (required; boolean): `stdout` or `stderr` reached the 1 MiB cap and was cut.
      - `durationMs` (required; integer): Wall time of the command as measured on the pod's machine, in milliseconds.
    - Example `gpuQuery`: `{"stdout":"name, memory.used [MiB]\nNVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, 0 MiB\n","stderr":"","exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"truncated":false,"durationMs":412}`
    - Example `failingInstall`: `{"stdout":"","stderr":"ERROR: No matching distribution found for nosuchpackage\n","exitCode":1,"timedOut":false,"truncated":false,"durationMs":2310}`
    - Example `timeout`: `{"stdout":"","stderr":"","exitCode":null,"timedOut":true,"truncated":false,"durationMs":5003}`
- `400`: The request could not be processed because it is malformed or conflicts with request rules.
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `badRequest`: `{"title":"Bad Request","status":400,"detail":"request could not be processed"}`
- `401`: Authentication failed because the bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or invalid.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `missingBearerToken`: `{"title":"Unauthorized","status":401,"detail":"missing bearer token"}`
- `403`: The bearer token is valid, but it does not grant access to the requested resource or action.
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.

  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.

# List Queued Pods

List the Runpod Pods queued for deploy-when-available, with each one's status, the pod it created, and why any failed.

`GET /v2/queued-pods`

**List queued pods**

Returns the caller's queued pods, cursor-paginated newest-first; an
omitted `limit` defaults to 1000. Every queued pod is listed whatever
its `status`, so the outcome of a queued create can be read after the
fact. Follow `pagination.nextCursor` until `hasNextPage` is false.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `cursor` (query; string; minimum length: `1`): Opaque resume cursor — pass the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` through verbatim; omit for the first page. A cursor is only valid for the operation and parameters that issued it; a malformed or foreign cursor is rejected with 422.
  - Example: `Y3JlYXRlZEF0PTE3NDg3ODA0MDA`
- `limit` (query; integer; minimum: `1`; maximum: `1000`): Page size, 1–1000. Defaults to 1000 when omitted.
  - Example: `50`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema
      - allOf:
        - `variant 1` (object)
          - `queuedPods` (required; array)
            - `items` (object): A pod waiting for capacity, or the record of one that waited. It carries what identifies and schedules the request; the full container settings are not echoed back, keep your create request.
              - `id` (required; string)
              - `status` (required; string; enum: `QUEUED`, `DEPLOYED`, `FAILED`, `EXPIRED`, `CANCELLED`): Where a queued pod is in its life. - `QUEUED` — waiting for capacity (from `queue.startsAt` when set) - `DEPLOYED` — capacity came and a pod was created; `podId` names it - `FAILED` — capacity came but the deploy was refused for good; `failureReason` says why - `EXPIRED` — `queue.expiresAt` passed without capacity - `CANCELLED` — cancelled with `DELETE /v2/queued-pods/{id}`
              - `podId` (required; nullable): The pod created once capacity came; null until then. Read it with `GET /v2/pods/{id}`.
              - `failureReason` (required): Set only when `status` is `FAILED`.
                - anyOf:
                  - `variant 1` (string; enum: `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, `SPENDING_LIMIT`, `GPU_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, `GPU_CONCURRENCY_EXCEEDED`, `ORG_RESTRICTED`, `UNKNOWN`): Why a `FAILED` queued pod could not deploy once capacity came. - `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` — the account balance was too low - `SPENDING_LIMIT` — the deploy would have passed the spending limit - `GPU_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` — the account's quota for this GPU type was reached - `GPU_CONCURRENCY_EXCEEDED` — the plan's concurrent GPU cap was reached - `ORG_RESTRICTED` — the account joined an organization, which cannot use queued deploys - `UNKNOWN` — anything else; contact support
                  - `variant 2` (null)
              - `name` (required; string): The name the pod will carry.
              - `image` (required; nullable): The image the pod will run. Null when it comes from `templateId` at deploy time.
              - `templateId` (required; nullable): The template the scheduler resolves at deploy time. Null for queued pods from this API, which expands `templateId` into `image` when the request is made.
              - `gpu` (required; object)
                - `id` (required; string): GPU type identifier
                - `count` (integer; default: `1`; minimum: `1`; maximum: `1024`): Number of GPUs
              - `cloud` (required; string; enum: `SECURE`, `COMMUNITY`): Cloud tier. - `SECURE` — Runpod-owned datacenter hardware - `COMMUNITY` — community-hosted hardware
              - `dataCenterIds` (required; array): The data centers the deploy is limited to; empty when any will do.
                - `items` (string)
              - `queue` (required; object): The `queue` options as stored, with the defaults applied.
                - `startsAt` (required; format: date-time; nullable): When waiting begins. Null when it began with the request.
                - `expiresAt` (required; string; format: date-time): When waiting ends.
                - `allowedHours` (required): Null when any hour is allowed.
                  - anyOf:
                    - `variant 1` (object): Hours of the day, in UTC, during which the queued pod may deploy, per weekday. Omit the object to allow any time. A weekday that is omitted is unrestricted; an empty array blocks that whole day. Each entry is an hour from 0 to 23 and allows deploys from that hour to the next.
                      - `monday` (array)
                        - `items` (integer; minimum: `0`; maximum: `23`)
                      - `tuesday` (array)
                        - `items` (integer; minimum: `0`; maximum: `23`)
                      - `wednesday` (array)
                        - `items` (integer; minimum: `0`; maximum: `23`)
                      - `thursday` (array)
                        - `items` (integer; minimum: `0`; maximum: `23`)
                      - `friday` (array)
                        - `items` (integer; minimum: `0`; maximum: `23`)
                      - `saturday` (array)
                        - `items` (integer; minimum: `0`; maximum: `23`)
                      - `sunday` (array)
                        - `items` (integer; minimum: `0`; maximum: `23`)
                    - `variant 2` (null)
                - `notifyEmail` (required; format: email; nullable): Null when no email was asked for.
              - `createdAt` (required; string; format: date-time)
              - `resolvedAt` (required; format: date-time; nullable): When the queued pod deployed, failed or expired. Null while it waits, and after a cancel.
        - `variant 2` (object): Mixin for cursor-paginated list responses. Compose it with `allOf` next to the resource's bare list schema so that a list shape shared with a non-paginated endpoint (e.g. a cluster's member pods) does not inherit a pagination block it cannot honour.
          - `pagination` (required; object): Cursor-pagination metadata, uniform across list endpoints. Every response carries it: follow `nextCursor` while `hasNextPage` is true to walk the full result set.
            - `nextCursor` (required; nullable): Pass as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page. Null on the last page.
            - `hasNextPage` (required; boolean): Whether more items exist after this page.
    - Example `queuedPods`: `{"queuedPods":[{"id":"clz1x9k4a0000qw3h8s7d2f1g","status":"DEPLOYED","podId":"7h9k2m4n6p","failureReason":null,"name":"pytorch-training","image":"runpod/pytorch:1.0.2-cu1281-torch280-ubuntu2404","templateId":null,"gpu":{"id":"NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090","count":1},"cloud":"SECURE","dataCenterIds":["EU-RO-1"],"queue":{"startsAt":null,"expiresAt":"2026-07-01T12:00:00Z","allowedHours":null,"notifyEmail":null},"createdAt":"2026-06-01T12:00:00Z","resolvedAt":"2026-06-01T13:05:00Z"}],"pagination":{"nextCursor":null,"hasNextPage":false}}`
- `401`: Authentication failed because the bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or invalid.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`

      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation

        - `items` (string)
    - Example `missingBearerToken`: `{"title":"Unauthorized","status":401,"detail":"missing bearer token"}`

  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.

# Get A Queued Pod

Retrieve a queued Runpod Pod by ID to see whether it is still waiting for capacity, which pod it created, or why it failed.

`GET /v2/queued-pods/{id}`

**Get a queued pod**

Returns a single queued pod by ID. Poll it after a `202` from
`createPod`: `status` moves from `QUEUED` to `DEPLOYED` (with
`podId`), `FAILED` (with `failureReason`), `EXPIRED`, or `CANCELLED`.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string): Queued pod identifier
  - Example: `clz1x9k4a0000qw3h8s7d2f1g`

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object): A pod waiting for capacity, or the record of one that waited. It carries what identifies and schedules the request; the full container settings are not echoed back, keep your create request.
      - `id` (required; string)
      - `status` (required; string; enum: `QUEUED`, `DEPLOYED`, `FAILED`, `EXPIRED`, `CANCELLED`): Where a queued pod is in its life. - `QUEUED` — waiting for capacity (from `queue.startsAt` when set) - `DEPLOYED` — capacity came and a pod was created; `podId` names it - `FAILED` — capacity came but the deploy was refused for good; `failureReason` says why - `EXPIRED` — `queue.expiresAt` passed without capacity - `CANCELLED` — cancelled with `DELETE /v2/queued-pods/{id}`
      - `podId` (required; nullable): The pod created once capacity came; null until then. Read it with `GET /v2/pods/{id}`.
      - `failureReason` (required): Set only when `status` is `FAILED`.
        - anyOf:
          - `variant 1` (string; enum: `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, `SPENDING_LIMIT`, `GPU_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, `GPU_CONCURRENCY_EXCEEDED`, `ORG_RESTRICTED`, `UNKNOWN`): Why a `FAILED` queued pod could not deploy once capacity came. - `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` — the account balance was too low - `SPENDING_LIMIT` — the deploy would have passed the spending limit - `GPU_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` — the account's quota for this GPU type was reached - `GPU_CONCURRENCY_EXCEEDED` — the plan's concurrent GPU cap was reached - `ORG_RESTRICTED` — the account joined an organization, which cannot use queued deploys - `UNKNOWN` — anything else; contact support
          - `variant 2` (null)
      - `name` (required; string): The name the pod will carry.
      - `image` (required; nullable): The image the pod will run. Null when it comes from `templateId` at deploy time.
      - `templateId` (required; nullable): The template the scheduler resolves at deploy time. Null for queued pods from this API, which expands `templateId` into `image` when the request is made.
      - `gpu` (required; object)

        - `count` (integer; default: `1`; minimum: `1`; maximum: `1024`): Number of GPUs

        - `items` (string)

        - `expiresAt` (required; string; format: date-time): When waiting ends.
        - `allowedHours` (required): Null when any hour is allowed.
          - anyOf:

A weekday that is omitted is unrestricted; an empty array blocks that whole day. Each entry is an hour from 0 to 23 and allows deploys from that hour to the next.

    - Example `queuedPod`: `{"id":"clz1x9k4a0000qw3h8s7d2f1g","status":"QUEUED","podId":null,"failureReason":null,"name":"pytorch-training","image":"runpod/pytorch:1.0.2-cu1281-torch280-ubuntu2404","templateId":null,"gpu":{"id":"NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090","count":1},"cloud":"SECURE","dataCenterIds":["EU-RO-1"],"queue":{"startsAt":null,"expiresAt":"2026-07-01T12:00:00Z","allowedHours":{"monday":[9,10,11,12,13,14,15,16]},"notifyEmail":null},"createdAt":"2026-06-01T12:00:00Z","resolvedAt":null}`

# List Clusters

List all Runpod Clusters owned by the authenticated user, including each Cluster's configuration, status, and aggregate Pod counts.

`GET /v2/clusters`

**List clusters**

Returns clusters owned by the authenticated user, cursor-paginated
newest-first; an omitted `limit` defaults to 1000. Follow
`pagination.nextCursor` until `hasNextPage` is false.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `filters` (query): Only return resources matching these filters, as URL-encoded JSON. The filters apply before the page is cut, so send the same value with each `cursor` to keep walking the filtered list.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object): An empty object, or an empty `tags` array, filters nothing.
      - `tags` (array; maximum items: `25`): Conditions on the resource's tags. A resource must match every condition; repeating a key adds a condition rather than widening the first one. At most 25, the most tags one resource can carry.
        - `items` (object)
          - `key` (required; string; minimum length: `1`; maximum length: `191`; pattern: `[^\t-\r  - ]`): Tag key, 1–191 characters as sent, with at least one that is not whitespace. Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored. Keys under the reserved `runpod:` prefix, in any letter case, are rejected.
          - `values` (array; maximum items: `100`): Matches a tag under `key` with any one of these values, compared exactly. Omitted or empty, the condition only requires the key to be present. `""` matches a tag whose value is empty. At most 100.
            - `items` (string; maximum length: `191`)
    - Example: `{"tags":[{"key":"env","values":["dev","prod"]},{"key":"team"}]}`
- `cursor` (query; string; minimum length: `1`): Opaque resume cursor — pass the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` through verbatim; omit for the first page. A cursor is only valid for the operation and parameters that issued it; a malformed or foreign cursor is rejected with 422.
  - Example: `Y3JlYXRlZEF0PTE3NDg3ODA0MDA`
- `limit` (query; integer; minimum: `1`; maximum: `1000`): Page size, 1–1000. Defaults to 1000 when omitted.
  - Example: `50`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `clusters` (required; array)
        - `items` (object): A cluster. Cluster-level fields describe the identity and homogeneous shape; `pods` is a lightweight summary of the members. Fetch the full member pods — with their container config, mounts, and runtime state — from `GET /v2/clusters/{id}/pods`.
          - `costCenter`: Cost center this resource's spend is attributed to. Absent when the resource is not attributed to a cost center, or when the caller lacks permission to view cost centers. Managed through `/v2/cost-centers`.
            - allOf:
              - `variant 1` (object)
                - `id` (required; string)
                - `value` (required; string): Cost center name exactly as stored, so it matches billing breakdowns.
          - `tags` (array): The tags on this resource that are visible to the caller. Keys and values are returned exactly as stored. Tags under the reserved `runpod:` prefix, such as the cost center, are never listed here. Absent when the resource's tags are unavailable to the caller; an empty array means none are visible.
            - `items` (object)
              - `id` (required; string): ID of the tag itself, shared by every resource it is attached to.
              - `key` (required; string)
              - `value` (required; string): May be empty.
          - `id` (required; string)
          - `name` (required; string)
          - `type` (required; string; enum: `APPLICATION`, `TRAINING`, `SLURM`, `RAY`): Cluster type. TRAINING is the generic distributed-training cluster; SLURM provisions a managed Slurm controller/compute topology; RAY provisions a managed Ray head/worker topology; APPLICATION is a general multi-node application cluster.
          - `compute` (required; object): The homogeneous compute shape of a cluster. Every pod in the cluster is identical: `podCount` pods, each with `gpuCountPerPod` GPUs of type `gpuTypeId`. Total GPUs = `podCount` \* `gpuCountPerPod`.
            - `gpuTypeId` (required; string; minimum length: `1`): GPU type for every pod in the cluster, as returned by GET /v2/catalog/gpus.
            - `gpuCountPerPod` (required; integer; minimum: `1`): Number of GPUs on each pod. Bounded above by the GPU type's per-cloud maximum (GpuType.maxCount); values beyond it are rejected.
            - `podCount` (required; integer; minimum: `2`; maximum: `250`): Number of pods (nodes) in the cluster.
          - `template` (string): ID of the template this cluster's pods were created from; omitted when they were not created from one.
          - `dataCenterId` (string): Data center the cluster is placed in (a cluster is always within a single data center). Derived from the member pods; omitted until at least one pod is placed.
          - `pods` (required; object): A lightweight summary of a cluster's member pods. Use `GET /v2/clusters/{id}/pods` to retrieve the full pod objects.
            - `total` (required; integer): Number of member pods currently provisioned for the cluster.
            - `byStatus` (required; object): Member pod counts keyed by pod status (the same values as `Pod.status`, e.g. RUNNING, PROVISIONING). Statuses with no pods are omitted.
              - Example: `{"RUNNING":3,"PROVISIONING":1}`
              - `additional properties` (integer)
          - `network`: The cluster's overlay network; omitted until the network is provisioned.
            - allOf:
              - `variant 1` (object): The cluster's private VXLAN overlay network (shared by all member pods).
                - `cidr` (required; string): The overlay network's CIDR block.
                - `vxlanId` (integer): VXLAN network identifier; omitted until assigned.
                - `vxlanPort` (integer): UDP port carrying the VXLAN traffic; omitted until assigned.
          - `primary`: The primary (master) node; omitted until a primary pod is placed. Its `sshEndpoint` is omitted until that pod is RUNNING with SSH exposed.
            - allOf:
              - `variant 1` (object): The cluster's primary (master) node, through which the cluster is typically driven. Omitted until a primary pod has been placed.
                - `podId` (required; string): ID of the primary member pod.
                - `status` (required; string; enum: `PROVISIONING`, `STARTING`, `RUNNING`, `EXITED`, `ERROR`, `TERMINATED`): Lifecycle status of a pod. - `PROVISIONING` — pod is being allocated - `STARTING` — container is starting - `RUNNING` — container is healthy - `EXITED` — container exited (stopped) - `ERROR` — container is in an unrecoverable error state - `TERMINATED` — pod has been permanently deleted
                - `sshEndpoint` (string): Public SSH endpoint (`host:port`) for the primary node; omitted when the primary is not yet RUNNING or does not expose SSH (22/tcp).
          - `createdAt` (required; string; format: date-time)
      - `pagination` (required; object): Cursor-pagination metadata, uniform across list endpoints. Every response carries it: follow `nextCursor` while `hasNextPage` is true to walk the full result set.
        - `nextCursor` (required; nullable): Pass as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page. Null on the last page.
        - `hasNextPage` (required; boolean): Whether more items exist after this page.
- `401`: Authentication failed because the bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or invalid.

# Document: Create A Cluster

Source path: api-reference-v2/clusters/create-a-cluster.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/api-reference-v2/clusters/create-a-cluster.mdx
Canonical documentation: https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/clusters/create-a-cluster
Description: Create a multi-node Runpod Cluster with a consistent compute shape and container configuration across every member Pod.

# Create A Cluster

Create a multi-node Runpod Cluster with a consistent compute shape and container configuration across every member Pod.

`POST /v2/clusters`

**Create a cluster**

Creates a multi-node cluster. `compute` sets the homogeneous
pod shape; the container configuration applies to every pod and can be spread
from a template response.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Request body** (required)

- Media type: `application/json`
  - Schema
    - allOf:
      - `variant 1`: Reusable container configuration shared across templates, pods, serverless endpoints, and clusters. Adding a field here automatically propagates to all of them.
        - allOf:
          - `variant 1` (object): Container configuration universal to every containerized resource. ContainerConfig composes it and adds `registry`; resources compose ContainerConfig.
            - `args` (string): The container's command, as a single raw string. This is the field `entrypoint` and `cmd` encode into, exposed in its stored form. Two shapes are accepted. A bare shell string is treated as CMD and split into arguments, which is what the console's "Container start command" field writes. A JSON object of the form `{"entrypoint":[...],"cmd":[...]}` sets either or both explicitly. Responses always return both representations: `args` exactly as stored, plus the deconstructed `entrypoint` and `cmd`. Supplying `args` together with `entrypoint` or `cmd` is allowed only when they describe the same command, so a read-modify-write client can send back everything it received. Send `""` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
            - `cmd` (array): Container CMD in exec form. When the image defines an ENTRYPOINT, this is the argument list passed to it. Encoded into the `args` field; supplying both is allowed only when they describe the same command. Send `[]` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
              - `items` (string)
            - `entrypoint` (array): Container ENTRYPOINT in exec form, overriding the image's own. Encoded into `args` field; supplying both is allowed only when they describe the same command. Send `[]` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
              - `items` (string)
            - `disk` (integer; minimum: `1`): Container disk in GB (ephemeral, wiped on restart)
            - `env` (object): Environment variables as key-value pairs
              - `additional properties` (string)
            - `image` (string): Docker image reference
            - `ports` (array): Exposed ports, formatted as port/protocol
              - `items` (string)
          - `variant 2` (object)
            - `registry` (nullable): Container registry credential ID for a private image: one of your credentials from `/v2/registries`. Leave it unset for a private Amazon ECR image. Runpod pulls those with an ECR delegation (`/v2/registries/delegations`) matched to the image's account, region and repository at pull time, so there is no delegation ID to pass here (a delegation ID is not a credential ID). A credential set here is used instead of any delegation.
      - `variant 2` (object): Request body for creating a cluster. `compute` defines the homogeneous pod shape; the container configuration (image, env, ports, registry, …) applies to every pod. Pass `templateId` to provision every member pod from a pod template instead of inline container fields. For a private image, pass `registry` (one of your credentials from `/v2/registries`); it is attached to every member pod, and an ID that does not exist or is not yours is a 400.
        - `compute` (required; object): The homogeneous compute shape of a cluster. Every pod in the cluster is identical: `podCount` pods, each with `gpuCountPerPod` GPUs of type `gpuTypeId`. Total GPUs = `podCount` \* `gpuCountPerPod`.
          - `gpuTypeId` (required; string; minimum length: `1`): GPU type for every pod in the cluster, as returned by GET /v2/catalog/gpus.
          - `gpuCountPerPod` (required; integer; minimum: `1`): Number of GPUs on each pod. Bounded above by the GPU type's per-cloud maximum (GpuType.maxCount); values beyond it are rejected.
          - `podCount` (required; integer; minimum: `2`; maximum: `250`): Number of pods (nodes) in the cluster.
        - `name` (required; string; minimum length: `1`)
        - `type` (required; string; enum: `APPLICATION`, `TRAINING`, `SLURM`, `RAY`): Cluster type. TRAINING is the generic distributed-training cluster; SLURM provisions a managed Slurm controller/compute topology; RAY provisions a managed Ray head/worker topology; APPLICATION is a general multi-node application cluster.
        - `templateId` (string; minimum length: `1`): ID of a pod template to provision every member pod from. The template supplies the container settings (image, args, disk, env, ports) and the container registry credential for private images. Mutually exclusive with `image`, `args`, `entrypoint`, `cmd`, `disk`, `env`, and `ports` (rejected with 400). `registry` combines with it: an explicit `registry` overrides the template's credential; omit it (or send `null` or an empty string) to use the template's. `mounts` combines with it too: the volume in `mounts` is attached to every member pod, overriding the template's volume settings. The cluster retains the link: the `template` response field is set. Must be a non-serverless pod template accessible to the caller.
        - `dataCenterIds` (array): Preferred data centers for placement. Omit or pass an empty array to let the scheduler choose. A cluster is always placed within a single data center.
          - Example: `["US-TX-3"]`
          - `items` (string)
        - `mounts`: Storage mounts for a cluster create: `persistent` or one `network` volume, not both. Clusters cannot mount global volumes, so `global` is rejected with 422. A mount `path` must not be empty (rejected with 422): an empty path reads as unset and would mount the volume at the template's path, or `/workspace` without a template.
          - allOf:
            - `variant 1` (object): Shared base type for all resources that mount storage volumes. `persistent` and `network` cannot both be set (rejected with 400). Each resource that uses this type sets its own limit on network volumes.
              - `persistent` (object): Host-local persistent storage. Pinned to the pod's host machine — data does not survive a host failure. Disallowed on CPU pods. Mutually exclusive with NetworkMount. Deprecated: prefer NetworkMount for any data you cannot recreate.
                - `size` (required; integer; minimum: `10`): Host-local persistent storage in GB. Minimum 10 GB.
                - `path` (required; string): Mount path inside the container. May be changed via PATCH.
              - `network` (array)
                - `items` (object): Reference to a NetworkVolume. Custom paths are honored at runtime on both GPU and CPU pods. On a pod, the volume can be mounted, moved, or unmounted after creation (see `UpdatePodMounts`).
                  - `volumeId` (required; string): ID of an existing NetworkVolume in the same data center as the pod.
                  - `path` (required; string): Mount path inside the container. No default — must be specified explicitly.
            - `variant 2` (object)
              - `persistent` (object)
                - `path` (string; minimum length: `1`)
              - `network` (array; maximum items: `1`)
                - `items` (object)
                  - `path` (string; minimum length: `1`)
        - `startJupyter` (boolean; default: `false`): Start Jupyter on every member pod, as on pod create.
        - `startSsh` (boolean; default: `false`): Provision SSH access on every member pod: injects a PUBLIC\_KEY environment variable carrying your account's registered SSH public key. Same semantics as the pod create flag.

**Responses**

- `201`: Created
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object): A cluster. Cluster-level fields describe the identity and homogeneous shape; `pods` is a lightweight summary of the members. Fetch the full member pods — with their container config, mounts, and runtime state — from `GET /v2/clusters/{id}/pods`.
      - `costCenter`: Cost center this resource's spend is attributed to. Absent when the resource is not attributed to a cost center, or when the caller lacks permission to view cost centers. Managed through `/v2/cost-centers`.
        - allOf:
          - `variant 1` (object)
            - `id` (required; string)
            - `value` (required; string): Cost center name exactly as stored, so it matches billing breakdowns.
      - `tags` (array): The tags on this resource that are visible to the caller. Keys and values are returned exactly as stored. Tags under the reserved `runpod:` prefix, such as the cost center, are never listed here. Absent when the resource's tags are unavailable to the caller; an empty array means none are visible.
        - `items` (object)
          - `id` (required; string): ID of the tag itself, shared by every resource it is attached to.
          - `key` (required; string)
          - `value` (required; string): May be empty.
      - `id` (required; string)
      - `name` (required; string)
      - `type` (required; string; enum: `APPLICATION`, `TRAINING`, `SLURM`, `RAY`): Cluster type. TRAINING is the generic distributed-training cluster; SLURM provisions a managed Slurm controller/compute topology; RAY provisions a managed Ray head/worker topology; APPLICATION is a general multi-node application cluster.
      - `compute` (required; object): The homogeneous compute shape of a cluster. Every pod in the cluster is identical: `podCount` pods, each with `gpuCountPerPod` GPUs of type `gpuTypeId`. Total GPUs = `podCount` \* `gpuCountPerPod`.
        - `gpuTypeId` (required; string; minimum length: `1`): GPU type for every pod in the cluster, as returned by GET /v2/catalog/gpus.
        - `gpuCountPerPod` (required; integer; minimum: `1`): Number of GPUs on each pod. Bounded above by the GPU type's per-cloud maximum (GpuType.maxCount); values beyond it are rejected.
        - `podCount` (required; integer; minimum: `2`; maximum: `250`): Number of pods (nodes) in the cluster.
      - `template` (string): ID of the template this cluster's pods were created from; omitted when they were not created from one.
      - `dataCenterId` (string): Data center the cluster is placed in (a cluster is always within a single data center). Derived from the member pods; omitted until at least one pod is placed.
      - `pods` (required; object): A lightweight summary of a cluster's member pods. Use `GET /v2/clusters/{id}/pods` to retrieve the full pod objects.
        - `total` (required; integer): Number of member pods currently provisioned for the cluster.
        - `byStatus` (required; object): Member pod counts keyed by pod status (the same values as `Pod.status`, e.g. RUNNING, PROVISIONING). Statuses with no pods are omitted.
          - Example: `{"RUNNING":3,"PROVISIONING":1}`
          - `additional properties` (integer)
      - `network`: The cluster's overlay network; omitted until the network is provisioned.
        - allOf:
          - `variant 1` (object): The cluster's private VXLAN overlay network (shared by all member pods).
            - `cidr` (required; string): The overlay network's CIDR block.
            - `vxlanId` (integer): VXLAN network identifier; omitted until assigned.
            - `vxlanPort` (integer): UDP port carrying the VXLAN traffic; omitted until assigned.
      - `primary`: The primary (master) node; omitted until a primary pod is placed. Its `sshEndpoint` is omitted until that pod is RUNNING with SSH exposed.
        - allOf:
          - `variant 1` (object): The cluster's primary (master) node, through which the cluster is typically driven. Omitted until a primary pod has been placed.
            - `podId` (required; string): ID of the primary member pod.
            - `status` (required; string; enum: `PROVISIONING`, `STARTING`, `RUNNING`, `EXITED`, `ERROR`, `TERMINATED`): Lifecycle status of a pod. - `PROVISIONING` — pod is being allocated - `STARTING` — container is starting - `RUNNING` — container is healthy - `EXITED` — container exited (stopped) - `ERROR` — container is in an unrecoverable error state - `TERMINATED` — pod has been permanently deleted
            - `sshEndpoint` (string): Public SSH endpoint (`host:port`) for the primary node; omitted when the primary is not yet RUNNING or does not expose SSH (22/tcp).
      - `createdAt` (required; string; format: date-time)
- `400`: The request could not be processed because it is malformed or conflicts with request rules.

  - Example: `cluster_abc123`

  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object): A cluster. Cluster-level fields describe the identity and homogeneous shape; `pods` is a lightweight summary of the members. Fetch the full member pods — with their container config, mounts, and runtime state — from `GET /v2/clusters/{id}/pods`.

          - `variant 1` (object)
            - `id` (required; string)
            - `value` (required; string): Cost center name exactly as stored, so it matches billing breakdowns.
      - `tags` (array): The tags on this resource that are visible to the caller. Keys and values are returned exactly as stored. Tags under the reserved `runpod:` prefix, such as the cost center, are never listed here. Absent when the resource's tags are unavailable to the caller; an empty array means none are visible.
        - `items` (object)
          - `id` (required; string): ID of the tag itself, shared by every resource it is attached to.
          - `key` (required; string)
          - `value` (required; string): May be empty.
      - `id` (required; string)
      - `name` (required; string)
      - `type` (required; string; enum: `APPLICATION`, `TRAINING`, `SLURM`, `RAY`): Cluster type. TRAINING is the generic distributed-training cluster; SLURM provisions a managed Slurm controller/compute topology; RAY provisions a managed Ray head/worker topology; APPLICATION is a general multi-node application cluster.
      - `compute` (required; object): The homogeneous compute shape of a cluster. Every pod in the cluster is identical: `podCount` pods, each with `gpuCountPerPod` GPUs of type `gpuTypeId`. Total GPUs = `podCount` \* `gpuCountPerPod`.
        - `gpuTypeId` (required; string; minimum length: `1`): GPU type for every pod in the cluster, as returned by GET /v2/catalog/gpus.
        - `gpuCountPerPod` (required; integer; minimum: `1`): Number of GPUs on each pod. Bounded above by the GPU type's per-cloud maximum (GpuType.maxCount); values beyond it are rejected.
        - `podCount` (required; integer; minimum: `2`; maximum: `250`): Number of pods (nodes) in the cluster.
      - `template` (string): ID of the template this cluster's pods were created from; omitted when they were not created from one.
      - `dataCenterId` (string): Data center the cluster is placed in (a cluster is always within a single data center). Derived from the member pods; omitted until at least one pod is placed.
      - `pods` (required; object): A lightweight summary of a cluster's member pods. Use `GET /v2/clusters/{id}/pods` to retrieve the full pod objects.
        - `total` (required; integer): Number of member pods currently provisioned for the cluster.
        - `byStatus` (required; object): Member pod counts keyed by pod status (the same values as `Pod.status`, e.g. RUNNING, PROVISIONING). Statuses with no pods are omitted.
          - Example: `{"RUNNING":3,"PROVISIONING":1}`
          - `additional properties` (integer)
      - `network`: The cluster's overlay network; omitted until the network is provisioned.
        - allOf:
          - `variant 1` (object): The cluster's private VXLAN overlay network (shared by all member pods).
            - `cidr` (required; string): The overlay network's CIDR block.
            - `vxlanId` (integer): VXLAN network identifier; omitted until assigned.
            - `vxlanPort` (integer): UDP port carrying the VXLAN traffic; omitted until assigned.
      - `primary`: The primary (master) node; omitted until a primary pod is placed. Its `sshEndpoint` is omitted until that pod is RUNNING with SSH exposed.
        - allOf:
          - `variant 1` (object): The cluster's primary (master) node, through which the cluster is typically driven. Omitted until a primary pod has been placed.
            - `podId` (required; string): ID of the primary member pod.
            - `status` (required; string; enum: `PROVISIONING`, `STARTING`, `RUNNING`, `EXITED`, `ERROR`, `TERMINATED`): Lifecycle status of a pod. - `PROVISIONING` — pod is being allocated - `STARTING` — container is starting - `RUNNING` — container is healthy - `EXITED` — container exited (stopped) - `ERROR` — container is in an unrecoverable error state - `TERMINATED` — pod has been permanently deleted
            - `sshEndpoint` (string): Public SSH endpoint (`host:port`) for the primary node; omitted when the primary is not yet RUNNING or does not expose SSH (22/tcp).
      - `createdAt` (required; string; format: date-time)

# List A Clusters Pods

List every Pod in a Runpod Cluster with each member's complete configuration and status, beyond the aggregate counts in the Cluster summary.

`GET /v2/clusters/{id}/pods`

**List a cluster's pods**

Returns the full member pods of a cluster. The cluster summary (`GET /v2/clusters/{id}`) carries only aggregate pod counts; this endpoint returns each member as a complete Pod object.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string): Cluster identifier
  - Example: `cluster_abc123`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object): A bare list of pods. `GET /v2/clusters/{id}/pods` returns it as-is (a cluster's members are a small, complete set); `GET /v2/pods` composes it with the pagination block via ListPodsResponse.
      - `pods` (required; array)
        - `items`
          - allOf:
            - `variant 1`: Reusable container configuration shared across templates, pods, serverless endpoints, and clusters. Adding a field here automatically propagates to all of them.
              - allOf:
                - `variant 1` (object): Container configuration universal to every containerized resource. ContainerConfig composes it and adds `registry`; resources compose ContainerConfig.
                  - `args` (string): The container's command, as a single raw string. This is the field `entrypoint` and `cmd` encode into, exposed in its stored form. Two shapes are accepted. A bare shell string is treated as CMD and split into arguments, which is what the console's "Container start command" field writes. A JSON object of the form `{"entrypoint":[...],"cmd":[...]}` sets either or both explicitly. Responses always return both representations: `args` exactly as stored, plus the deconstructed `entrypoint` and `cmd`. Supplying `args` together with `entrypoint` or `cmd` is allowed only when they describe the same command, so a read-modify-write client can send back everything it received. Send `""` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
                  - `cmd` (array): Container CMD in exec form. When the image defines an ENTRYPOINT, this is the argument list passed to it. Encoded into the `args` field; supplying both is allowed only when they describe the same command. Send `[]` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
                    - `items` (string)
                  - `entrypoint` (array): Container ENTRYPOINT in exec form, overriding the image's own. Encoded into `args` field; supplying both is allowed only when they describe the same command. Send `[]` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
                    - `items` (string)
                  - `disk` (integer; minimum: `1`): Container disk in GB (ephemeral, wiped on restart)
                  - `env` (object): Environment variables as key-value pairs
                    - `additional properties` (string)
                  - `image` (string): Docker image reference
                  - `ports` (array): Exposed ports, formatted as port/protocol
                    - `items` (string)
                - `variant 2` (object)
                  - `registry` (nullable): Container registry credential ID for a private image: one of your credentials from `/v2/registries`. Leave it unset for a private Amazon ECR image. Runpod pulls those with an ECR delegation (`/v2/registries/delegations`) matched to the image's account, region and repository at pull time, so there is no delegation ID to pass here (a delegation ID is not a credential ID). A credential set here is used instead of any delegation.
            - `variant 2` (object)
              - `costCenter`: Cost center this resource's spend is attributed to. Absent when the resource is not attributed to a cost center, or when the caller lacks permission to view cost centers. Managed through `/v2/cost-centers`.
                - allOf:
                  - `variant 1` (object)
                    - `id` (required; string)
                    - `value` (required; string): Cost center name exactly as stored, so it matches billing breakdowns.
              - `tags` (array): The tags on this resource that are visible to the caller. Keys and values are returned exactly as stored. Tags under the reserved `runpod:` prefix, such as the cost center, are never listed here. Absent when the resource's tags are unavailable to the caller; an empty array means none are visible.
                - `items` (object)
                  - `id` (required; string): ID of the tag itself, shared by every resource it is attached to.
                  - `key` (required; string)
                  - `value` (required; string): May be empty.
              - `id` (required; string)
              - `name` (required; string)
              - `status` (required; string; enum: `PROVISIONING`, `STARTING`, `RUNNING`, `EXITED`, `ERROR`, `TERMINATED`): Lifecycle status of a pod. - `PROVISIONING` — pod is being allocated - `STARTING` — container is starting - `RUNNING` — container is healthy - `EXITED` — container exited (stopped) - `ERROR` — container is in an unrecoverable error state - `TERMINATED` — pod has been permanently deleted
              - `actions` (required; array): Valid state transitions for the current status.
                - `items` (string; enum: `start`, `stop`, `restart`, `terminate`): State transition to trigger on a pod.
              - `mounts` (required): Storage mounts attached to a pod. `persistent` (the volume disk) is mutually exclusive with both `network` and `global` (enforced at the handler with 400 if combined). A pod takes up to 4 network volumes and 1 global volume. Every network volume must be in the pod's data center, each volume may be listed once, and mount paths must not overlap; a request that breaks one of these is rejected. To change a pod's mounts after creation, see `UpdatePodMounts`.
                - allOf:
                  - `variant 1` (object): Shared base type for all resources that mount storage volumes. `persistent` and `network` cannot both be set (rejected with 400). Each resource that uses this type sets its own limit on network volumes.
                    - `persistent` (object): Host-local persistent storage. Pinned to the pod's host machine — data does not survive a host failure. Disallowed on CPU pods. Mutually exclusive with NetworkMount. Deprecated: prefer NetworkMount for any data you cannot recreate.
                      - `size` (required; integer; minimum: `10`): Host-local persistent storage in GB. Minimum 10 GB.
                      - `path` (required; string): Mount path inside the container. May be changed via PATCH.
                    - `network` (array)
                      - `items` (object): Reference to a NetworkVolume. Custom paths are honored at runtime on both GPU and CPU pods. On a pod, the volume can be mounted, moved, or unmounted after creation (see `UpdatePodMounts`).
                        - `volumeId` (required; string): ID of an existing NetworkVolume in the same data center as the pod.
                        - `path` (required; string): Mount path inside the container. No default — must be specified explicitly.
                  - `variant 2` (object)
                    - `network` (array; maximum items: `4`): Up to 4 network volumes, all in the pod's data center.
                      - `items` (object): Reference to a NetworkVolume. Custom paths are honored at runtime on both GPU and CPU pods. On a pod, the volume can be mounted, moved, or unmounted after creation (see `UpdatePodMounts`).
                        - `volumeId` (required; string): ID of an existing NetworkVolume in the same data center as the pod.
                        - `path` (required; string): Mount path inside the container. No default — must be specified explicitly.
                    - `global` (array; maximum items: `1`): At most one global volume, with no data center constraint. Combinable with `network` but not with `persistent` (rejected with 400): a persistent disk is dropped whenever a volume is attached. Same PATCH rules as `network`.
                      - `items` (object): Reference to a GlobalVolume. Usage-billed, so it has no size. On a pod, the volume can be mounted, moved, or unmounted after creation (see `UpdatePodMounts`).
                        - `volumeId` (required; string): ID of an existing GlobalVolume.
                        - `path` (string): Mount path inside the container. Optional; a default is chosen for you when omitted.
              - `gpu`: Present for GPU pods; omitted from CPU pods.
                - allOf:
                  - `variant 1`
                    - allOf:
                      - `variant 1` (object)
                        - `id` (required; string): GPU type identifier
                        - `count` (integer; default: `1`; minimum: `1`; maximum: `1024`): Number of GPUs
                      - `variant 2` (object)
                        - `vcpuCount` (required; number; format: double; minimum: `1`): Total vCPU count allocated to the pod across all requested GPUs.
                        - `memory` (required; number; format: double; minimum: `1`): Total system RAM in GB allocated to the pod across all requested GPUs.
              - `cpu`: Present for CPU pods; omitted from GPU pods.
                - allOf:
                  - `variant 1`
                    - allOf:
                      - `variant 1` (object)
                        - `id` (required; string; minimum length: `1`): CPU flavor identifier, as returned by GET /v2/catalog/cpus.
                        - `vcpuCount` (required; integer; minimum: `2`): Number of vCPUs. Must be valid for the selected CPU flavor and must be a power of two.
                      - `variant 2` (object)
                        - `memory` (required; integer; minimum: `1`): Memory allocated to the pod in GB.
              - `cloud` (required; string; enum: `SECURE`, `COMMUNITY`): Cloud tier. - `SECURE` — Runpod-owned datacenter hardware - `COMMUNITY` — community-hosted hardware
              - `dataCenterId` (required; nullable): Data center where the pod is running (assigned by scheduler)
              - `cudaVersion` (required; nullable): CUDA version reported by the host machine. Retained while the pod is stopped — a stopped pod keeps its machine assignment and resumes onto the same host. Null means unknown or not applicable (CPU pods, or a host that has not reported one), not that CUDA is absent.
              - `ssh` (required): SSH connection details, via the Runpod proxy or directly to the pod's published `22/tcp` port.
                - allOf:
                  - `variant 1` (object): How to connect to this pod over SSH. Both variants authenticate with the account's registered SSH public keys (`PUT /v2/account/ssh-keys`), which reach the pod only if it was created with `startSsh` — a pod created without it has no SSH access regardless of what this block reports.
                    - `proxy` (required): Connection through Runpod's SSH proxy. Works without exposing a port and without a public IP, but carries an interactive shell only — SCP, SFTP, rsync, and port forwarding need `direct`. Null until the pod has a machine assignment.
                      - anyOf:
                        - `variant 1` (object): One way to reach the pod over SSH, as both its parts and a ready-to-run invocation.
                          - `host` (required; string): Hostname or IP to connect to.
                          - `port` (required; integer): TCP port to connect to.
                          - `username` (required; string): SSH username. For the proxy this is an opaque routing token, not a user account on the pod.
                          - `command` (required; string): The equivalent `ssh` invocation, ready to run. Add `-i <path>` if the matching private key is not one of your default identities, and `-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no` to skip the host-key prompt on short-lived pods.
                        - `variant 2` (null)
                    - `direct` (required): Connection straight to the pod's sshd over its published `22/tcp` mapping. Supports the full SSH feature set. Null unless `22/tcp` is in `ports` and the running pod has been assigned a public port for it — so it is usually absent while the pod is provisioning or stopped. It can still appear on a stopped pod, so check that `status` is `RUNNING` before connecting. Also null when listing pods with `GET /v2/pods`; fetch a single pod by ID to obtain the live mapping.
                      - anyOf:
                        - `variant 1` (object): One way to reach the pod over SSH, as both its parts and a ready-to-run invocation.
                          - `host` (required; string): Hostname or IP to connect to.
                          - `port` (required; integer): TCP port to connect to.
                          - `username` (required; string): SSH username. For the proxy this is an opaque routing token, not a user account on the pod.

                        - `variant 2` (null)
              - `cluster`: Cluster membership; omitted from a standalone pod. Member pods are managed through `/v2/clusters/{id}` — they are excluded from `GET /v2/pods` by default (pass `includeClusterPods=true` to include them) and cannot be modified or deleted via the pod endpoints.
                - allOf:
                  - `variant 1` (object): A pod's membership in a cluster.
                    - `id` (required; string): ID of the cluster this pod belongs to.
                    - `rank` (required; nullable): The pod's node rank within the cluster (NODE\_RANK), or null until the index is assigned during provisioning. Rank 0 is the cluster's entry node (`Cluster.primary`); for SLURM it is the controller.
                    - `role`: SLURM or RAY role; omitted for TRAINING/APPLICATION clusters, which do not assign roles.

                        - `variant 1` (string; enum: `SLURM_CONTROLLER`, `SLURM_COMPUTE`, `RAY_HEAD`, `RAY_WORKER`): A cluster member's role. Assigned for SLURM and RAY clusters; omitted for TRAINING/APPLICATION members.

              - `cost` (required; number; format: float): The pod's hourly compute rate in USD. It's returned in every status, including `EXITED`, so it isn't what you're paying right now: a stopped pod isn't billed for compute, only for its volume disk.
              - `locked` (required; boolean): Whether the pod is locked (prevents stopping or resetting)
              - `globalNetworking` (required; object)
                - `enabled` (required; boolean): Whether global networking is enabled, giving the pod a private IP reachable across data centers. Derived from whether the pod has an assigned global-network address.

                - anyOf:

                    - `gpus` (array)
                      - `items` (object): Per-GPU utilization metrics.
                        - `util` (integer)
                        - `memoryUtil` (integer)
                    - `cpu` (object): Single-value utilization percentage (0–100). Shared by `cpu` and `memory`.
                      - `util` (integer)
                    - `memory` (object): Single-value utilization percentage (0–100). Shared by `cpu` and `memory`.
                      - `util` (integer)
                    - `ports` (array)
                      - `items` (object): Live port mapping for a running pod.
                        - `private` (integer)
                        - `public` (nullable)
                        - `type` (string)
                        - `ip` (nullable)
                  - `variant 2` (null)
              - `createdAt` (required; string; format: date-time)
