# Document: List Public Templates

Source path: api-reference-v2/catalog/list-public-templates.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-public-templates.mdx
Canonical documentation: https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-public-templates
Description: Search Runpod public templates by official, verified, or community source and inspect reusable Pod and Serverless configurations.

# List Public Templates

Search Runpod public templates by official, verified, or community source and inspect reusable Pod and Serverless configurations.

`GET /v2/catalog/templates`

**List public templates**

Returns the public template catalog. `source` selects which slice:
`official` (the default) is Runpod-curated templates, `verified` is
community templates Runpod has verified, and `community` is everything
else other users have shared publicly. Both pod and serverless
templates appear — use each entry's `serverless` flag to tell them
apart. `registry` is always null for templates you don't own. Your own
templates (public or private) are managed under `/v2/templates`; fetch
any individual template — catalog or owned — via `/v2/templates/{id}`.

A versioned template line appears as its current tags: each is a
deployable template of its own.

Without `search`, templates are ordered most deployed first: by the number
of unique users who deployed them.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `source` (query; string; enum: `official`, `verified`, `community`; default: `official`): Which slice of the catalog to return: `official` for Runpod-curated templates (default), `verified` for Runpod-verified community templates, or `community` for all other publicly shared templates.
  - Example: `official`
- `search` (query; string; minimum length: `1`; maximum length: `200`): Search text, matched case-insensitively. Every word must match. A skill matches on its name, description and tags; a repo also on its GitHub owner and name; a template on its name and image, and a versioned template's tag also on its line's name and description. Enables `orderBy=RELEVANCE`, which becomes the default order.
  - Example: `comfyui`
- `type` (query; string; enum: `SINGLE`, `VERSIONED`): Only return standalone (`SINGLE`) or versioned (`VERSIONED`) templates. Omit for both.
  - Example: `VERSIONED`
- `product` (query; array): Only return items that deploy to one of these products. Comma-separated.
  - Example: `["SERVERLESS"]`
- `minReliability` (query; number; format: double; minimum: `0`; maximum: `1`): Only return items whose `health.reliability` is at least this value. Unscored items are excluded when this is set.
  - Example: `0.9`
- `category` (query; string; enum: `CPU`, `NVIDIA`, `AMD`): Only return templates in this category.
  - Example: `NVIDIA`
- `orderBy` (query; string; enum: `RELEVANCE`, `POPULAR`, `UPDATED`, `HEALTH`, `NAME`): Defaults to `RELEVANCE` when `search` is set and `POPULAR` otherwise. `RELEVANCE` without `search` is rejected with 400.
  - Example: `POPULAR`
- `orderDirection` (query; string; enum: `ASC`, `DESC`): Sort direction. Defaults to `ASC` for `orderBy=NAME` and `DESC` otherwise.
  - Example: `DESC`
- `cursor` (query; string; minimum length: `1`): Opaque resume cursor — pass the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` through verbatim; omit for the first page. A cursor is only valid for the operation and parameters that issued it; a malformed or foreign cursor is rejected with 422.
  - Example: `Y3JlYXRlZEF0PTE3NDg3ODA0MDA`
- `limit` (query; integer; minimum: `1`; maximum: `1000`): Page size, 1–1000. Defaults to 1000 when omitted.
  - Example: `50`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `templates` (required; array)
        - `items`: A public template. Every `id` is deployable and resolves at `GET /v2/templates/{id}`.
          - allOf:
            - `variant 1`
              - allOf:
                - `variant 1`: Reusable container configuration shared across templates, pods, serverless endpoints, and clusters. Adding a field here automatically propagates to all of them.
                  - allOf:
                    - `variant 1` (object): Container configuration universal to every containerized resource. ContainerConfig composes it and adds `registry`; resources compose ContainerConfig.
                      - `args` (string): The container's command, as a single raw string. This is the field `entrypoint` and `cmd` encode into, exposed in its stored form. Two shapes are accepted. A bare shell string is treated as CMD and split into arguments, which is what the console's "Container start command" field writes. A JSON object of the form `{"entrypoint":[...],"cmd":[...]}` sets either or both explicitly. Responses always return both representations: `args` exactly as stored, plus the deconstructed `entrypoint` and `cmd`. Supplying `args` together with `entrypoint` or `cmd` is allowed only when they describe the same command, so a read-modify-write client can send back everything it received. Send `""` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
                      - `cmd` (array): Container CMD in exec form. When the image defines an ENTRYPOINT, this is the argument list passed to it. Encoded into the `args` field; supplying both is allowed only when they describe the same command. Send `[]` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
                        - `items` (string)
                      - `entrypoint` (array): Container ENTRYPOINT in exec form, overriding the image's own. Encoded into `args` field; supplying both is allowed only when they describe the same command. Send `[]` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
                        - `items` (string)
                      - `disk` (integer; minimum: `1`): Container disk in GB (ephemeral, wiped on restart)
                      - `env` (object): Environment variables as key-value pairs
                        - `additional properties` (string)
                      - `image` (string): Docker image reference
                      - `ports` (array): Exposed ports, formatted as port/protocol
                        - `items` (string)
                    - `variant 2` (object)
                      - `registry` (nullable): Container registry credential ID for a private image: one of your credentials from `/v2/registries`. Leave it unset for a private Amazon ECR image. Runpod pulls those with an ECR delegation (`/v2/registries/delegations`) matched to the image's account, region and repository at pull time, so there is no delegation ID to pass here (a delegation ID is not a credential ID). A credential set here is used instead of any delegation.
                - `variant 2` (object)
                  - `id` (required; string)
                  - `name` (required; string)
                  - `mounts` (required; object): Storage mounts attached to a template. Templates support only a single persistent mount today; any `network` property is rejected with 422 by the schema validator. PATCH semantics: omitting `mounts` or sending `{}` leaves the existing mount unchanged.
                    - `persistent` (object): Host-local persistent storage. Pinned to the pod's host machine — data does not survive a host failure. Disallowed on CPU pods. Mutually exclusive with NetworkMount. Deprecated: prefer NetworkMount for any data you cannot recreate.
                      - `size` (required; integer; minimum: `10`): Host-local persistent storage in GB. Minimum 10 GB.
                      - `path` (required; string): Mount path inside the container. May be changed via PATCH.
                  - `serverless` (required; boolean): Whether this template is for serverless workers (true) or pods (false)
                  - `public` (required; boolean): Whether this template is visible to other Runpod users
                  - `category` (required; string; enum: `CPU`, `NVIDIA`, `AMD`): Controls how the template is grouped and filtered in the Runpod console. It does not affect hardware selection, scheduling, or billing. - `CPU` — CPU-only workloads - `NVIDIA` — NVIDIA GPU workloads - `AMD` — AMD GPU workloads
                  - `startSsh` (required; boolean): Whether containers created from this template get SSH access provisioned at startup (`PUBLIC_KEY` env injection).
                  - `startJupyter` (required; boolean): Whether containers created from this template start JupyterLab at startup (`JUPYTER_PASSWORD` env injection).
                  - `allowedCudaVersions` (required; array): Acceptable CUDA versions for containers created from this template, as `major.minor`. Empty means any version. Expanded into GPU pod and serverless endpoint creates; CPU pods ignore it.
                    - `items` (string)
            - `variant 2` (object): The Hub fields of a catalog template. A `VERSIONED` item is one tag of a versioned line: `id`, `name`, `image` and the container fields are the tag's, as `GET /v2/templates/{id}` returns them, and `versionedTemplateId` names the line.
              - `type` (required; string; enum: `SINGLE`, `VERSIONED`): `SINGLE` is a standalone template. `VERSIONED` is a tag of a versioned template line; the list shows each line's current tags.
              - `versionedTemplateId` (required; nullable): The versioned line this tag belongs to. Null for `SINGLE`.
              - `currentVersion` (required; nullable): The line's current version. Null for `SINGLE`, and for a tag whose line has no current version.
              - `official` (required; boolean): Whether Runpod publishes the template.
              - `verified` (required; boolean): Whether Runpod has verified this community template.
              - `products` (required; array)
                - `items` (string; enum: `POD`, `SERVERLESS`): Where a catalog item deploys.
              - `health` (required; object): How reliably a catalog item deploys.
                - `tier` (required; string; enum: `VERIFIED`, `UNVERIFIED`, `UNSTABLE`): `UNVERIFIED` while `reliability` is null. Otherwise `UNSTABLE` below Runpod's cutoff for the object's kind and `VERIFIED` at or above it. Set your own bar with `minReliability`.
                - `reliability` (required; format: double; nullable; minimum: `0`; maximum: `1`): Share of recent deploys that reached a healthy state; 0.9 means 90%. Null until there is enough deploy history to score.
                - `computedAt` (required; format: date-time; nullable): When `reliability` was last computed. Null when never scored.
              - `gpuCompatibility` (required; object): The GPUs and CUDA versions a catalog item declares. Empty lists mean it declares none.
                - `recommendedGpuTypeIds` (required; array): GPU type IDs, as in `GET /v2/catalog/gpus`.
                  - `items` (string)
                - `incompatibleGpuTypeIds` (required; array): GPU type IDs, as in `GET /v2/catalog/gpus`.
                  - `items` (string)
                - `minVramInGb` (required; nullable): Null when it declares none. Repos never declare one.
                - `allowedCudaVersions` (required; array)
                  - `items` (string)
                - `minCudaVersion` (required; nullable): The lowest CUDA version it runs on, applied when `allowedCudaVersions` is empty. Null when it declares none. Templates never declare one.
              - `stats` (required; object): Unique users who deployed the template, refreshed periodically. For a `VERSIONED` item, the sum over every tag in its line.
                - `deployers` (required; integer): All time.
                - `deployersLast30Days` (required; integer)
              - `createdAt` (required; string; format: date-time)
              - `updatedAt` (required; string; format: date-time): When the template's content was last edited.
      - `pagination` (required; object): Cursor-pagination metadata, uniform across list endpoints. Every response carries it: follow `nextCursor` while `hasNextPage` is true to walk the full result set.
        - `nextCursor` (required; nullable): Pass as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page. Null on the last page.
        - `hasNextPage` (required; boolean): Whether more items exist after this page.
    - Example `templates`: `{"templates":[{"id":"30zmvf89kd","name":"PyTorch 2.8","image":"runpod/pytorch:1.0.2-cu1281-torch280-ubuntu2404","args":"","disk":50,"mounts":{},"ports":["8888/http","22/tcp"],"env":{},"registry":null,"serverless":false,"public":true,"category":"NVIDIA","startSsh":true,"startJupyter":true,"allowedCudaVersions":[],"type":"SINGLE","versionedTemplateId":null,"currentVersion":null,"official":true,"verified":false,"products":["POD"],"health":{"tier":"VERIFIED","reliability":0.99,"computedAt":"2026-11-04T06:00:00Z"},"gpuCompatibility":{"recommendedGpuTypeIds":[],"incompatibleGpuTypeIds":[],"minVramInGb":null,"allowedCudaVersions":[],"minCudaVersion":null},"stats":{"deployers":1840,"deployersLast30Days":211},"createdAt":"2025-06-02T00:00:00Z","updatedAt":"2025-07-10T00:00:00Z"}],"pagination":{"nextCursor":null,"hasNextPage":false}}`
- `400`: The request could not be processed because it is malformed or conflicts with request rules.
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `badRequest`: `{"title":"Bad Request","status":400,"detail":"request could not be processed"}`
- `401`: Authentication failed because the bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or invalid.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `missingBearerToken`: `{"title":"Unauthorized","status":401,"detail":"missing bearer token"}`
- `403`: The bearer token is valid, but it does not grant access to the requested resource or action.
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)

  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.

# Get A Public Template

Retrieve a Runpod public template with its health, deploy stats and, for a versioned line, every version and tag.

`GET /v2/catalog/templates/{id}`

**Get a public template**

Returns one public template. This covers every public template,
including ones the list leaves out: your own, and ones below the
list's quality bar.

For a versioned line, `versions` lists every version with its tags.
The top-level fields are the requested tag's when you ask by tag ID,
and the first current tag's when you ask by line ID. A line ID
resolves only while the line has a current tag; its published tags
resolve regardless, with `currentVersion` null when nothing is
current.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string): A template ID from `GET /v2/catalog/templates`, a versioned line's ID, or any of its tags' IDs.
  - Example: `opvzatg7kb`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema
      - allOf:
        - `variant 1`: A public template. Every `id` is deployable and resolves at `GET /v2/templates/{id}`.
          - allOf:
            - `variant 1`
              - allOf:
                - `variant 1`: Reusable container configuration shared across templates, pods, serverless endpoints, and clusters. Adding a field here automatically propagates to all of them.
                  - allOf:
                    - `variant 1` (object): Container configuration universal to every containerized resource. ContainerConfig composes it and adds `registry`; resources compose ContainerConfig.
                      - `args` (string): The container's command, as a single raw string. This is the field `entrypoint` and `cmd` encode into, exposed in its stored form. Two shapes are accepted. A bare shell string is treated as CMD and split into arguments, which is what the console's "Container start command" field writes. A JSON object of the form `{"entrypoint":[...],"cmd":[...]}` sets either or both explicitly. Responses always return both representations: `args` exactly as stored, plus the deconstructed `entrypoint` and `cmd`. Supplying `args` together with `entrypoint` or `cmd` is allowed only when they describe the same command, so a read-modify-write client can send back everything it received. Send `""` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
                      - `cmd` (array): Container CMD in exec form. When the image defines an ENTRYPOINT, this is the argument list passed to it. Encoded into the `args` field; supplying both is allowed only when they describe the same command. Send `[]` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
                        - `items` (string)
                      - `entrypoint` (array): Container ENTRYPOINT in exec form, overriding the image's own. Encoded into `args` field; supplying both is allowed only when they describe the same command. Send `[]` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.
                        - `items` (string)
                      - `disk` (integer; minimum: `1`): Container disk in GB (ephemeral, wiped on restart)
                      - `env` (object): Environment variables as key-value pairs
                        - `additional properties` (string)
                      - `image` (string): Docker image reference
                      - `ports` (array): Exposed ports, formatted as port/protocol
                        - `items` (string)
                    - `variant 2` (object)
                      - `registry` (nullable): Container registry credential ID for a private image: one of your credentials from `/v2/registries`. Leave it unset for a private Amazon ECR image. Runpod pulls those with an ECR delegation (`/v2/registries/delegations`) matched to the image's account, region and repository at pull time, so there is no delegation ID to pass here (a delegation ID is not a credential ID). A credential set here is used instead of any delegation.
                - `variant 2` (object)
                  - `id` (required; string)
                  - `name` (required; string)
                  - `mounts` (required; object): Storage mounts attached to a template. Templates support only a single persistent mount today; any `network` property is rejected with 422 by the schema validator. PATCH semantics: omitting `mounts` or sending `{}` leaves the existing mount unchanged.
                    - `persistent` (object): Host-local persistent storage. Pinned to the pod's host machine — data does not survive a host failure. Disallowed on CPU pods. Mutually exclusive with NetworkMount. Deprecated: prefer NetworkMount for any data you cannot recreate.
                      - `size` (required; integer; minimum: `10`): Host-local persistent storage in GB. Minimum 10 GB.
                      - `path` (required; string): Mount path inside the container. May be changed via PATCH.
                  - `serverless` (required; boolean): Whether this template is for serverless workers (true) or pods (false)
                  - `public` (required; boolean): Whether this template is visible to other Runpod users
                  - `category` (required; string; enum: `CPU`, `NVIDIA`, `AMD`): Controls how the template is grouped and filtered in the Runpod console. It does not affect hardware selection, scheduling, or billing. - `CPU` — CPU-only workloads - `NVIDIA` — NVIDIA GPU workloads - `AMD` — AMD GPU workloads
                  - `startSsh` (required; boolean): Whether containers created from this template get SSH access provisioned at startup (`PUBLIC_KEY` env injection).
                  - `startJupyter` (required; boolean): Whether containers created from this template start JupyterLab at startup (`JUPYTER_PASSWORD` env injection).
                  - `allowedCudaVersions` (required; array): Acceptable CUDA versions for containers created from this template, as `major.minor`. Empty means any version. Expanded into GPU pod and serverless endpoint creates; CPU pods ignore it.
                    - `items` (string)
            - `variant 2` (object): The Hub fields of a catalog template. A `VERSIONED` item is one tag of a versioned line: `id`, `name`, `image` and the container fields are the tag's, as `GET /v2/templates/{id}` returns them, and `versionedTemplateId` names the line.
              - `type` (required; string; enum: `SINGLE`, `VERSIONED`): `SINGLE` is a standalone template. `VERSIONED` is a tag of a versioned template line; the list shows each line's current tags.
              - `versionedTemplateId` (required; nullable): The versioned line this tag belongs to. Null for `SINGLE`.
              - `currentVersion` (required; nullable): The line's current version. Null for `SINGLE`, and for a tag whose line has no current version.
              - `official` (required; boolean): Whether Runpod publishes the template.
              - `verified` (required; boolean): Whether Runpod has verified this community template.
              - `products` (required; array)
                - `items` (string; enum: `POD`, `SERVERLESS`): Where a catalog item deploys.
              - `health` (required; object): How reliably a catalog item deploys.
                - `tier` (required; string; enum: `VERIFIED`, `UNVERIFIED`, `UNSTABLE`): `UNVERIFIED` while `reliability` is null. Otherwise `UNSTABLE` below Runpod's cutoff for the object's kind and `VERIFIED` at or above it. Set your own bar with `minReliability`.
                - `reliability` (required; format: double; nullable; minimum: `0`; maximum: `1`): Share of recent deploys that reached a healthy state; 0.9 means 90%. Null until there is enough deploy history to score.
                - `computedAt` (required; format: date-time; nullable): When `reliability` was last computed. Null when never scored.
              - `gpuCompatibility` (required; object): The GPUs and CUDA versions a catalog item declares. Empty lists mean it declares none.
                - `recommendedGpuTypeIds` (required; array): GPU type IDs, as in `GET /v2/catalog/gpus`.
                  - `items` (string)
                - `incompatibleGpuTypeIds` (required; array): GPU type IDs, as in `GET /v2/catalog/gpus`.
                  - `items` (string)
                - `minVramInGb` (required; nullable): Null when it declares none. Repos never declare one.
                - `allowedCudaVersions` (required; array)
                  - `items` (string)
                - `minCudaVersion` (required; nullable): The lowest CUDA version it runs on, applied when `allowedCudaVersions` is empty. Null when it declares none. Templates never declare one.
              - `stats` (required; object): Unique users who deployed the template, refreshed periodically. For a `VERSIONED` item, the sum over every tag in its line.
                - `deployers` (required; integer): All time.
                - `deployersLast30Days` (required; integer)
              - `createdAt` (required; string; format: date-time)
              - `updatedAt` (required; string; format: date-time): When the template's content was last edited.
        - `variant 2` (object)
          - `versions` (required; array): A versioned line's versions, newest first, deprecated ones included. Empty for `SINGLE`.
            - `items` (object)
              - `id` (required; string)
              - `version` (required; string)
              - `name` (required; string)
              - `changelog` (required; string): Empty when there is none.
              - `channel` (required): Null once a newer version takes the channel.
                - oneOf:
                  - `variant 1` (string; enum: `CURRENT`, `BETA`, `ALPHA`): The release channel a version holds.
                  - `variant 2` (null)
              - `deprecatedAt` (required; format: date-time; nullable)
              - `createdAt` (required; string; format: date-time)
              - `tags` (required; array)
                - `items` (object): One deployable image of a version.
                  - `templateId` (required; string): Deploy with this; it resolves at `GET /v2/templates/{id}`.
                  - `name` (required; string)
                  - `image` (required; string)
                  - `channel` (required)
                    - oneOf:
                      - `variant 1` (string; enum: `CURRENT`, `BETA`, `ALPHA`, `DEPRECATED`): The channel a tag holds. `DEPRECATED` once superseded.
                      - `variant 2` (null)
    - Example `versioned`: `{"id":"opvzatg7kb","name":"ROCm","image":"runpod/rocm:1.6.0-rocm644-ubuntu2404-py312-pytorch271","args":"","disk":50,"mounts":{},"ports":["8888/http","22/tcp"],"env":{},"registry":null,"serverless":false,"public":true,"category":"AMD","startSsh":true,"startJupyter":true,"allowedCudaVersions":[],"type":"VERSIONED","versionedTemplateId":"cmv9r2rer000vbcnlha8hwf9c","currentVersion":"2.7.1","official":true,"verified":false,"products":["POD"],"health":{"tier":"VERIFIED","reliability":0.99,"computedAt":"2026-11-04T06:00:00Z"},"gpuCompatibility":{"recommendedGpuTypeIds":[],"incompatibleGpuTypeIds":[],"minVramInGb":null,"allowedCudaVersions":[],"minCudaVersion":null},"stats":{"deployers":1840,"deployersLast30Days":211},"createdAt":"2026-10-15T16:25:38Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-30T18:19:02Z","versions":[{"id":"cmv9r2to100diufgzw2zvmr30","version":"2.7.1","name":"ROCm","changelog":"Template 1.6.0: ROCm 6.4.4 and PyTorch 2.7.1.","channel":"CURRENT","deprecatedAt":null,"createdAt":"2026-10-15T16:25:39Z","tags":[{"templateId":"opvzatg7kb","name":"ROCm 6.4.4 · Ubuntu 24.04 · 1.6.0-2.7.1","image":"runpod/rocm:1.6.0-rocm644-ubuntu2404-py312-pytorch271","channel":"CURRENT"}]}]}`

# Document: List Skills

Source path: api-reference-v2/catalog/list-skills.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-skills.mdx
Canonical documentation: https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-skills
Description: Search Runpod skills: step-by-step guides an agent follows to set up a workload on Runpod, such as ComfyUI on a pod.

# List Skills

Search Runpod skills: step-by-step guides an agent follows to set up a workload on Runpod, such as ComfyUI on a pod.

`GET /v2/catalog/skills`

**List skills**

Returns skills: step-by-step guides, published by Runpod, that an
agent follows to set up a workload. Each skill has a README and one
or more variants; open one with `GET /v2/catalog/skills/{id}`.

Without `search`, skills are ordered most recently updated first.
`minReliability`, `product` and `category` don't apply to skills and
are rejected with 422, as is any other undeclared parameter.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `search` (query; string; minimum length: `1`; maximum length: `200`): Search text, matched case-insensitively. Every word must match. A skill matches on its name, description and tags; a repo also on its GitHub owner and name; a template on its name and image, and a versioned template's tag also on its line's name and description. Enables `orderBy=RELEVANCE`, which becomes the default order.
  - Example: `comfyui`
- `tags` (query; array): Only return items carrying every one of these tags, matched exactly and case-insensitively. Comma-separated.
  - Example: `["comfyui","image"]`
- `mcpSupport` (query; array): Only return skills with one of these MCP support levels. Comma-separated. Skills that don't state one are excluded when this is set.
  - Example: `["FULL","PARTIAL"]`
- `orderBy` (query; string; enum: `RELEVANCE`, `UPDATED`, `NAME`): Defaults to `RELEVANCE` when `search` is set and `UPDATED` otherwise. `RELEVANCE` without `search` is rejected with 400.
  - Example: `UPDATED`
- `orderDirection` (query; string; enum: `ASC`, `DESC`): Sort direction. Defaults to `ASC` for `orderBy=NAME` and `DESC` otherwise.
  - Example: `DESC`
- `cursor` (query; string; minimum length: `1`): Opaque resume cursor — pass the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` through verbatim; omit for the first page. A cursor is only valid for the operation and parameters that issued it; a malformed or foreign cursor is rejected with 422.
  - Example: `Y3JlYXRlZEF0PTE3NDg3ODA0MDA`
- `limit` (query; integer; minimum: `1`; maximum: `1000`): Page size, 1–1000. Defaults to 1000 when omitted.
  - Example: `50`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `skills` (required; array)
        - `items` (object): A skill: a step-by-step guide, published by Runpod, that an agent follows to set up a workload. Read its README at `GET /v2/catalog/skills/{id}/readme`.
          - `id` (required; string): Stable skill identifier.
          - `name` (required; string)
          - `description` (required; string)
          - `tags` (required; array): Lowercase kebab-case labels.
            - `items` (string)
          - `mcpSupport` (required): Null when the skill doesn't say.
            - anyOf:

# Document: List Hub Repos

Source path: api-reference-v2/catalog/list-hub-repos.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-hub-repos.mdx
Canonical documentation: https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-hub-repos
Description: Search Runpod Hub repos: GitHub repositories Runpod builds into deployable images, with reliability scores and deploy counts.

# List Hub Repos

Search Runpod Hub repos: GitHub repositories Runpod builds into deployable images, with reliability scores and deploy counts.

`GET /v2/catalog/repos`

**List Hub repos**

Returns Hub repos: GitHub repositories Runpod builds into images you
can deploy. Open one with `GET /v2/catalog/repos/{id}` for its listed
release and deploy defaults.

Without `search`, repos are ordered most deployed first.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `search` (query; string; minimum length: `1`; maximum length: `200`): Search text, matched case-insensitively. Every word must match. A skill matches on its name, description and tags; a repo also on its GitHub owner and name; a template on its name and image, and a versioned template's tag also on its line's name and description. Enables `orderBy=RELEVANCE`, which becomes the default order.
  - Example: `comfyui`
- `product` (query; array): Only return items that deploy to one of these products. Comma-separated.
  - Example: `["SERVERLESS"]`
- `minReliability` (query; number; format: double; minimum: `0`; maximum: `1`): Only return items whose `health.reliability` is at least this value. Unscored items are excluded when this is set.
  - Example: `0.9`
- `category` (query; string; minimum length: `1`; maximum length: `100`): Only return items in this category, matched exactly and case-insensitively.
  - Example: `image`
- `tags` (query; array): Only return items carrying every one of these tags, matched exactly and case-insensitively. Comma-separated.
  - Example: `["comfyui","image"]`
- `source` (query; string; enum: `official`, `community`): `official` returns repos Runpod publishes (see `official` on the repo). `community` returns the rest. Omit for all.
  - Example: `official`
- `owner` (query; string; minimum length: `1`; maximum length: `100`): Only return repos from this GitHub owner, matched exactly and case-insensitively.
  - Example: `runpod-workers`
- `orderBy` (query; string; enum: `RELEVANCE`, `POPULAR`, `UPDATED`, `HEALTH`, `NAME`): Defaults to `RELEVANCE` when `search` is set and `POPULAR` otherwise. `RELEVANCE` without `search` is rejected with 400.
  - Example: `POPULAR`
- `orderDirection` (query; string; enum: `ASC`, `DESC`): Sort direction. Defaults to `ASC` for `orderBy=NAME` and `DESC` otherwise.
  - Example: `DESC`
- `cursor` (query; string; minimum length: `1`): Opaque resume cursor — pass the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` through verbatim; omit for the first page. A cursor is only valid for the operation and parameters that issued it; a malformed or foreign cursor is rejected with 422.
  - Example: `Y3JlYXRlZEF0PTE3NDg3ODA0MDA`
- `limit` (query; integer; minimum: `1`; maximum: `1000`): Page size, 1–1000. Defaults to 1000 when omitted.
  - Example: `50`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `repos` (required; array)
        - `items` (object): A Hub repo: a GitHub repository Runpod builds into a deployable image. Read its README at `GET /v2/catalog/repos/{id}/readme`.
          - `id` (required; string)
          - `name` (required; string)
          - `description` (required; string): Empty when the repo has none.

            - `items` (string; enum: `POD`, `SERVERLESS`): Where a catalog item deploys.

            - `items` (string)

# Get A Hub Repo

Retrieve a Runpod Hub repo with its listed release and the defaults it deploys with.

`GET /v2/catalog/repos/{id}`

**Get a Hub repo**

Returns one repo with its listed release, including the GPUs, disk
and environment variables the release deploys with. Read the README
at `GET /v2/catalog/repos/{id}/readme`.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string): Repo ID, as returned by `GET /v2/catalog/repos`.
  - Example: `cm862p99s000008ilegk86af6`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema: A repo with its license and listed release.
      - allOf:
        - `variant 1` (object): A Hub repo: a GitHub repository Runpod builds into a deployable image. Read its README at `GET /v2/catalog/repos/{id}/readme`.

          - `name` (required; string)
          - `description` (required; string): Empty when the repo has none.
          - `products` (required; array)
            - `items` (string; enum: `POD`, `SERVERLESS`): Where a catalog item deploys.
          - `category` (required; nullable)
          - `tags` (required; array)
            - `items` (string)
          - `official` (required; boolean): Whether Runpod publishes it: true for repos owned by the `runpod-workers` GitHub organization.

            - `reliability` (required; format: double; nullable; minimum: `0`; maximum: `1`): Share of recent deploys that reached a healthy state; 0.9 means 90%. Null until there is enough deploy history to score.
            - `computedAt` (required; format: date-time; nullable): When `reliability` was last computed. Null when never scored.
          - `stats` (required; object)
            - `deploys` (required; integer)

            - `views` (required; integer): Hub page views.

        - `variant 2` (object)
          - `license` (required; nullable)
          - `latestRelease` (required)
            - anyOf:
              - `variant 1`: The listed release, with its notes and deploy defaults.
                - allOf:
                  - `variant 1` (object): The release the Hub lists for a repo.
                    - `id` (required; string): Hub release ID.
                    - `tag` (required; string): Git tag.
                    - `releasedAt` (required; string; format: date-time)
                    - `image` (required; nullable): The built image. Null while the build is still running.
                    - `deployable` (required; boolean): Whether the release has a built image to deploy.
                  - `variant 2` (object)
                    - `name` (required; string)
                    - `notes` (required; string): The release notes. Empty when there are none.
                    - `deploy` (required; object): How the release deploys by default, from its `hub.json`.
                      - `computeType` (required; string; enum: `GPU`, `CPU`)
                      - `endpointType` (required; string; enum: `QUEUE`, `LOAD_BALANCER`): Request-routing semantics for a modern serverless endpoint. - `QUEUE` — submit asynchronous or synchronous jobs through the managed queue. - `LOAD_BALANCER` — send requests directly to worker-defined HTTP paths. Configure via `env`: `PORT` (server port, default 80), `PORT_HEALTH` (health-check port, default 80), and `HEALTH_CHECK_PATH` (path the load balancer polls for worker health, default `/ping`).
                      - `cpu` (required): The CPU flavor and vCPU count when `computeType` is `CPU`. A release that names no flavor gets `cpu3g`, and one that names no vCPU count gets 4. Null for GPU.
                        - anyOf:
                          - `variant 1` (object)
                            - `id` (required; string; minimum length: `1`): CPU flavor identifier, as returned by GET /v2/catalog/cpus.
                            - `vcpuCount` (required; integer; minimum: `2`): Number of vCPUs. Must be valid for the selected CPU flavor and must be a power of two.
                          - `variant 2` (null)

                        - `items` (string)
                      - `gpuCount` (required; integer)
                      - `containerDiskInGb` (required; nullable): Null when the release doesn't set one.
                      - `gpuCompatibility` (required; object): The GPUs and CUDA versions a catalog item declares. Empty lists mean it declares none.
                        - `recommendedGpuTypeIds` (required; array): GPU type IDs, as in `GET /v2/catalog/gpus`.
                          - `items` (string)
                        - `incompatibleGpuTypeIds` (required; array): GPU type IDs, as in `GET /v2/catalog/gpus`.
                          - `items` (string)
                        - `minVramInGb` (required; nullable): Null when it declares none. Repos never declare one.
                        - `allowedCudaVersions` (required; array)
                          - `items` (string)
                        - `minCudaVersion` (required; nullable): The lowest CUDA version it runs on, applied when `allowedCudaVersions` is empty. Null when it declares none. Templates never declare one.
                      - `volume` (required): The volume the release asks for. Null when it asks for none.
                        - anyOf:
                          - `variant 1` (object): A volume a release asks to have attached at deploy.
                            - `required` (required; boolean): Whether the deploy needs the volume, rather than only offering one.
                            - `types` (required; array): The volume types it accepts. Never empty.
                              - `items` (string; enum: `GLOBAL`, `NETWORK`): A kind of volume a deploy can attach.
                          - `variant 2` (null)
                      - `env` (required; array)
                        - `items` (object): An environment variable the repo reads, with its default.
                          - `key` (required; string)
                          - `default` (required; nullable): The default value as a string. Null when there is none.
                          - `description` (required; nullable)
                          - `required` (required; boolean): Whether the repo needs a value for this variable.
              - `variant 2` (null)
    - Example `repo`: `{"id":"cm862p99s000008ilegk86af6","name":"ComfyUI","description":"ComfyUI as a serverless API.","products":["SERVERLESS"],"category":"image","tags":["comfyui"],"official":true,"repository":{"owner":"runpod-workers","name":"worker-comfyui","url":"https://github.com/runpod-workers/worker-comfyui","ownerAvatarUrl":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/123456?v=4"},"health":{"tier":"VERIFIED","reliability":0.97,"computedAt":"2026-11-04T06:00:00Z"},"stats":{"deploys":41210,"stars":812,"views":190455},"license":"MIT","latestRelease":{"id":"cm8a1b2c3000108l4d5e6f7g8","tag":"v5.4.1","releasedAt":"2026-10-28T00:00:00Z","image":"runpod/worker-comfyui:5.4.1-base","deployable":true,"name":"v5.4.1","notes":"Adds Flux.2 support.","deploy":{"computeType":"GPU","endpointType":"QUEUE","cpu":null,"gpuTypeIds":["NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090","NVIDIA L4"],"gpuCount":1,"containerDiskInGb":20,"gpuCompatibility":{"recommendedGpuTypeIds":["NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090","NVIDIA L4"],"incompatibleGpuTypeIds":[],"minVramInGb":null,"allowedCudaVersions":["12.8","12.9"],"minCudaVersion":null},"volume":null,"env":[{"key":"COMFY_LOG_LEVEL","default":"DEBUG","description":"Log level for ComfyUI.","required":false}]}},"createdAt":"2025-03-01T00:00:00Z","updatedAt":"2026-10-28T00:00:00Z"}`

# List Cost Centers

**List cost centers**

`hasNextPage` is false.

  - Example: `team`
- `cursor` (query; string; minimum length: `1`): Opaque resume cursor — pass the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` through verbatim; omit for the first page. A cursor is only valid for the operation and parameters that issued it; a malformed or foreign cursor is rejected with 422.
  - Example: `Y3JlYXRlZEF0PTE3NDg3ODA0MDA`
- `limit` (query; integer; minimum: `1`; maximum: `1000`): Page size, 1–1000. Defaults to 1000 when omitted.
  - Example: `50`

# Create A Cost Center

Create a Runpod cost center and optionally attribute pods, clusters, serverless endpoints, and network volumes to it.

`POST /v2/cost-centers`

**Create a cost center**

Creates a cost center — a named label that groups resource spend so it can be broken out in billing. Pass `resources` to attribute resources at creation time; attaching is all-or-nothing, and a resource that already belongs to another cost center is rejected rather than moved.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Request body** (required)

- Media type: `application/json`
  - Schema (object)
    - `value` (required; string; minimum length: `1`; maximum length: `50`; pattern: `^\s*\S`): Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed.
    - `resources` (array; maximum items: `100`): Resources to attribute to the new cost center.
      - `items` (object)
        - `id` (required; string; minimum length: `1`)
        - `type` (required; string; enum: `POD`, `CLUSTER`, `SERVERLESS_ENDPOINT`, `NETWORK_VOLUME`): Kind of resource a cost center or tag can be attached to.
  - Example `bare`: `{"value":"team-ml"}`
  - Example `withResources`: `{"value":"team-ml","resources":[{"id":"p9k2m4n6q8","type":"POD"},{"id":"nv_7h3x1q","type":"NETWORK_VOLUME"}]}`

**Responses**

- `201`: Created
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `id` (required; string)
      - `value` (required; string): Cost center name exactly as stored, so it matches billing breakdowns.
    - Example `costCenter`: `{"id":"clz1x9k4a0000qw3h8s7d2f1g","value":"team-ml"}`
- `400`: The request could not be processed because it is malformed or conflicts with request rules.
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `badRequest`: `{"title":"Bad Request","status":400,"detail":"request could not be processed"}`
- `401`: Authentication failed because the bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or invalid.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `missingBearerToken`: `{"title":"Unauthorized","status":401,"detail":"missing bearer token"}`

# List A Cost Centers Resources

List the Runpod pods, clusters, serverless endpoints, and network volumes attributed to a cost center.

`GET /v2/cost-centers/{id}/resources`

**List a cost center's resources**

Returns the resources attributed to one cost center, cursor-paginated;
an omitted `limit` defaults to 1000. Each entry is the `{type}/{id}`
pair `DELETE /v2/cost-centers/{id}/{resourceType}/{resourceId}` takes.
A cost center with nothing attributed returns an empty list; one that
does not exist or is not the caller's returns 404.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string; minimum length: `1`): Cost center identifier.
- `cursor` (query; string; minimum length: `1`): Opaque resume cursor — pass the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` through verbatim; omit for the first page. A cursor is only valid for the operation and parameters that issued it; a malformed or foreign cursor is rejected with 422.
  - Example: `Y3JlYXRlZEF0PTE3NDg3ODA0MDA`
- `limit` (query; integer; minimum: `1`; maximum: `1000`): Page size, 1–1000. Defaults to 1000 when omitted.
  - Example: `50`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `resources` (required; array)
        - `items` (object)
          - `id` (required; string; minimum length: `1`)
          - `type` (required; string; enum: `POD`, `CLUSTER`, `SERVERLESS_ENDPOINT`, `NETWORK_VOLUME`): Kind of resource a cost center or tag can be attached to.
      - `pagination` (required; object): Cursor-pagination metadata, uniform across list endpoints. Every response carries it: follow `nextCursor` while `hasNextPage` is true to walk the full result set.
        - `nextCursor` (required; nullable): Pass as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page. Null on the last page.
        - `hasNextPage` (required; boolean): Whether more items exist after this page.
    - Example `resources`: `{"resources":[{"id":"p9k2m4n6q8","type":"POD"},{"id":"nv_7h3x1q","type":"NETWORK_VOLUME"}],"pagination":{"nextCursor":null,"hasNextPage":false}}`
- `401`: Authentication failed because the bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or invalid.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `missingBearerToken`: `{"title":"Unauthorized","status":401,"detail":"missing bearer token"}`
- `403`: The bearer token is valid, but it does not grant access to the requested resource or action.

      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `insufficientAccess`: `{"title":"Forbidden","status":403,"detail":"access denied"}`
- `404`: The requested resource was not found or is not accessible to the caller.
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.

# List Tags

List the Runpod tags available to the authenticated user.

`GET /v2/tags`

**List tags**

Returns the caller's tags, newest first, cursor-paginated. Tags under
the reserved `runpod:` prefix, such as cost centers, are never listed.
Follow `pagination.nextCursor` until `hasNextPage` is false.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `cursor` (query; string; minimum length: `1`): Opaque resume cursor — pass the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` through verbatim; omit for the first page. A cursor is only valid for the operation and parameters that issued it; a malformed or foreign cursor is rejected with 422.
  - Example: `Y3JlYXRlZEF0PTE3NDg3ODA0MDA`
- `limit` (query; integer; minimum: `1`; maximum: `1000`): Page size, 1–1000. Defaults to 1000 when omitted.
  - Example: `50`

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.

          - `value` (required; string): Returned exactly as stored. May be empty.
          - `createdAt` (required; string; format: date-time)
          - `updatedAt` (required; string; format: date-time)

        - `hasNextPage` (required; boolean): Whether more items exist after this page.
    - Example `tags`: `{"tags":[{"id":"clz1x9k4a0000qw3h8s7d2f1g","key":"env","value":"dev","createdAt":"2026-11-04T09:00:00Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-04T09:00:00Z"}],"pagination":{"nextCursor":null,"hasNextPage":false}}`

# Create A Tag

Create a Runpod tag and optionally attach it to pods, clusters, serverless endpoints, and network volumes.

`POST /v2/tags`

**Create a tag**

Creates a tag. Pass `resources` to attach it at creation time; the tag is created and attached in one step, so if any resource cannot be attached, no tag is created.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Request body** (required)

- Media type: `application/json`
  - Schema (object)
    - `key` (required; string; minimum length: `1`; maximum length: `191`; pattern: `[^\t-\r  - ]`): Tag key, 1–191 characters as sent, with at least one that is not whitespace. Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored. Keys under the reserved `runpod:` prefix, in any letter case, are rejected.
    - `value` (required; string; maximum length: `191`): Tag value, at most 191 characters. May be empty. Stored exactly as sent, whitespace included.
    - `resources` (array; maximum items: `100`): Existing resources to attach the new tag to.
      - `items` (object)
        - `id` (required; string; minimum length: `1`)
        - `type` (required; string; enum: `POD`, `CLUSTER`, `SERVERLESS_ENDPOINT`, `NETWORK_VOLUME`): Kind of resource a cost center or tag can be attached to.
  - Example `bare`: `{"key":"env","value":"dev"}`
  - Example `withResources`: `{"key":"env","value":"dev","resources":[{"id":"p9k2m4n6q8","type":"POD"},{"id":"nv_7h3x1q","type":"NETWORK_VOLUME"}]}`

**Responses**

- `201`: Created
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `id` (required; string): Shared by every resource the tag is attached to.
      - `key` (required; string): Returned exactly as stored.
      - `value` (required; string): Returned exactly as stored. May be empty.
      - `createdAt` (required; string; format: date-time)
      - `updatedAt` (required; string; format: date-time)
    - Example `tag`: `{"id":"clz1x9k4a0000qw3h8s7d2f1g","key":"env","value":"dev","createdAt":"2026-11-04T09:00:00Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-04T09:00:00Z"}`
- `400`: The request could not be processed because it is malformed or conflicts with request rules.
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `badRequest`: `{"title":"Bad Request","status":400,"detail":"request could not be processed"}`
- `401`: Authentication failed because the bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or invalid.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)

# Delete A Tag

Delete a Runpod tag and remove it from every resource it is attached to.

`DELETE /v2/tags/{id}`

**Delete a tag**

Deletes a tag and removes it from every resource it is attached to. The resources themselves are unchanged, and nothing needs to be detached first.       - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation

        - `items` (string)
    - Example `badRequest`: `{"title":"Bad Request","status":400,"detail":"request could not be processed"}`

# Update A Tag

Change the key or value of a Runpod tag. Resources it is attached to keep it.

`PATCH /v2/tags/{id}`

**Update a tag**

Changes a tag's key, value, or both. The tag keeps its ID and stays attached to the same resources. Returns 404 when the tag does not exist or is not the caller's.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string; minimum length: `1`): Tag identifier.

**Request body** (required)

- Media type: `application/json`
  - Schema (object): The fields to change; omitted fields are unchanged. Resources the tag is attached to stay attached.
    - `key` (string; minimum length: `1`; maximum length: `191`; pattern: `[^\t-\r  - ]`): Tag key, 1–191 characters as sent, with at least one that is not whitespace. Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored. Keys under the reserved `runpod:` prefix, in any letter case, are rejected.
    - `value` (string; maximum length: `191`): Tag value, at most 191 characters. May be empty. Stored exactly as sent, whitespace included.
  - Example `value`: `{"value":"prod"}`
  - Example `keyAndValue`: `{"key":"environment","value":"prod"}`

  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.

  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `id` (required; string): Shared by every resource the tag is attached to.
      - `key` (required; string): Returned exactly as stored.
      - `value` (required; string): Returned exactly as stored. May be empty.
      - `createdAt` (required; string; format: date-time)
      - `updatedAt` (required; string; format: date-time)
    - Example `tag`: `{"id":"clz1x9k4a0000qw3h8s7d2f1g","key":"environment","value":"prod","createdAt":"2026-11-04T09:00:00Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-04T09:30:00Z"}`

    - Schema (object)

      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation
      - `errors` (array): Individual request-validation failures.
        - `items` (string)
    - Example `badRequest`: `{"title":"Bad Request","status":400,"detail":"request could not be processed"}`
- `401`: Authentication failed because the bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or invalid.
  - Media type: `application/problem+json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `title` (required; string): Short human-readable summary
      - `status` (required; integer): HTTP status code
      - `detail` (required; string): Human-readable explanation

# List A Tags Resources

List the Runpod pods, clusters, serverless endpoints, and network volumes a tag is attached to.

`GET /v2/tags/{id}/resources`

**List a tag's resources**

Returns the resources a tag is attached to, newest attachment first,
cursor-paginated. Each entry is the `{type}/{id}` pair
`/v2/tags/{id}/resources/{resourceType}/{resourceId}` takes. A tag
attached to nothing returns an empty list; one that does not exist, is
deleted, is not the caller's, or is reserved returns 404.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string; minimum length: `1`): Tag identifier.
- `cursor` (query; string; minimum length: `1`): Opaque resume cursor — pass the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` through verbatim; omit for the first page. A cursor is only valid for the operation and parameters that issued it; a malformed or foreign cursor is rejected with 422.
  - Example: `Y3JlYXRlZEF0PTE3NDg3ODA0MDA`
- `limit` (query; integer; minimum: `1`; maximum: `1000`): Page size, 1–1000. Defaults to 1000 when omitted.
  - Example: `50`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object)
      - `resources` (required; array)
        - `items` (object)
          - `id` (required; string; minimum length: `1`)
          - `type` (required; string; enum: `POD`, `CLUSTER`, `SERVERLESS_ENDPOINT`, `NETWORK_VOLUME`): Kind of resource a cost center or tag can be attached to.
      - `pagination` (required; object): Cursor-pagination metadata, uniform across list endpoints. Every response carries it: follow `nextCursor` while `hasNextPage` is true to walk the full result set.
        - `nextCursor` (required; nullable): Pass as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page. Null on the last page.
        - `hasNextPage` (required; boolean): Whether more items exist after this page.
    - Example `resources`: `{"resources":[{"id":"p9k2m4n6q8","type":"POD"},{"id":"nv_7h3x1q","type":"NETWORK_VOLUME"}],"pagination":{"nextCursor":null,"hasNextPage":false}}`
- `401`: Authentication failed because the bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or invalid.

# Remove A Tag From A Resource

Remove a Runpod tag from a pod, cluster, serverless endpoint, or network volume.

`DELETE /v2/tags/{id}/resources/{resourceType}/{resourceId}`

**Remove a tag from a resource**

Removes a tag from one resource. The tag, the resource and the tag's other attachments are untouched. Returns 404 when the tag does not exist, is not the caller's, or is reserved (a cost center); when the resource does not carry it, so repeating a DELETE that succeeded returns 404; or when the resource is not the caller's to change. The detail names that last resource as `{resourceType}/{resourceId}`.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `id` (path; required; string; minimum length: `1`): Tag identifier.
- `resourceType` (path; required; string; enum: `POD`, `CLUSTER`, `SERVERLESS_ENDPOINT`, `NETWORK_VOLUME`): Kind of resource.
- `resourceId` (path; required; string; minimum length: `1`): Resource identifier.

# List Audit Logs

List your Runpod audit trail to see who acted on each resource, with filters for actor, action, time range, and text, newest first.

`GET /v2/audit-logs`

**List audit logs**

Returns the account's audit trail, newest first, cursor-paginated; an omitted `limit` defaults to 200. Each entry records who acted (`actorId`, `email`), what they did (`action`), to which resource (`resourceType`, `resourceId`), and the details of the change (`value`). When the caller belongs to an organization the trail is the organization's, and `actorIds` narrows it to specific members; otherwise it is the trail of the account the request acts for. Filters combine with AND. Entries older than the account's audit log retention window are not returned, and an account whose plan does not include audit logs is answered 403. Follow `pagination.nextCursor` until `hasNextPage` is false.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `actorIds` (query; array): Only return entries performed by these users. Comma-separated user IDs. Available to organization accounts only; a personal or team account is answered 400.
  - Example: `["user_id_abc_123","user_id_def_456"]`
- `actions` (query; array): Only return entries whose `action` is one of these names, matched exactly as recorded. Comma-separated.
  - Example: `["create","delete"]`
- `startTime` (query; string; format: date-time): Earliest instant to include, inclusive (RFC 3339). The account's audit log retention window still applies: entries that have aged out are not returned even when this reaches further back.
  - Example: `2026-09-01T00:00:00Z`
- `endTime` (query; string; format: date-time): Latest instant to include, inclusive (RFC 3339). Must be after `startTime` when both are given; 400 otherwise.
  - Example: `2026-09-30T23:59:59Z`
- `search` (query; string; minimum length: `1`): Case-insensitive substring match against `email`, `resourceType`, `resourceId`, `action` and `value`; `actorId` is not searched. Surrounding whitespace is ignored.
  - Example: `abc123`
- `cursor` (query; string; minimum length: `1`): Opaque resume cursor — pass the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` through verbatim; omit for the first page. A cursor is only valid for the operation and parameters that issued it; a malformed or foreign cursor is rejected with 422.
  - Example: `Y3JlYXRlZEF0PTE3NDg3ODA0MDA`
- `limit` (query; integer; minimum: `1`; maximum: `200`): Page size, 1–200. Defaults to 200 when omitted.
  - Example: `50`

          - `email` (required; nullable): Email of the actor when the action was recorded. Null when unknown.
          - `resourceType` (required; string): Kind of resource the action applied to, as recorded at write time. Not an enum: values are free-form, mostly lower camel case, and new kinds appear without an API version change. Current writers record values such as `pod`, `apiKey`, `sharedApiKey`, `secret`, `costCenter`, `paymentMethod`, `billingAccount`, `registryCredential`, `organization` and `group`, and `unknown` when the writer recorded no kind.
          - `resourceId` (required; string): ID of the affected resource. Empty when the action was not about one resource; a bulk action lists every affected ID, comma-separated.
          - `action` (required; string): Name of the action, as recorded at write time. Not an enum: values are free-form, mostly lower case verbs, and new actions appear without an API version change. Current writers record values such as `create`, `update`, `delete`, `rename`, `lock`, `unlock`, `start`, `reset`, `add` and `setBillingMode`.
          - `value` (required; nullable): Details of the change as a JSON-encoded string. The structure varies by action; parse it as JSON for a structured view. A bulk action split across several entries adds an `auditChunk` object with `index` and `of`. Null when the action recorded no details.

      - `pagination` (required; object): Cursor-pagination metadata, uniform across list endpoints. Every response carries it: follow `nextCursor` while `hasNextPage` is true to walk the full result set.
        - `nextCursor` (required; nullable): Pass as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page. Null on the last page.
        - `hasNextPage` (required; boolean): Whether more items exist after this page.
    - Example `auditLogs`: `{"auditLogs":[{"actorId":"user_id_abc_123","email":"actor@example.com","resourceType":"pod","resourceId":"abc123","action":"delete","value":"{\"status\":\"TERMINATED\"}","timestamp":"2026-09-02T00:00:00Z"},{"actorId":"user_id_abc_123","email":"actor@example.com","resourceType":"pod","resourceId":"abc123","action":"rename","value":"{\"name\":\"training-run-7\"}","timestamp":"2026-09-01T18:30:00Z"},{"actorId":"user_id_def_456","email":"admin@example.com","resourceType":"secret","resourceId":"sec_789","action":"update","value":"{\"id\":\"sec_789\",\"name\":\"HF_TOKEN\",\"sharedWithOrganization\":true}","timestamp":"2026-09-01T09:15:00Z"}],"pagination":{"nextCursor":"eyJ0cyI6IjIwMjYtMDktMDFUMDk6MTU6MDBaIn0=","hasNextPage":true}}`

# Document: Get Aggregated Billing History

Source path: api-reference-v2/billing/get-aggregated-billing-history.mdx
Pinned source: https://github.com/runpod/docs/blob/c845f73c104cb4b69f4caa11f27180533ad8546f/api-reference-v2/billing/get-aggregated-billing-history.mdx
Canonical documentation: https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/billing/get-aggregated-billing-history
Description: Retrieve time-bucketed total Runpod spend across Pods, Serverless, storage, Public Endpoints, and Clusters for the authenticated account.

# Get Aggregated Billing History

Retrieve time-bucketed total Runpod spend across Pods, Serverless, storage, Public Endpoints, and Clusters for the authenticated account.

`GET /v2/billing`

**Get aggregated billing history**

Returns time-bucketed total spend across all billable Runpod resources for the authenticated user. Use startTime/endTime with bucketSize for an explicit range, or lastN with bucketSize for the most recent buckets. Each record reports one bucket's total plus pod, serverless, storage, public endpoint, and Instant Cluster cost components. The metadata block echoes the resolved query window, record count, and totals across all returned buckets.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `startTime` (query; string; format: date-time): Start of the billing period (RFC 3339). Defaults to 30 days ago. Snapped down to the start of its bucketSize bucket so the window aligns with the returned records; provide a boundary-aligned value (e.g. midnight for bucketSize=day) to avoid widening.
  - Example: `2026-05-01T00:00:00Z`
- `endTime` (query; string; format: date-time): End of the billing period (RFC 3339), exclusive. Defaults to now. Snapped up to the end of the bucketSize bucket it lands in (unless already on a boundary) so the window aligns with the returned records.
  - Example: `2026-06-01T00:00:00Z`
- `bucketSize` (query; string; enum: `hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`; default: `day`): Length of each billing time bucket. Defaults to day.
- `lastN` (query; integer; minimum: `1`): Return the last N buckets of bucketSize, ending with the current (in-progress) bucket — e.g. lastN=100 with bucketSize=day is "last 100 days". The resolved window is aligned to bucket boundaries: startTime is the start of the earliest bucket (e.g. midnight of the earliest day) and endTime is the end of the current bucket. Mutually exclusive with startTime/endTime; provide one or the other, not both.
  - Example: `30`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object): Aggregated billing records across all Runpod resources.
      - `records` (required; array)
        - `items`: A single time-bucketed record of total spend across all billable Runpod resources, with each cost component broken out. Returned by GET /v2/billing.
          - allOf:
            - `variant 1` (object): Half-open time range \[startTime, endTime) in RFC 3339. On a record it is the time bucket; on a query echo it is the resolved window.
              - `startTime` (required; string; format: date-time): Start of the range, inclusive (RFC 3339).
              - `endTime` (required; string; format: date-time): End of the range, exclusive (RFC 3339).
            - `variant 2` (object): Total spend across all billable Runpod resources with each cost component broken out, fully prefixed by resource. Backs the aggregate record's amounts and the metadata totals. Serverless amounts are inclusive of platform charges.
              - `totalAmount` (required; number; format: double): Total cost in USD for the bucket across all resources.
              - `podGpuAmount` (required; number; format: double): GPU pod compute cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `podCpuAmount` (required; number; format: double): CPU pod compute cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `podDiskAmount` (required; number; format: double): Pod disk cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `serverlessGpuAmount` (required; number; format: double): Serverless GPU compute cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `serverlessCpuAmount` (required; number; format: double): Serverless CPU compute cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `serverlessDiskAmount` (required; number; format: double): Serverless disk cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `serverlessFeeAmount` (required; number; format: double): Unused and always 0. Platform charges are included in the serverless compute amounts.
              - `storageStandardAmount` (required; number; format: double): Standard network volume storage cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `storageHighPerformanceAmount` (required; number; format: double): High-performance network volume storage cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `endpointAmount` (required; number; format: double): Runpod public endpoint cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `clusterGpuAmount` (required; number; format: double): Cluster GPU compute cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `clusterDiskAmount` (required; number; format: double): Cluster disk cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `clusterNetworkingAmount` (required; number; format: double): Cluster inter-node networking cost in USD for the bucket.
      - `metadata` (required; object)
        - `query` (required): Resolved query window and granularity (routes without a filter).
          - allOf:

# Get Pod Billing History

Retrieve time-bucketed billing details for one or all Runpod Pods, including GPU, CPU, disk, total costs, and query metadata.

`GET /v2/billing/pods`

**Get pod billing history**

Returns pod-only billing detail for the authenticated user, split into time buckets by startTime/endTime with bucketSize or by lastN recent buckets. Use podId to narrow the response to one GPU or CPU pod; without it, records are emitted per pod per bucket. Each record includes podId, GPU, CPU, disk, and total amounts, while metadata echoes the resolved query and totals across the pod records. Use listBilling when you need aggregate spend across every billable resource family.

**Authentication:** `bearerAuth`

**Parameters**

- `startTime` (query; string; format: date-time): Start of the billing period (RFC 3339). Defaults to 30 days ago. Snapped down to the start of its bucketSize bucket so the window aligns with the returned records; provide a boundary-aligned value (e.g. midnight for bucketSize=day) to avoid widening.
  - Example: `2026-05-01T00:00:00Z`
- `endTime` (query; string; format: date-time): End of the billing period (RFC 3339), exclusive. Defaults to now. Snapped up to the end of the bucketSize bucket it lands in (unless already on a boundary) so the window aligns with the returned records.
  - Example: `2026-06-01T00:00:00Z`
- `bucketSize` (query; string; enum: `hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`; default: `day`): Length of each billing time bucket. Defaults to day.
- `lastN` (query; integer; minimum: `1`): Return the last N buckets of bucketSize, ending with the current (in-progress) bucket — e.g. lastN=100 with bucketSize=day is "last 100 days". The resolved window is aligned to bucket boundaries: startTime is the start of the earliest bucket (e.g. midnight of the earliest day) and endTime is the end of the current bucket. Mutually exclusive with startTime/endTime; provide one or the other, not both.
  - Example: `30`
- `podId` (query; string): Filter to a specific pod (GPU or CPU).
  - Example: `pod_abc123`

**Responses**

- `200`: OK
  - Header `RateLimit` (string): Live quota state for the caller, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Header `RateLimit-Policy` (string): The quota policy behind `RateLimit`, per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft.
  - Media type: `application/json`
    - Schema (object): Billing records for pods.
      - `records` (required; array)
        - `items`: A single time-bucketed pod billing record, covering both GPU and CPU pods. Returned by GET /v2/billing/pods.

            - `variant 1` (object): Half-open time range \[startTime, endTime) in RFC 3339. On a record it is the time bucket; on a query echo it is the resolved window.
              - `startTime` (required; string; format: date-time): Start of the range, inclusive (RFC 3339).
              - `endTime` (required; string; format: date-time): End of the range, exclusive (RFC 3339).
            - `variant 2` (object): Pod cost components covering both GPU and CPU pods. Backs a record's amounts and the metadata totals.
              - `totalAmount` (required; number; format: double): Total pod cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `gpuAmount` (required; number; format: double): GPU pod compute cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `cpuAmount` (required; number; format: double): CPU pod compute cost in USD for the bucket.
              - `diskAmount` (required; number; format: double): Pod disk cost in USD for the bucket.
            - `variant 3` (object)
              - `podId` (required; string): The pod this record bills. When the podId filter is set every record carries that id; otherwise one record is emitted per pod per bucket.
      - `metadata` (required; object)
        - `query` (required)
          - allOf:
            - `variant 1`: Resolved query window and granularity (routes without a filter).
              - allOf:
                - `variant 1` (object): Half-open time range \[startTime, endTime) in RFC 3339. On a record it is the time bucket; on a query echo it is the resolved window.
                  - `startTime` (required; string; format: date-time): Start of the range, inclusive (RFC 3339).
                  - `endTime` (required; string; format: date-time): End of the range, exclusive (RFC 3339).

            - `variant 2` (object)

        - `recordCount` (required; integer): Number of records returned (buckets times distinct pods).
        - `uniquePodCount` (required; integer): Number of distinct pods the records span.
